Three coupled questions have to be answered together for the gesture to be defined: the rename rule, the placement rule, and whether an incomplete paste writes now or stages.
decisions.story: Marco built a small pricing block in Canvas: a couple of local bindings and a call that uses them. He wants the same block a second time, tweaked. He selects the three nodes and hits Ctrl+D to duplicate. In a text editor he would copy the lines and rename `subtotal` by hand; in Blueprint the duplicate just appears floating. He needs to know what Canvas puts in his `.jet` file: what the second `subtotal` is called, where the new lines go, and whether the duplicate that still has an unwired input is already in his source or waiting to be wired.
decisions.inWild:
Selection Marco duplicates (three nodes: two bindings + one call):

  fn quote(base: Money) -> Money {
      subtotal = base * qty            // <- selected
      tax = subtotal * rate            // <- selected
      log_line(subtotal)               // <- selected
      return subtotal + tax
  }

On Ctrl+D, `subtotal` and `tax` already exist in this scope — the clone cannot reuse those names. And the clone's `qty` / `rate` inputs point at bindings that were NOT in the selection, so the copy has two inputs with nothing wired to them yet. What Canvas writes for those two facts is undefined today.
decisions.detail: Recommend E (hybrid: D's split + C's naming intent without modals + B's control as an explicit modifier). Devil pass across all five: (C) prompt-on-collision interrupts the most frequent gesture with a modal per name — death by dialog; but the intent behind it (the user often wants a meaningful name, not `subtotal2`) is real. (A) eager-complete writes values the user never chose (`qty` silently 0) — rejected as a default; nothing in E writes a default-filled input. (B) always-stage is wrong as a default for self-contained clones but right as an on-demand mode: an expert arranging a large paste wants placement and wiring before any write. (D) is the correct core: source-text clipboard (one path — graph, cross-file, plain text editor), atomic first-free-suffix rename against the destination scope, immediate materialization when self-contained, staged fallback when inputs are unresolved. (E) = D plus two additions that supply the missing control without new ceremony: after a materializing paste, the renamed bindings appear as non-blocking rename chips — the suffixed name is highlighted in the graph and one click/F2 runs the ordinary rename-binding transaction (no modal, ignorable, disappears on next edit); and paste-as-staged is available as an explicit modifier (Ctrl+Shift+V and a context-menu entry) for deliberate stage-first workflows even when the selection is self-contained. Devil pass on E: chips could be visual noise on a 10-binding paste. Patch: chips coalesce into one "3 bindings renamed — review" pill above the pasted cluster when more than 3 renames happen; the pill expands to the list. Rename-chip renames are the shipped rename transaction, so scope-correctness and undo come for free (I8 — no second rename path).

options.name: Eager complete (suffix rename, fill defaults)
options.detail: Paste always writes source immediately. Colliding bindings get the first free numeric suffix (`subtotal` -> `subtotal2`). Clones land right after the selection's source span. Any input left unresolved by the copy is filled with a typed default so the source is always complete and type-checks — the user edits the default afterward.
options.code:
Ctrl+D result written immediately:

  fn quote(base: Money) -> Money {
      subtotal = base * qty
      tax = subtotal * rate
      log_line(subtotal)
      subtotal2 = base * 0        // qty unresolved -> default 0
      tax2 = subtotal2 * 0.0      // rate unresolved -> default 0.0
      log_line(subtotal2)
      return subtotal + tax
  }

Type-checks, but `0` / `0.0` are values Marco never chose.

options.name: Always stage (defer every paste)
options.detail: Every pasted/duplicated node lands as a staged node (#388): dashed unsaved ring, view-state only, nothing in source. The user positions and wires; the first wire connecting a clone to the graph spine materializes it (with rename resolved then). Nothing is written for a clone until it is wired.
options.code:
Ctrl+D result: three staged (dashed) nodes appear beside the originals.
`.jet` is UNCHANGED until the user wires them:

  fn quote(base: Money) -> Money {
      subtotal = base * qty
      tax = subtotal * rate
      log_line(subtotal)
      return subtotal + tax
  }

Even a fully self-contained duplicate stays dashed until the user makes a
connection it does not actually need.

options.name: Prompt on collision, append at block end
options.detail: Paste writes source but pauses to prompt for each colliding binding name (suggested `subtotal_copy`, editable). Clones append at the end of the current block. Complete materialization after the prompts are answered.
options.code:
Ctrl+D opens, per collision:

  Name for copied binding "subtotal":  [ subtotal_copy ]   Rename / Skip
  Name for copied binding "tax":       [ tax_copy ]        Rename / Skip

Then writes at block end:

  fn quote(base: Money) -> Money {
      subtotal = base * qty
      tax = subtotal * rate
      log_line(subtotal)
      return subtotal + tax
      subtotal_copy = base * qty
      tax_copy = subtotal_copy * rate
      log_line(subtotal_copy)
  }
(unreachable-after-return here is illustrative; real placement is end of the live block)

options.name: Source-text clipboard (one path), suffix rename, stage only when unresolved
options.detail: Copy serializes the selection to real Jet source text on the clipboard, so paste is one mechanism across graph, other files, and a plain text editor. A self-contained selection materializes immediately: first-free suffix rename applied atomically to defs and in-selection uses, inserted right after the selection's span. A selection whose inputs are unresolved falls back to a staged node (#388) instead of writing default-filled or dangling source — Canvas never writes source the user did not complete.
options.code:
Case 1 — self-contained duplicate (all inputs internal): materializes now.

  subtotal = base * qty
  tax = subtotal * rate
  log_line(subtotal)
  subtotal2 = base * qty         // qty resolves to the same in-scope binding
  tax2 = subtotal2 * rate        // renamed def + use, atomic
  log_line(subtotal2)

Clipboard also holds the same text — paste into main.jet or a text editor works.

Case 2 — a copied node's input was NOT in the selection: that clone stages
(dashed ring), writes nothing, and materializes with the rename resolved the
moment Marco wires its input. Always-valid source, no surprise defaults.

options.name: D plus rename chips and an explicit stage modifier (hybrid, recommended)
options.detail: Everything in option D unchanged: source-text clipboard as the one paste mechanism, atomic first-free-suffix rename, insertion after the selection's span, staged fallback for unresolved inputs. Added: (1) after a materializing paste, auto-renamed bindings show non-blocking rename chips — click or F2 runs the ordinary rename transaction, ignoring them costs nothing, >3 renames coalesce into one expandable pill; (2) Ctrl+Shift+V (and context menu "Paste as staged") stages any paste deliberately, even self-contained ones, for place-and-wire-first workflows. Beginner path is untouched: Ctrl+D just works and reads cleanly. Expert path gains naming intent and write timing without a single modal.
options.code:
Ctrl+D (self-contained) — writes immediately, like D:

  subtotal2 = base * qty     [subtotal2 ✎]   <- chip, click to rename
  tax2 = subtotal2 * rate    [tax2 ✎]
  log_line(subtotal2)

Click chip -> inline name edit -> ordinary rename transaction rewrites
def + uses; ignore the chips and they vanish on the next edit.

Ctrl+Shift+V — same clipboard, but lands as staged (dashed) nodes:
nothing written; position and wire first; first spine wire materializes
with the same suffix-rename rules.

Unresolved-input paste: staged automatically, exactly as in D.

comparisons.note: Ctrl+W/Ctrl+V clones nodes as new graph objects with auto-suffixed titles and no naming or placement rules, because clones are asset data, not source. Dangling input pins are simply unconnected — legal in a graph, meaningless in a source file. Jet has to answer the questions Blueprint gets to skip; option D keeps Blueprint's frictionless feel for self-contained clones while staging (not dangling) the incomplete ones.
comparisons.code:
Ctrl+W on a node -> "MyNode" clones as "MyNode" with pins unconnected;
no rename dialog, no file, no validity requirement.

comparisons.note: Right-click Duplicate drops a floating copy that runs nothing until you attach it under a hat block — this is exactly staged materialization (#388): the copy exists in the editor but is inert until connected. Option D uses that model precisely for the incomplete case, matching a mental model non-programmers already have.
comparisons.code:
Duplicate -> a detached stack floats; it does nothing until snapped under
a `when green flag clicked` (or other) hat.

comparisons.note: Copying lines and pasting them is a byte operation — the editor never renames your variables, so you fix collisions by hand. Option D's source-text clipboard is byte-compatible with this (the clipboard IS Jet text), but adds the graph-aware suffix rename the text editor can't do, so a graph paste is safe where a raw text paste would shadow `subtotal`.
comparisons.code:
Paste of `subtotal = base * qty` next to an existing `subtotal` ->
two bindings named `subtotal`; the text editor does not rename either.

decisions.title: Debugger backing: what drives breakpoints, watches, and exec pulse
decisions.gist: What actually powers the Canvas debugger — a real native debug session against the running program, a re-run of the tier-0 interpreter with instrumentation, or a hybrid — and, above all, whether the on-screen liveness is real or simulated.
decisions.explainer:
Glossary. Native debug session: `jet debug` driving the real compiled process through an lldb/DAP backend (tests/debug.rs) — real breakpoints, real variable reads, real stepping, mapped from generated Rust frames back to Jet source spans. DAP: Debug Adapter Protocol, the same wire format VS Code's debugger uses. Tier-0 interpreter: Jet's comptime interpreter that evaluates a program without producing a native binary (the JIT is a separate tier-1 dev accelerator). Exec pulse: the animated highlight flowing along exec wires showing which path is executing. Watch: a pinned expression whose value the debugger shows as you step. Per the ratified D-CANVAS-DEBUGSTATE1, breakpoints and watches are LOCAL editor state anchored to source spans and the source hash — Canvas never writes them into `.jet`.

The wall. Every debugger row in the matrix (session selector, step/next/continue/stop, breakpoints/watches, active-node/wire pulse, call stack) is projection-only or a UI shell with zero behavior tests — the debug rail buttons in html.rs do nothing yet. This is the single largest unbuilt surface and it is the one most able to lie: an animation can imply the program is running when it is not. The owner's hard rule for the whole epoch is that the UI must never fake liveness. This ballot picks the engine, and the engine determines what is real.
decisions.story: Dana sets a breakpoint on the `charge(card)` node in her payment function and clicks Run in Canvas. She expects the graph to stop there, show her the real `card` value the program actually has, let her step to the next node, and pulse the exec wire along the path that actually ran. She needs to trust that what glows is what happened — if the debugger showed her a plausible-but-simulated value or pulsed a path the real program did not take, she would ship a bug believing she had watched it not happen.
decisions.detail: Recommend D (debug the tier that is actually running; hybrid of A's truth and B's reach, with none of B's simulation). The gap options A-C share: they assume the program under debug is a compiled binary. Canvas's beginner loop runs under `jet dev` — tier-0 interpreter or tier-1 JIT — where there is no native process for lldb to attach to; under option A alone, the beginner's most common session shows "not running," and the debugger is an expert-only feature. But R12 and the ratified D-DEVMODE1 make the dev tier's behavior byte-identical to the compiled program, and when a program runs under jet dev, that tier IS the runtime — instrumenting the engine that is actually executing is real liveness, not simulation (the same reason Scratch's glow is honest: its interpreter is its runtime, and the same reason Blueprint's pulse is honest: its VM is its runtime). Devil pass across all four: (B) as a stand-alone overlay re-RUNS the program beside the real one — that remains simulation and stays rejected; the difference in D is attachment to the session the user's Run actually started, never a second execution. (C) mixes a real session with interpreter-animated motion — still the worst of both, rejected. (A) is correct for compiled runs and remains exactly D's native backend; it just leaves the dev loop dark. (D) one debugger UX, one seam, two honest backends: run was `jet run`/compiled target -> native lldb/DAP session (option A verbatim); run was `jet dev` -> the executing tier reports breakpoints/steps/values/path from inside itself (the JitBackend seam precedent — same protocol facts, different engine). The status chip always names the engine ("debugging: compiled process" / "debugging: dev tier"), values shown are always read from the engine executing them, and wires never pulse without a live session. Devil pass on D: two backends could drift (a breakpoint behaves differently across tiers). Patch: R12 parity already pins tier behavior with the differential batteries; the debug facts (stop span, value render, path taken) join those existing parity tests, so a drift is a test failure, not a UX surprise. Beginners get a debugger that works the first time they click Run in dev mode; experts get the same real lldb/DAP session option A promised — nothing on screen is ever simulated.

options.name: Native debug session (real process)
options.detail: Canvas drives the existing `jet debug` lldb/DAP backend against the real compiled program. Breakpoints, watches, variable reads, call stack, and stepping are real; the exec pulse highlights the path the process actually executed, advancing at real stops. Frames map from generated Rust back to Jet source spans via the existing source map. When nothing is running, wires do not pulse and the UI reports "not running."
options.code:
Dana clicks Run with a breakpoint on `charge`:

  [ debug session: checkout(card, cart) ]  paused at charge
  Watches:   total = 4299   (real value from the process)
             card.limit = 5000
  Call stack: checkout  <- main
  Exec pulse: price -> if(false) -> [charge]  (path actually taken, lit)

  Step Over -> advances to `return Ok(receipt)`; receipt = Receipt{...} real.
  No session running -> wires dark, header reads "not running".
Breakpoints stay local editor state (D-CANVAS-DEBUGSTATE1); `.jet` is untouched.

options.name: Interpreter overlay (re-run, instrumented)
options.detail: Canvas re-runs the program on the tier-0 interpreter with instrumentation and animates a deterministic, smooth exec pulse plus interpreter-computed watch values. No native process is involved. Visually the richest and most controllable, but the values and path are the interpreter's, which can differ from the compiled program.
options.code:
Dana clicks Run:

  [ interpreter overlay ]
  Watches:   total = 4299   (interpreter's evaluation)
  Exec pulse: smooth flowing highlight along price -> if -> charge

Risk made concrete: if `price(cart)` reads a clock, hits the network, or
depends on evaluation order, the interpreter's `total` and chosen path may
not match what the shipped binary does — the glow would show a run that
did not happen. Honest only if labeled "simulated preview," not "debug."

options.name: Hybrid (native state + interpreter pulse)
options.detail: A native session provides real variable/stack/step state; the exec-wire pulse animation is driven by the interpreter overlay for smoothness. State is real, motion is simulated.
options.code:
Dana clicks Run:

  Watches:   total = 4299            (real, from native session)
  Call stack: checkout <- main       (real)
  Exec pulse: smooth flow price->if->charge   (interpreter-animated)

The numbers are true but the flowing highlight is the interpreter's guess;
if the two disagree on the taken branch, the UI shows real values under a
pulse tracing a different path — a truthful-looking screen that lies in motion.

options.name: Debug the running tier: native session for compiled runs, in-tier session under jet dev (hybrid, recommended)
options.detail: One debugger UX behind one seam, backend chosen by what is actually executing. Compiled target: the existing jet debug lldb/DAP backend — option A verbatim, real process, real frames mapped by the existing source map. Under jet dev: the tier-0/tier-1 engine that IS running the program reports its own stops, values, and taken path — real liveness because it is the runtime, guaranteed behavior-identical by R12/D-DEVMODE1 and pinned by the existing parity batteries, which the debug facts join. The engine is always named on screen; no session, no pulse, ever. Breakpoints/watches stay local span-anchored state (D-CANVAS-DEBUGSTATE1) and drive both backends identically.
options.code:
Dana under `jet dev` (the beginner default), breakpoint on `charge`:

  [ debugging: dev tier — paused at charge ]
  Watches:    total = 4299        (read from the executing tier)
  Call stack: checkout <- main
  Exec pulse: price -> if(false) -> [charge]   (path the tier actually took)

Same function, compiled run (`jet run` / release binary):

  [ debugging: compiled process — paused at charge ]
  Watches:    total = 4299        (real process memory via lldb/DAP)

Same breakpoints, same UI, same protocol facts; the chip names the engine.
No live session -> wires dark, header "not running". Nothing simulated:
what glows is what the running engine did.

comparisons.note: Blueprint's exec pulse and watch values are real because the Blueprint VM IS the runtime — single-stepping the VM is single-stepping the program, so its glow never lies. The lesson is not "animate a pulse"; it is "debug the actual runtime." Jet's actual runtime is the compiled process, so the faithful equivalent of Blueprint's debugger is the native session (option A), not a separate interpreter that merely looks like Blueprint.
comparisons.code:
BP debugger: breakpoint on a node -> VM halts -> real pin values shown ->
exec wire glows the path the VM took (real, because VM == runtime).

comparisons.note: VS Code debugs the real process over DAP: it stops at real breakpoints, shows real variables, and steps real frames; it never animates a speculative execution path. decisions.title: REPL Core effect authorization
decisions.gist: Choose how existing Jet effects are authorized inside the REPL.
decisions.explainer: Jet already has one effect language: D-EFF4's roots, D-EFFTREE1 paths, lexical #Grant regions, and invocation policy through the existing --allow-fs/--allow-env/--allow-exec/--allow-net/--allow-io/--allow-time/--allow-rand flags. This ballot adds no REPL-specific grant names, grant commands, or persistent permission store. All options keep Core's current static bare-root tags; they do not globally retag Core with compiler-minted leaves. Dynamic capability data distinguishes resources and operations beneath a statically proven root. Thus an Env capability may permit reading HOME but not writing HOME; an Exec capability for one pinned Exec.Run target never permits Exec.Exit; an Io capture channel never permits terminal input. The canonical REPL filesystem root is fixed once: `jet repl --project DIR` uses the canonical project root, otherwise the process's starting cwd. The evaluator opens that root as a directory handle before accepting input. A symlink used to reach the starting location is resolved once when opening the root; later path components are descriptor-relative and no-follow. Because `core.os` has no current static effect root and this ballot does not retag Core, every `core.os` operation remains native-only E1802 in the REPL, including host facts and `set_current_dir`; therefore evaluated code cannot mutate cwd, and the fixed root handle never changes. --allow-fs is only the existing Fs invocation ceiling and never broadens reach beyond that fixed root. Every file operation uses verified handles; if the platform cannot enforce race-safe confinement it fails closed. Process execution pins executable identity before authorization, never re-resolves PATH, uses a verified cwd and minimal declared environment, bounds time, forwards interrupt, kills/reaps children, and separately authorizes redirects. Network authority pins scheme, hostname, port, and resolved addresses; redirects or new DNS results require fresh authority. Env.Read and Env.Write are dynamically separate exact-key resources under bare Env; session authorization for one key/direction never covers another. Ambient Time operations (wall clock, local zone, sleep, stopwatch/instant) require Time; a Clock created from an explicit seed/value is injected data and needs no ambient authority. Ambient/OS and secure randomness require Rand; an explicitly seeded Rng is injected data and needs none. `core.crypto.random` remains E1802 while it is native-only; if the interpreter gains it, it follows secure Rand policy. REPL-owned stdout/stderr capture is inherent evaluator plumbing: print/eprint and subprocess Capture write only to the REPL's captured output and require no runtime Io authority. Reading stdin, raw terminal access, inheriting/streaming a subprocess terminal, or redirecting to an external stream requires #Grant(Io) plus Io policy. A subprocess file redirect requires Fs for the verified file handle; Capture alone grants neither Io nor Fs. FFI, tasks, raw memory, display/UI backends, servers, and other native-only facilities remain E1802. Missing lexical authority remains E0712. E1802 remains only for unavailable interpreter features. This decision allocates E1803 to REPL runtime-policy denial, missing invocation policy, or confinement failure after lexical proof. E1803 must be registered in diagnostics with what/why/fix and pinned by a UI snapshot before implementation uses it.
decisions.story: Maya is learning Jet in a cloned service. She wraps a config read in the same #Grant(Fs) construct used by checked programs, then pastes a formatter command. Static checking proves which effect roots the turn can reach, but the REPL must still decide which real project file or executable that erased capability may touch. Maya needs the safe choice explained at the moment it matters. Dev needs the same effect proof with explicit invocation flags in a scripted session, without learning a REPL-only authorization system.

options.name: Prompted invocation policy
options.detail: Require an enclosing #Grant(root) for every effectful turn. In an interactive TTY, when the corresponding existing --allow-root policy was not supplied, pause before each not-yet-authorized external operation and offer once, session, or deny. Once covers exactly the displayed operation/resource tuple and is discarded before execution, so success or failure cannot retain it. Session stores exactly `(root effect, operation kind, resource identity/scope)` in memory: Env.Read HOME does not cover Env.Write HOME, Exec.Run tool A does not cover tool B or Exec.Exit, and a multi-resource turn prompts separately in execution order before performing each newly reached operation. On reuse, the same authorization preflight names the matching session allowance and offers continue or revoke; revoke deletes that tuple before the operation and returns to once/session/deny. This prompt/preflight is the sole inspection and revocation surface, not a second permission mechanism. All session tuples disappear on REPL exit or restart. Existing --allow-root flags skip ordinary root prompts for that invocation but do not relax confinement or lexical #Grant; non-TTY never prompts and requires the corresponding flag. Exec.Exit is never subsumed by Exec.Run, a session tuple, or --allow-exec: every interactive exit gets a separate `[y/N]` consequence prompt, while non-TTY requires #Grant(Exec) plus --allow-exec and exits without prompting. Recommended: beginner authority stays contextual and safe, experts get auditable flags, and both use Jet's one effect model. All shared confinement, pinning, Env, Time, Rand, Io, diagnostic, and native-only invariants above apply. Process Capture is inherent REPL output; Inherit/Stream/file redirects require their separately proven Io/Fs roots and policies.
options.code:
$ jet repl --project /work/api
user> use core.files as files
ok
user> #Grant(Fs) { caps -> files.read("config.toml") }
Core effect Fs requests runtime authority before this operation.
  operation: read
  target:    config.toml
  confined:  /work/api (descriptor-relative, no symlinks)
  [o] once  [s] exact tuple for this session  [d] deny
s
port = 8080 : Result

user> #Grant(Fs) { caps -> files.read("config.toml") }
Using session Fs.Read authority for `config.toml`. [c] continue  [r] revoke
c
port = 8080 : Result

user> use core.env as env
ok
user> #Grant(Env) { caps -> env.get("HOME") }
Core effect Env requests runtime authority: Read key HOME. [o] once  [s] exact tuple for session  [d] deny
s
/work/api : Option
user> #Grant(Env) { caps -> env.set("HOME", "/tmp") }
Core effect Env requests runtime authority: Write key HOME. [o] once  [s] exact tuple for session  [d] deny
d
Error [E1803]: Env.Write for `HOME` was denied
 Why: session authority covers Env.Read for this key, not mutation
 Fix: choose once or session only if this write is intended

user> use core.process as process
ok
user> #Grant(Exec) { caps -> process.run(["jet", "fmt", "build/preview.jet"]) }
Core effect Exec requests runtime authority before this operation.
  executable: /work/api/.jet/toolchain/bin/jet (identity pinned)
  argv:       jet fmt build/preview.jet
  cwd:        /work/api
  env:        minimal declared environment
  timeout:    30s
  redirects:  Capture (inherent REPL output; no Io grant)
  [o] once  [s] exact Exec.Run tuple for session  [d] deny
o
ProcessResult(code: 0, output: , errors: ) : Result

user> #Grant(Exec) { caps -> process.exit(7) }
Core effect Exec requests orderly REPL exit with status 7. [y/N]
y
# terminal restored; children reaped; REPL exits 7

$ printf 'use core.files as files\n#Grant(Fs) { caps -> files.read("config.toml") }\n' | jet repl --allow-fs
port = 8080 : Result

options.name: Flags only
options.detail: Require #Grant(root) in the turn and the corresponding existing --allow-root flag at REPL startup. Never prompt and never persist policy. The flag opens only that bare-root invocation ceiling; each lexical capability remains dynamically narrowed to the concrete operation/resource. All shared confinement, root fixation, process/network pinning, Env key/direction, Time/Clock, Rand/Rng, Io/Capture, diagnostic, and native-only invariants above apply independently. Thus --allow-env plus #Grant(Env) may perform the exact Env.Read/Env.Write operation reached, seeded Clock/Rng need no flag, Capture needs no --allow-io, Inherit/Stream need #Grant(Io) plus --allow-io, and a file redirect also needs #Grant(Fs) plus --allow-fs. A missing flag reports E1803 after lexical proof. Exec.Exit is a distinct operation never obtained from an Exec.Run resource capability; under this flags-only option it requires #Grant(Exec) plus --allow-exec, performs orderly cleanup, and never prompts. Without both it cannot terminate anything. This is maximally predictable for automation and experts, but beginners must understand invocation policy before their first ambient operation.
options.code:
$ jet repl
user> use core.files as files
ok
user> #Grant(Fs) { caps -> files.read("config.toml") }
Error [E1803]: this REPL invocation does not allow Fs
 Why: #Grant proves lexical authority, but host policy did not pass --allow-fs
 Fix: restart with `jet repl --allow-fs`; access remains confined to the REPL root

$ jet repl --allow-fs --allow-exec
user> use core.files as files
ok
user> #Grant(Fs) { caps -> files.read("config.toml") }
port = 8080 : Result
user> use core.process as process
ok
user> #Grant(Exec) { caps -> process.exit(0) }
# orderly exit: terminal restored, children reaped, status 0

$ printf 'use core.files as files\n#Grant(Fs) { caps -> files.read("config.toml") }\n' | jet repl --allow-fs
port = 8080 : Result

options.name: Pure REPL only
options.detail: The REPL executes pure Core plus deterministic injected Clock/Rng values only. #Grant remains valid Jet syntax, but external Fs, Env, Exec, Net, Io input, ambient Time, and ambient Rand are intentionally unavailable in this interpreter and therefore report current E1802 with the jet run/build escape. Existing --allow-* flags do not widen the REPL. No dynamic resource capabilities or persistence exist. Exec.Exit is the sole control exception: process.exit(code) does not require host Exec authority and is interpreted as an orderly REPL quit after terminal restoration; process.run/cmd/pipeline remain E1802. This draws the strongest boundary but rejects the accepted goal of exploring side-effect-safe Core in place.
options.code:
$ jet repl
user> use core.encoding.json as json
ok
user> json.parse("{\"port\":8080}")
Data(fields: [port: 8080]) : Result

user> use core.files as files
ok
user> #Grant(Fs) { caps -> files.read("config.toml") }
Error [E1802]: the REPL interpreter cannot run `core.files.read()`
 Why: this option keeps external Fs unavailable even inside #Grant
 Fix: put the code in a file and use `jet run`; --allow-fs does not widen the REPL

user> use core.process as process
ok
user> #Grant(Exec) { caps -> process.exit(0) }
# orderly REPL quit; terminal restored

$ jet repl --allow-exec
error: --allow-exec does not widen a pure-only REPL

comparisons.note: Deno separates filesystem, environment, process, and network policy and supports prompts or flags. Jet differs by requiring its existing lexical #Grant proof as well as invocation policy, and by attaching resource limits to capability handles.
comparisons.code:
Deno: --allow-read=./config --allow-net=api.example.com
Jet: #Grant(Fs) { caps -> ... } plus --allow-fs or the option-A prompt

comparisons.note: Capability-oriented filesystems operate relative to an already-open directory handle. This avoids the check-then-open race and symlink swap that realpath-prefix sandboxes miss.
comparisons.code: root_fd -> open child component with no-follow -> operate on returned handle

comparisons.note: Common REPLs inherit ambient host authority. Pasted code can mutate files/environment, launch subprocesses, or connect to the network without a lexical capability proof.
Pure evaluation rejects ambient effects unless impurity is explicitly enabled. This informs option C and the deterministic non-TTY rule in A/B.

decisions.title: Batch semantic codemod object law
decisions.gist: Choose how one replayable codemod object expresses ordered semantic rewrites across examples and UI fixtures.
decisions.explainer: D-CODEMOD1 remains the one engine. `jet codemod dry-run|apply|undo` and existing v1 objects/logs stay valid. A missing `version`, or `version: 1`, with `{entry, operation: "rename", from, to}` lowers internally to one `symbol_rename` rule and keeps today's entry-closure scope and output compatibility. Existing v1 logs remain readable; new logs carry `schema: 2` but undo lowers both schemas to the same verified inverse plan. A v2 object lowers to the same TextEdit plan, journal, log, and undo model; no second executor exists. A v2 object requires `project`, resolved relative to the object file, and `roots`. The canonical project path owns `.jet/codemods/<sanitized-name>.log.json`, `.lock`, and any recovery journal. For card #451, each root names either one regular `.jet` file or a directory, and must canonicalize beneath `<project>/examples` or `<project>/tests/ui`; `..`, absolute escape, and symlink escape fail. Directory discovery recursively sorts regular `.jet` files by project-relative byte path; a file root discovers only that file. Each discovered file is an entry compilation unit; its transitive Jet imports join that unit. The same physical file imported by several entries is indexed and edited once. Imports outside editable roots may be read for parsing, name resolution, and semantic identity but never edited; a rule selecting one fails with its path. Non-Jet files are ignored except the exact paired `tests/ui/<name>.stderr` of a touched UI fixture and declared snapshot inputs. Every rule resolves against the currently staged tree after prior rules. Within each compilation unit, every bare identifier in a match template resolves through semindex at the candidate node; that resolved definition anchor, not spelling, controls the match. Every non-capture identifier introduced by a replacement template must resolve uniquely in that same staged compilation unit before an edit is accepted. A rename destination is checked in every affected definition/reference scope and fails on collision or changed binding. A semantic symbol anchor is `(canonical definition module path, symbol kind, current definition span)`; references bind to that anchor through semindex. Independent same-spelled definitions remain independent anchors; selectors either match all and assert the total or narrow with `defined_in`. If a match source or destination resolves to zero or multiple definitions in any unit, the rule fails with unit path and candidates. Rules run in listed order. Within one rule, overlapping/nested edits fail; overlap across rules is intentional sequencing because rule N sees reindexed output from rule N-1. Duplicate ids, unknown fields, ambiguous anchors, unused captures, invalid replacement nodes, and zero matches unless `allow_zero: true` fail. Validation is transactional data, not a code-only check: a `clean` root must finish with zero lexer/parser/sema diagnostics; every touched `fixture` `.jet` must render a complete stderr snapshot. Without `snapshot_after`, generated stderr must equal the existing paired `.stderr` byte-for-byte. With `snapshot_after`, each value is a project-relative path resolved beneath the canonical project; every component must be non-symlink and the final input must be a regular file. Absolute paths, `..`, project escape, symlink, directory, and aliasing the destination `.stderr` fail. That file contains the complete replacement bytes; generated stderr must equal it byte-for-byte, and the paired `.stderr` becomes a planned edit shown in dry-run and committed/undone with source. Dry-run and apply take the exclusive codemod lock before discovery and hold it through discovery, indexing, every staged rule, validation, diagnostic rendering, final hash verification, and output/commit. The lock coordinates codemod processes only; ordinary editors need not honor it. Therefore the engine fingerprints every discovered source, read-only import, existing `.stderr`, and `snapshot_after` input on first read, rehashes all of them after rendering, and refuses with exact drift paths before printing a ready plan or writing anything if any changed. Apply rechecks every destination immediately before its rename and refuses observed drift. This does not close the check-to-rename race with a noncooperating editor: only codemod peers honor the lock, so an editor can still write after the check and be overwritten by the rename. Apply prints that limitation before confirmation; `--yes` accepts it. It writes same-directory temp files, fsyncs file contents, writes+fsyncs a journal containing transaction id, state, every before/after hash, complete before bytes, temp path, and destination, then fsyncs parent directories. Commit uses sequential same-filesystem renames; it is recoverable, not falsely advertised as globally atomic or safe from noncooperating concurrent writers. After each rename it advances and fsyncs journal state. On write/rename/fsync failure, rollback restores a destination only when its current hash equals the transaction's recorded after-hash; any other hash may be an unseen concurrent write, so recovery preserves that destination and the journal, reports the conflict, and refuses further codemod work. A crash leaves the journal. Before any later dry-run/apply/undo, the engine locks and recovers: hashes matching all after states complete the log; mixed/before states attempt the same conditional rollback, restoring only destinations still at recorded transaction hashes. Ambiguous drift or failed recovery preserves the journal, changes nothing further, prints exact paths/hashes, and refuses all codemod work until recovery can succeed. Only successful completion writes+fsyncs the schema-2 replay log and removes+fsyncs the journal. Undo first locks and verifies every current after-hash, then uses the identical temp/journal/fsync/recovery protocol to restore byte-exact before content, including `.stderr`; any mismatch causes zero writes. Dry-run writes no source, snapshot, log, temp, or new journal; after the final stable-snapshot rehash it prints path-ordered rule counts, validation, and unified source+snapshot diffs while still holding the lock.
decisions.story: Maya must update a helper across runnable examples and diagnostic fixtures. One rule renames a semantic function; another changes a call shape while preserving its argument. She needs one reviewed plan where code and every affected UI snapshot move together. Dev needs deterministic discovery, stable symbol identity, exact match counts, crash recovery, and byte-exact undo before approving the apply.

options.name: Typed AST templates
options.detail: Rules are `symbol_rename` or `ast_rewrite`. An AST rule declares `node` as `expr`, `stmt`, `item`, or `type`; `match` and `replace` are current Jet source parsed in that node class. `$name` captures exactly one subtree. `$args...` captures an ordered zero-or-more sequence only where that node grammar has a list. A repeated scalar capture requires structural equality. Bare identifiers, labels, literals, operators, and syntax match exactly after semantic name resolution; comments and layout do not participate. Replacement uses only declared captures, preserves captured bytes when safe, and otherwise formats the replacement node with `jet fmt`; variadic captures splice only into the same list kind. Every root declares `clean` or `fixture`. `clean` requires zero lexer/parser/sema diagnostics after every rule. `fixture` requires the generated final diagnostic output to equal the paired `.stderr` byte-for-byte. If expected output intentionally changes, `snapshot_after` maps the `.jet` path to a repository file containing the complete new `.stderr`; dry-run compares generated bytes to it and shows the paired `.stderr` diff, while apply writes those exact verified bytes in the same transaction. A code-only apply is impossible. Recommended: Jet-shaped patterns are readable to beginners; node classes, semantic anchors, captures, exact counts, and snapshots give experts precise control without regex.

options.name: Finite semantic operations
options.detail: Rules choose a closed registry: `symbol_rename`, `call_rename`, `call_add_named_arg`, `import_move`, or `marker_replace`. `symbol_rename` takes a semantic selector and identifier. `call_rename` changes only calls resolved to the selected function. `call_add_named_arg` parses `value` as one Jet expression, rejects an existing or positionally conflicting label, and inserts through the AST argument list. `import_move` takes exact resolved `from` and `to` module paths and preserves the local alias. `marker_replace` takes exact current PascalCase marker names, changes the marker AST node only, and rejects different argument arity; it does not text-replace comments or strings. No interpolation exists in B. Unknown operations/fields fail. Roots, anchors, ordering, exact `matches`, validation, full snapshot pairing, recoverable transaction, log, and undo are identical to the shared law. This is easiest to discover and audit, but a new migration shape requires a future ratified registry entry.

options.name: Semantic selectors and typed edits
options.detail: Each rule has `select` plus `edit`. Selectors allow only `node`, `symbol_kind`, `resolved_name`, `defined_in`, `called_from`, and exact `argument_count`; globs are project-relative and may narrow but never widen roots. Edits are `rename_symbol`, `replace_callee`, `insert_named_arg`, or `replace_node`. `replace_node.source` is parsed as the selected node class. It may interpolate `$argument[N]`, `$receiver`, or `$node`; indices are zero-based, each placeholder expands to that captured AST subtree, and no other `$` form exists. A missing/out-of-range placeholder, wrong node class, label collision, or marker/value parse error fails. Marker edits use `node: "marker"`, exact PascalCase `resolved_name`, and a complete replacement marker source such as `#New(arg)`; arguments are never implicitly copied. Roots, anchors, ordering, exact counts, validation, full snapshot pairing, journal, log, and undo follow the shared law. This gives experts strongest targeting, but simple work requires learning selector/edit vocabulary.

comparisons.note: Structural templates with holes stay readable across formatting. Option A adds Jet node classes and semantic resolution.
Semantic matchers separate identity from edits. Option C adopts that precision with a deliberately small selector set.
Compiler facts produce checked edits and conflicts stop the run. Jet adds ordered multi-rule objects, paired diagnostic snapshots, and recoverable replay logs.

decisions.title: Default jet prove execution semantics
decisions.gist: Choose what default `jet prove` runs and what pass, proved, incomplete, failure, and panic mean.
decisions.explainer:
Common producer law: TARGET may be one `.jet` file, package directory, or workspace directory. Resolution and lexicographic file order reuse `jet test`. Front-end checks run first. Per file, doctests run in source order, then the existing compiled test harness runs `#Test` declarations in declaration order. Parameterized `#Test fn` uses the existing seeded property generator and shrinker; plain `#Test` is unit evidence. Failed `require` or `require_eq` inside the test harness is a caught assertion: that test fails, later harness tests continue, final exit is at least 1. `panic(...)`, bounds/key stops, and failed `@Pre`/`@Post` contracts are uncaught runtime stops. They retain E3001/E3005, terminate that child with 70, mark declarations trapped in that child skipped with `prior_runtime_panic`, and the controller continues independent later files and budgets. A reached contract attaches to the producer invocation that called it; an unreached clause remains declared/not_observed. Deterministic budgets reuse the build/package producer; statistical budgets reuse the benchmark profile and pinned baseline producer. Order is front end, doctests, unit/property harness, deterministic budgets, statistical budgets. Front-end failure marks execution evidence skipped/prior_frontend_failure. Exit precedence after valid invocation is 101 ICE, then 70 if any child had an uncaught runtime stop, then 1 for user/static/caught-assertion/budget/policy failure, then 0. Exit 2 is malformed CLI before any report. No raw rustc message, generated-Rust path, backtrace, or type name may enter any view.

Every option produces the same semantic ProofReport envelope. Required fields are `schemaVersion`, `evidencePolicy`, `target`, `tool`, `result`, `exitCode`, `summaries`, `evidence`, and `diagnostics`. `target={kind:file|package|workspace,root,members:[{path,sha256}],inputSha256}`. `tool={jet,proofProducer,targetTriple}`. `result=pass|pass_incomplete|fail`. Every summaries member is required: `frontEnd={selected,proved,failed,skipped}`; `doctest` and `unit` each `{selected,passed,failed,skipped}`; `property={selected,passed,failed,skipped,generatedCases,shrunkFailures}`; `contract={selected,declared,observed,passed,failed,notObserved,skipped}`; `deterministicBudget` and `statisticalBudget` each `{selected,met,failed,skipped,unavailable}`. Evidence items require `{id,producer,kind,state,outcome,count,source,attachment,reason,property,contract,budget,diagnosticIndexes}`. `kind=front_end|doctest|unit|property|contract|deterministic_budget|statistical_budget`; `state=declared|checked|executed|zero|unavailable|skipped`; `outcome=proved|passed|failed|observed|not_observed|met|unavailable|not_run`; absent typed payloads are null. Property payload is `{effectiveSeed,caseIndex,generatedCases,shrinkTrace:[{name,value}],source:{path,line,column},toolchain:{jet,targetTriple}}`. Contract payload is `{marker:Pre|Post,site:{path,line,column},observation:reached_pass|reached_fail|not_reached}`. Budget payload is `{profile,kind:deterministic|statistical,observations,baselineId,limit,actual,unit}` with unknown values null.

Diagnostics are a required typed union which preserves product output, not merely a code. Every variant has `{type,code,severity,message,origin,span,caret,notes,frames,context,safeLocals}`. `type=front_end|producer|runtime`; `severity=error|warning`; `origin={stage,producer}`; span is null or `{path,startLine,startColumn,endLine,endColumn,sourceLine}`; caret is null or `{startColumn,width}`; notes is ordered text. Front-end and producer diagnostics such as E0965/E2901 preserve their exact What message, Why and Fix as ordered notes, source span, source line, and caret; frames/context/safeLocals are empty. Runtime E3001/E3005 preserve the Jet message, Jet source span/caret, ordered Jet frames, source context lines, and D-OBS2 safe locals `{name,type,value,redacted}`; they contain no rustc material. Evidence references diagnostics by zero-based `diagnosticIndexes`.

Every summary is derived from evidence, never independently counted. For frontEnd, doctest, unit, and property, `selected = proved|passed + failed + skipped` using the fields appropriate to that kind. Property `generatedCases` is the sum of evidence property.generatedCases and `shrunkFailures` counts failed property evidence with a nonempty shrinkTrace. Contract summary is `{selected,declared,observed,passed,failed,notObserved,skipped}` with `selected=declared=passed+failed+notObserved+skipped` and `observed=passed+failed`; each count derives from contract observation evidence. Each budget summary satisfies `selected=met+failed+skipped+unavailable`; all five counts derive from budget evidence. A report violating an equation is invalid. `zero` is successful discovery with count 0 and is complete. `unavailable` means an applicable producer could not start or lacked input; reason is `missing_baseline|missing_tool|unsupported_target|producer_start_failed`; state and outcome are both `unavailable`, matching D-JPROOF1. `skipped` is deliberate non-execution; reason is `prior_frontend_failure|prior_runtime_panic|not_executed_by_mode|fail_fast_policy`. Existing E0613/E2901/E3001/E3005/E0965 copy passes through unchanged. This decision allocates E2940 with registry-ready copy: What `required proof evidence is unavailable`; Why `the complete_required policy needs {producer}, but {reason}`; Fix `{producer-specific imperative action}`. Render example: `Error [E2940]: required proof evidence is unavailable` / `Why: the complete_required policy needs statistical budget checkout-p95, but no matching baseline exists` / `Fix: run jet bench src/payments.jet on the pinned profile to record the baseline`. It ships only after diagnostics registry, exact UI snapshot, `jet explain`, generated reference, and coverage satisfy I4.

One in-memory ProofReport drives terminal semantics and `--json` prints that exact ProofReport object, with no artifact metadata wrapper. D-JPROOF1 alone chooses `.jproof` serialization, path, identity, privacy, overwrite, and delivery metadata. Its artifact envelope embeds the byte-for-byte same semantic object as required member `proofReport`; artifact metadata is its sibling, never merged into or substituted for ProofReport. This ballot requires D-JPROOF1 to embed the exact ProofReport for pass, incomplete, caught assertion, producer failure, E3001, and E3005 before exit 0/1/70; it alleges no artifact path or wire schema. Usage 2, pre-identity load failure 1, and ICE 101 produce no valid artifact. No option invokes replay or a solver. `proved` is reserved for a fact universally discharged by the existing front end. Tests, sampled properties, doctests, reached contracts, and budgets say passed, failed, observed, or met.
decisions.story: Mara inherits a payment package with compiler-checked refinements, unit and property tests, doctests, `@Pre`/`@Post` contracts, and performance budgets. She needs one beginner command that runs existing evidence without calling sampled behavior proved. CI needs the identical typed report, including full Jet diagnostics, shrunk property evidence, skipped work, unavailable baselines, and a durable failed or panicked `.jproof` report.
decisions.inWild:
$ jet prove src/payments.jet
CHECKED  types, refinements, effects
PASSED   12 unit, 4 property, 3 doctest
OBSERVED 7 contract checks; 2 declared clauses not reached
UNAVAILABLE statistical budget `checkout-p95`: missing baseline
RESULT   pass; evidence incomplete
# D-JPROOF1 embeds this exact ProofReport before exit.
$ echo $?
0

# Exact current runtime stderr: no compile-diagnostic wrapper.
$ jet prove src/panic_worker.jet
panic: worker stopped
  --> src/panic_worker.jet:9 in worker
    |

decisions.title: .jproof evidence artifact contract
decisions.gist: Choose the durable envelope around the exact ProofReport produced by `jet prove`.
decisions.explainer:
D-PROVE-SEM1 owns the sole semantic object: exact `ProofReport={schemaVersion,evidencePolicy,target,tool,result,exitCode,summaries,evidence,diagnostics}`. `.jproof` embeds that complete object under logical member `proofReport`; no parallel fact, evidence, outcome, diagnostic, count, or producer schema exists in this decision. The logical version-1 envelope has exactly six required members: `schema:"jet.jproof"`, `version:1`, 64-lowercase-hex `report_id`, `artifact:{path}`, `privacy:{absolute_paths,argv,environment,full_source,producer_transcripts,safe_locals}`, and the complete `proofReport`. Artifact metadata is only `schema`, `version`, `report_id`, `artifact`, and `privacy`. `jet prove --json` prints the A-canonical ProofReport plus one LF, not the artifact envelope, in every option. Human output projects that same object. D-PROVE-SEM1 decides semantic states, summaries, diagnostics, exits, and when reports exist; this decision only persists the object.

Version 1 target identity is exactly ProofReport.target. `kind` is file/package/workspace; `root` is the normalized project-relative selected root; `members[{path,sha256}]` is the complete sorted normal-loader input closure: Jet sources/imports, effective package/workspace manifests, lock data, generated sources, and build inputs that affect checked TIR. Each path is project-relative and unique; generated/logical inputs receive their stable project-relative loader identity. Members sort by exact UTF-8 path bytes. `inputSha256` is SHA-256 of each member's A-canonical JSON plus LF, concatenated in member order. Tool identity remains ProofReport.tool. Nothing outside ProofReport is allowed to alter target or producer meaning.

`report_id` is lowercase SHA-256 of the exact A-canonical ProofReport bytes plus one LF. It excludes all envelope metadata because none is semantic; path, privacy declaration, serialization option, and later signatures cannot change semantic identity. Readers recompute target.inputSha256 and report_id before trusting the artifact. The emitted artifact's separate SHA-256 covers every canonical artifact byte and is the boundary a later signing decision would sign, excluding only a future envelope `signatures` member/record; this ballot adds no signing or trust command.

Privacy happens before persistence, inside the D-PROVE-SEM1 report producer. The envelope cannot redact or add semantics without breaking report_id. It records the applied policy: absolute paths, argv, environment, full source, and producer transcripts omitted; D-OBS2 governs safe-local redaction already present in ProofReport. Project-relative paths, source spans/lines, semantic diagnostic messages, property counterexamples/shrink values, budget values, and any unredacted safe local present in ProofReport are disclosed. Users must treat `.jproof` as sensitive evidence. No unratified include-source, encryption, destination, overwrite, or inspection flag is introduced.

A-canonical JSON means UTF-8, no BOM, no insignificant whitespace, exactly one LF after a complete JSON value, object keys sorted by Unicode scalar value recursively, arrays kept in ProofReport order, and integers in shortest decimal; floats and negative zero are forbidden. Schema/extension keys must be NFC. User/source strings and paths preserve exact Unicode scalars. Escape quote/backslash as `\"`/`\\`; use `\b|\t|\n|\f|\r` and lowercase `\u00xx` for other controls; emit all other scalars as UTF-8, including U+2028/U+2029, and never escape `/`. Duplicate keys after key normalization fail. Version-1 readers retain unknown envelope and ProofReport members as complete JSON values, include them in canonical hashes/order, and losslessly re-emit them; unknown enums fail unsupported. Unknown major version fails E3613.

Artifact lifecycle is common except final-path policy. Jet canonicalizes the project, takes an exclusive mode-0600 project proof lock, creates new artifact directories mode 0700, and resolves every parent/final component no-follow. Absolute/`..` escape, symlink, non-directory parent, or non-regular final is E3614. A same-directory random temp is opened exclusive/no-follow mode 0600, fully written, file-fsynced, atomically committed without replacement, then parent-dir-fsynced before success. Unsupported primitives fail before writing. Failure removes only the owned temp. Crash leftovers are cleaned under lock only after reserved-name and regular/no-link validation. Cooperative runs serialize; exclusive temp plus no-replace prevents an uncooperative creator from being overwritten. No partial final artifact is observable.

E3611-E3614 are disjoint from sibling replay diagnostics and reserved here: corrupt/hash/canonical failure; wrong target; unsupported artifact version; unsafe path. Each exits 1. Malformed CLI remains 2, runtime stop 70, ICE 101. They must enter diagnostics.md, exact UI snapshots, `jet explain`, generated references, and coverage before shipping under I4.
decisions.story: Mara archives a successful refinement proof, then a failed property report. Six months later a reviewer must identify the exact file, package, or workspace inputs and Jet producer, recover the same ProofReport CI saw from `--json`, distinguish corruption from a proof failure, and know which sensitive values were omitted. Serialization may vary, but no artifact format may reinterpret, summarize, or duplicate proof semantics.

 Why: `.jet/proofs/file/refinements` is a symbolic link, so Jet cannot confine the write beneath this project
 Fix: replace the link with a regular project directory, then run `jet prove examples/features/types/refinements.jet` again

decisions.title: General replay capture invocation and .jreplay law
decisions.gist: Choose how users start replay capture while keeping one exact, private, deterministic .jreplay contract.
decisions.explainer:
Common law for A, B, and C follows. D-PROVE-REPLAY1 consumption stays exactly `jet prove <target> --replay <artifact>`; no option creates `jet replay`, changes `jet run`, or adds auxiliary out/encrypt/key/case flags. Each option chooses one complete capture invocation. Capture grammar is closed and parseable. Flag models use exactly `jet prove TARGET --capture` or `jet prove TARGET --capture=ARTIFACT`, and sensitive counterparts replace the flag with `--capture-sensitive`; TARGET is the sole positional before the flag, ARTIFACT exists only after `=`, and a spaced artifact argument is usage error 2. Subcommand models use exactly `jet prove capture TARGET` or `jet prove capture TARGET ARTIFACT`, with sensitive counterpart `capture-sensitive`; TARGET is first positional and optional ARTIFACT second, while a third positional is usage error 2. `--` is not accepted by capture forms. Relative artifacts are project-relative; absolute artifacts follow common explicit-path law.\n\nTarget selection reuses current `jet run TARGET` resolution without a replay-only selector. A `.jet` file is one runnable unit when current run resolution accepts its file entry, otherwise capture reports that existing diagnostic. A package directory selects its manifest's current default runnable target; a workspace directory enumerates current runnable member defaults in lexicographic package-name/path order. Package/workspace capture requires exactly one resolved runnable target after current selection; zero or multiple fail E3624 before build or program effects and list exact package, target, and entry paths. One invocation produces one run and at most one artifact. Capture first resolves target, checks source, computes the full reachable effect/native graph, validates ordinary invocation authority, privacy mode, cardinality, target support, and output destination, then builds. Capture never grants an effect: every ambient operation still needs its normal lexical gate and existing `--allow-*` invocation policy. FFI, native callbacks, dynamic loading, tasks/concurrency, wall-driven scheduling, Fs, Env, Exec, Db, Gpu, and any opaque call graph fail E3625 during preflight; Jet must prove absence before starting the child, never discover them after partial effects. Replay grants zero ambient effects and opens no clock, RNG, stdin, terminal, DNS, socket, file, environment, subprocess, FFI, task, or GPU boundary. It only reads the artifact and build inputs, injects records, and verifies requests/outcome; any attempted unrecorded ambient boundary is E3623.

The canonical bytes are: 8-byte ASCII magic `JREPLAY\0`; little-endian u16 major and minor; little-endian u32 canonical-header length; canonical-header bytes; zero or more frames; footer. Version 1.0 header is UTF-8 JSON with no BOM, ASCII field names sorted by byte value, no whitespace, no duplicate keys, strings escaped with JSON's shortest valid escape, integers as minimal base-10 JSON integers, no floats, and no null for required fields. User text is preserved as exact Unicode scalar values and never normalized; unpaired surrogates and invalid UTF-8 fail E3622. Schema paths are UTF-8 project-relative forward-slash paths with no empty, `.`, `..`, absolute, NUL, or symlink component; a non-UTF-8 project path is unsupported E3625. Binary values use unpadded base64url; signed/unsigned 64-bit values that exceed exact JSON integer range use lowercase fixed-width hexadecimal strings; floats use exact lowercase IEEE-754 bit-pattern hexadecimal strings, preserving NaN payload and signed zero. Required header fields are `schema`, `version`, `artifact_id`, `producer`, `identity`, `capture`, `privacy_salt`, `limits`, and `run`; unknown required fields/record kinds fail E3620. Unknown optional fields are permitted only under sorted `extensions` maps, are hashed, preserved by copy/export, and ignored by an older same-major reader. Binary prefix major/minor must equal header version major/minor byte-for-byte; disagreement is corrupt E3622. Same major with understood required vocabulary is accepted; newer major fails E3620 without guessing.

Normative complete v1 one-frame fixture is 1054 bytes and contains TimeWall kind 0x0001 at sequence 0. Full-file base64 is ``. Frame prefix hex is `010100000000000000000082000000`; canonical payload length is 130 and payload SHA-256 is `4f707c1f1646e3140e8568677986c97e9ba96b578b5458a6de84d127c37bea9d`; frame SHA-256 is `a6d276ec274673175c47deaaa8ba148859cebdf752efbdb5d89c2fbbe03f653f`; footer frame count is 1 and payload-byte count is 130; content id is `c10aee50b2a70ae2bfc02072`; footer SHA-256 (bytes before JEND) is `ba8d8e037dbb6e1cd90251551e40f6ebeb6a56df9c22249b6bbdc8126128b8ed`; full-file SHA-256 is `72bf4a0448f895b84993950ee59061d04ea3fe4378fdd05c4c679d717dae7090`. The fixture privacy_salt is the deterministic 32-zero-byte test value `AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA`; production salts are OS-random. All values are normative and pinned byte-for-byte. Its normative test-vector path is `.jet/replays/fixture-c10aee50b2a7.jreplay`; production uses a random privacy_salt and therefore prints `.jet/replays/fixture-<artifact-id>.jreplay`, never this predetermined id. Every transcript below labels artifact content abbreviated. Frame kind registry is closed in v1: 0x0001 TimeWall `{site_id,call_id,unix_ns}`; 0x0002 TimeMonotonic `{site_id,call_id,ticks_ns}`; 0x0003 TimeSleep `{site_id,call_id,requested_ns,outcome}` where outcome is exactly `{"kind":"completed"}` or `{"error":"interrupted","kind":"error"}`; 0x0010 RandBits `{site_id,call_id,requested_bits,bits}`; 0x0020 IoRead `{site_id,call_id,stream_id,requested_bytes}`; 0x0021 IoChunk `{stream_id,chunk_index,bytes}`; 0x0022 IoEnd `{stream_id,chunks,total_bytes,outcome}` where outcome is exactly `{"kind":"eof"}` or `{"error":<portable error>,"kind":"error"}`; 0x0030 NetRequest `{site_id,call_id,request_id,method,scheme,host,port,path,redirect_index,header_digests,body_digest}` where redirect_index is u32 and header_digests is an application-order array of `{name,digest_sha256}`; 0x0031 NetDns `{request_id,addresses}` where addresses is an application-return-order array of canonical textual IP addresses; 0x0032 NetResponse `{request_id,status,headers}` where status is u16 and headers is an application-order array of `{name,value}` with exact text/bytes Jet values; 0x0033 NetChunk `{request_id,chunk_index,bytes}`; 0x0034 NetEnd `{request_id,chunks,total_bytes,outcome}` where outcome is exactly `{"kind":"eof"}` or `{"error":<portable error>,"kind":"error"}`; 0x00f0 Outcome is exactly normal/explicit exit `{"kind":"exit","status":i32,"stderr_len":u64,"stderr_sha256":"64 hex","stdout_len":u64,"stdout_sha256":"64 hex"}` or runtime stop `{"diagnostic_code":"<exact emitted Jet code>","exit_code":70,"kind":"runtime_stop","stderr_len":u64,"stderr_sha256":"64 hex","stdout_len":u64,"stdout_sha256":"64 hex"}`; runtime_stop preserves E3001, E3005, or any other existing exit-70 diagnostic code exactly and never relabels it; diagnostic_code is forbidden for exit and required for runtime_stop, so null is never encoded; 0x4000 GameEvent `{name,payload}`, where name is exactly `game.v1.action|game.v1.fixed_step|game.v1.backend|game.v1.budget`. Absent variant fields and extra top-level fields are forbidden; extensions stay under `extensions`. `site_id` is lowercase SHA-256 of length-delimited checked TIR hash, function stable id, instruction ordinal, and u16 kind. `call_id` is zero-based per-site invocation count. Io stream_id and Net request_id equal the start-frame sequence. Canonical Jet values use these complete tagged objects and no other keys: unit `{"t":"unit"}` requires only `t`; Bool `{"t":"bool","v":true|false}` requires `t,v`; signed/unsigned integer `{"bits":8|16|32|64|128,"t":"int"|"uint","v":"<minimal decimal string>"}` requires `bits,t,v`; Float `{"bits":32|64,"t":"float","v":"<fixed-width lowercase IEEE-754 hex>"}` requires `bits,t,v`; text `{"t":"text","v":"<exact Unicode scalar sequence>"}` requires `t,v`; bytes `{"t":"bytes","v":"<unpadded base64url>"}` requires `t,v`; list `{"t":"list","v":[<canonical Jet value>,...]}` requires `t,v` and preserves order; record `{"fields":[{"name":"<ASCII field name>","value":<canonical Jet value>},...],"t":"record"}` requires `fields,t`, each field requires exactly `name,value`, and fields sort by ASCII name. Missing, extra, or duplicate keys/fields, unsupported widths/types, and noncanonical values are E3622.\n\nPortable error is exactly one string from `interrupted|timed_out|would_block|broken_pipe|connection_aborted|connection_refused|connection_reset|not_connected|address_in_use|address_unavailable|permission_denied|not_found|unexpected_eof|invalid_data`. Each platform adapter has a pinned OS-error-to-one-string table. An OS error absent from or ambiguous in that table fails closed with E3625, terminates capture, and emits no valid artifact; raw OS numbers/messages are never recorded. TimeSleep permits only `interrupted`; IoEnd and NetEnd permit the whole registry.\n\nEach frame is u8 flags (bit 0 required; other bits zero), u16 kind, u64 sequence, u32 payload length, payload bytes, and 32 raw SHA-256 bytes over flags through payload. Numbers are little-endian. Sequence starts at 0 and is contiguous. Payload is the same canonical JSON law. Duplicate sequence/site/request ids, out-of-order frames, unknown required kind, noncanonical JSON, bad length/hash/footer, trailing bytes, or truncation is E3622. Footer is ASCII `JEND`, u64 frame count, u64 total payload bytes, then SHA-256 covering exactly byte 0 through the byte immediately before ASCII `JEND`; no footer byte participates. Artifact identity uses a separate deterministic content-id hash: serialize header-through-frames with `artifact_id` as exactly 24 ASCII zeroes, SHA-256 those bytes, take the first 24 lowercase hex digits, then serialize the real header and footer. A reader verifies both the zeroed-field content id and the actual-byte footer hash. Default final path is `.jet/replays/<sanitized-entry>-<artifact_id[0..12]>.jreplay`; sanitization is lowercase ASCII alphanumeric plus `-`, with other runs replaced by one `-`. Records are ordered by actual single-thread boundary order. Time and Rand values fit one frame. Io/Net byte streams use contiguous chunks of at most 1 MiB with stream id, chunk index, EOF/error terminal record. Limits are 100000 frames, 1 MiB per payload, and 256 MiB total artifact. Crossing a limit stops the child, deletes the temp, emits E3628, and emits no valid artifact.

A Time request records operation, stable checked-TIR site id, arguments, and exact returned wall/monotonic value or sleep completion; replay uses a virtual clock and never sleeps. Rand records operation, site, requested shape/length, and exact returned bits. Safe mode records Time only. Rand is raw nondeterministic data and requires the same sensitive consent as Io.Read/terminal and Net; sensitive mode records Time, Rand, Io.Read/terminal, and Net. Net outbound matching uses method, scheme, host, explicit port, path, ordered header-name/value digests, body digest, redirect index, and stable site; response records application-visible DNS addresses, status, ordered headers, chunks, EOF/error. Replay requires byte-identical request digests and consumes the next matching record; missing, extra, reordered, wrong-site, wrong-shape, or unconsumed records are E3623. No performance sample, span, allocation, scheduler event, lock event, wall-duration profile, source map, flamegraph, or OTel field may appear; those belong only to card #441 `.jtrace`.

Untainted data may still contain secrets. Every option's safe form refuses reachable Rand, raw Io.Read, terminal input, and Net before execution with E3627. Each option's explicitly named sensitive form is the sole consent path for storing their exact raw values; preflight prints authorities, host names, maximum bytes, residual disclosures, and destination, and requires typing the exact TTY phrase `capture sensitive`; non-interactive capture refuses E3627. Its artifact is mode 0600 but not encrypted: anyone who can read it can read stdin, response bodies, DNS results, paths, host names, panic text, and run metadata. Any value Jet proves secret or tainted in outbound URL userinfo, query values, header names/values, or body fails E3627 before the request is sent and no artifact is finalized. Every artifact generates a control-plane 32-byte OS-random `privacy_salt`, encoded in the header as exactly 43-character unpadded base64url; generation failure is E3629 before program execution. Header digest preimage is ASCII `jet.replay.v1/net-header`, one NUL byte, raw 32-byte salt, u64-big-endian name length, exact name bytes, u64-big-endian value length, exact value bytes. Body digest preimage is ASCII `jet.replay.v1/net-body`, one NUL, raw salt, u64-big-endian body length, exact body bytes. Each stored digest is 64 lowercase SHA-256 hex; replay decodes/length-checks salt, recomputes each digest, and divergence is E3623. Fixed-salt digest vectors use 32 zero bytes: header name UTF-8 `x-test` and value UTF-8 `abc` produce `da5c4be2ec0c362a0a7f2ecf6c989f6702f356b67223ba5e520c33c3dde111fa`; body UTF-8 `hello` produces `a0187a1248e5a0292177421845e354004354b6b9c59b985d9daed43d335c3a05`. Implementations pin both preimages and expected hashes. Because salt is stored and values may have low entropy, this hides plaintext bytes but does not prevent offline guessing; preflight states that residual disclosure. Stdout/stderr raw bytes are never stored: outcome stores byte length plus SHA-256 and replay compares both. Terminal still receives live stdout/stderr. Secret/taint proven at any stored inbound boundary fails E3627 even in B; users must supply sanitized deterministic input. Reports never print payloads.

This decision allocates disjoint codes: E3620 `replay schema version is incompatible`; E3621 `replay semantic identity does not match`; E3622 `replay artifact is corrupt`; E3623 `replay diverged at record {sequence}`; E3624 `replay target cardinality is not one`; E3625 `replay capture cannot model {operation}`; E3626 `replay capture lacks {effect} authority`; E3627 `replay capture refused sensitive data`; E3628 `replay capture exceeded its artifact limit`; E3629 `replay artifact could not be finalized`. Why names respectively the unsupported version, first identity field, byte/frame violation, request digest, candidates, unsupported effect/native/task/adapter, missing existing grant, raw/tainted field, actual vs maximum size, or exact path/race/filesystem failure. Fix gives the corresponding supported reader, recorded revision/toolchain, intact artifact, recapture action, single current target, source/target change, existing lexical and invocation grant, sanitized input/B choice, input reduction, or path action. E3620-E3629 exit 1 and each requires diagnostics.md exact what/why/fix, UI snapshot, jet explain, and generated reference before use. Usage is 2, captured/replayed E3001 panic 70, ICE 101.

After preflight, Jet creates a mode-0600 same-directory temp using no-follow exclusive creation, streams bounded frames, fsyncs content, writes/fsyncs footer, closes, verifies canonical bytes/hash/id, then atomically rename-no-replace to final path and fsyncs the directory. Existing final path is accepted only when its complete bytes equal the new artifact; Jet deletes temp and reports `already captured`. Different bytes at that path fail E3629; nothing overwrites. Default naming is content-deterministic. Explicit paths supplied by the chosen invocation must be project-beneath, no-follow, and nonexistent. Crash leaves only `.jreplay.tmp.<pid>.<nonce>`; next capture removes an old temp only after no-follow ownership/mode check and never treats it as evidence. A normal exit, explicit nonzero exit, or captured `runtime_stop` exit 70 finalizes the artifact. runtime_stop preserves the exact emitted diagnostic code: E3001, E3005, or any other existing exit-70 code; none is relabeled. CLI returns 0 for exit 0, 1 for explicit nonzero exit or replay/capture diagnostic, 70 for captured/replayed panic, 2 for wrong CLI, 101 for ICE. Authority/cardinality/privacy/unsupported/build failure, signal/kill, limit, recorder/finalization failure, and ICE emit no valid artifact. Capture streams child stdout/stderr and then prints artifact/outcome on stderr so program stdout remains exact.

Identity binds schema, Jet toolchain build id, Core ABI, TIR schema/hash, target triple/backend/profile, producer engine, entry identity, every checked source hash, package/workspace/lock/build-input digest, and authority/capture manifest. Replay requires exact source/build/TIR/target identity; mismatch is E3621. Capture adapters in dev and AOT are independent implementations over the same executable TIR: neither shells into or trusts the other. Semantic target identity (sources, lock/build inputs, checked TIR) is distinct from `execution_adapter`. Version 1 adapters are exactly `dev-tir-v1` and `aot-native-v1`. The only counterpart mapping is `dev-tir-v1 <-> aot-native-v1` for the same native target triple, ABI, profile, Core ABI, and checked TIR hash. Adapter identity may differ only by that mapping; semantic identity remains exact. Replay executes the recorded adapter first, then that mapped counterpart when supported. Each must consume all records and match outcome, and their outcomes must match each other. A target with no counterpart reports `parity: not available` and may reproduce but may not claim dev/AOT equivalence. Browser/WASM, native, and other targets never substitute a host backend. Card #238 `game.Replay.record("path.jreplay")` remains the source-owned game capture invocation and explicit path. It writes this same envelope with required record namespace `game.v1.*` for action snapshots, fixed-step timing, backend identity, and budget events owned by #238; general Time/Rand/Io/Net records are not duplicated for the same game fact. Its explicit path follows the same no-overwrite/finalization law, and `jet prove game.jet --replay path.jreplay` is the consumer.
decisions.story: Maya has one payment worker that panics after clock and random choices. She needs one bounded capture command, one private artifact, and an offline replay that proves the same outcome in the real dev and AOT engines. Dev must know exactly what bytes and authority entered the artifact; CI must reject stale source, corruption, divergence, unsupported effects, ambiguous package entries, and unsafe capture before claiming proof.
decisions.inWild:

options.name: Paired safe and sensitive flags
options.detail: Beginner capture is exactly `jet prove TARGET --capture` or `jet prove TARGET --capture=ARTIFACT` and records Time only. Expert escalation is the paired `--capture-sensitive` form and records Time/Rand/Io/Net after common disclosure. Both inherit identical artifact, authority, lifecycle, diagnostics, and parity; privacy refusal is E3627, never E3626. Recommended: safe default shortest, sensitive intent script-visible.
