decisions.detail:
Scope: approve the exact resolved 55-package temporary bridge superset only. Exact direct specs: argon2 0.5.3 (defaults off; alloc,password-hash), sha2 0.10.9 (defaults off), blake3 1.8.2 (defaults off; std,pure), hkdf 0.12.4 (defaults off), x25519-dalek 2.0.1 (defaults off; precomputed-tables,zeroize), subtle 2.6.1 (defaults off), chacha20poly1305 0.10.1 (defaults off; alloc), and ed25519-dalek 2.2.0 (defaults off; alloc,zeroize). The last two are the exact XChaCha20-Poly1305 and strict Ed25519 implementation gate shared by API1 and KEYWRAP1. blake3/pure disables BLAKE3 SIMD, assembly, and native object compilation, but its Rust build script still uses the approved build-time closure cc 1.2.66, find-msvc-tools 0.1.9, and shlex 2.0.1 and may discover or probe a native compiler. Acceptance requires a trace proving that path compiles and links no C/assembly object and emits no native object on every approved target. No entropy provider or fallback is approved. rand_core 0.6.4 is approved only as a trait/API transitive activated by password-hash without getrandom; it must never source salt, nonce, or key bytes.

Ephemeral session verification evidence and limits. The following /tmp paths identify ephemeral session evidence, not durable source artifacts. Cargo.lock: /tmp/crypto-lock-work/Cargo.lock, SHA-256 42e2879fae279e42e1a99422e94d7a96bc8965a07a4ec7b1f47bbe922c214a2d. Host metadata: /tmp/crypto-lock-work/metadata.json, SHA-256 0447f74ec3e0d21ee3f30092a83b5b09d4201cca8ce51d78ddd4fa77065e6491. Full 55-package SBOM v2: /tmp/crypto-lock-work/sbom-v2.json, SHA-256 dbe299850bf88167eea701a76e6e6f66af493f792c7d48a31ad794f27df8e6fc; it records names, versions, sources, Cargo.lock-derived registry checksums, resolved host features, SPDX expressions, and hashes of discovered license files. Generator: /tmp/crypto-evidence-generator.mjs, SHA-256 ece8aea00431f5ab5332e441644fd2ed9fc836a101ea2a342302baae1108cc39. Linux x86_64 host build trace: /tmp/crypto-lock-work/build-host.trace, SHA-256 c847cb5b539c8daab4eb66c2370509a195c8c0f1882f54beb878a7523586c5e7. It proves one host build, not cross-target process/symbol absence. The approved cc/find-msvc-tools/shlex build closure may perform compiler discovery/probing; acceptance must prove blake3/pure compiles, links, and emits no native object.

RustSec evidence is not a full scan. Provenance: https://github.com/RustSec/advisory-db.git revision e20296422feea6aab5cd36bf993c68d22e4aa24f, tree 0f86dcbe2da77cfc3ade95084200866afc00b5c0, archive /tmp/crypto-lock-work/rustsec-db.tar SHA-256 468b402bffb0ffbc713a2cbaada4b23413c0300b314cb75ad98ba0612ef9320. The current rustsec-audit.json predates this revised 55-package lock and is invalid as evidence for it; it is retained only as historical manual package-name/semver comparison. API1 and KEYWRAP1 remain blocked until a fresh full report covers this exact lock. Release requires cargo-audit 0.21.2 with recorded tool-binary hash and exact command `cargo audit --db VERIFIED_DB --file OPERATION_TARGET_LOCK --json`, stdout JSON, exit 0, DB hashes, and no ignore file, for every minimal lock. Findings, yanks, or unmaintained exceptions require a new owner ballot.

Trust evidence is unsigned. Current hashes prove local identity, not publisher authority. Release requires Ed25519 strict DSSE PAE over payload type application/vnd.jet.crypto-bridge-lock.v1 and RFC8785 fields schema, decision, generator_sha256, lock_sha256, sbom_sha256, rustsec_report_sha256, rustsec_db_sha256, target_matrix_sha256, sequence, valid_from, valid_until. Trust is 2-of-3 toolchain-pinned offline keys. Rotation is sequence+1 signed by 2 old and 2 new keys. Revocation is signed by 2 current keys and names key id plus minimum rejected sequence. Rollback, expiry, duplicate signer, mixed artifact, unknown/revoked key, or stripped signature fails before network. The owner can decide this exact evidence model and graph from the recorded hashes; the unsigned ephemeral /tmp bundle is not durable source or release-ready evidence. Before any generated build or network access, release tooling must deterministically regenerate every artifact, require exact hash matches, and place the matched lock, SBOM, audit, target-matrix, and trace evidence into durable signed release artifacts.

Target matrix: /tmp/crypto-lock-work/target-matrix.json SHA-256 6a73c20ba9ec6a5bc4e4bcf35ab7abf4d5b4abc904c288fde90f254c83125389. Operations: sha2; hkdf+hmac+sha2; blake3 portable; subtle; x25519-dalek+curve25519-dalek+fiat+zeroize; XChaCha20-Poly1305 via chacha20poly1305+chacha20+poly1305+aead+cipher; strict Ed25519 via ed25519-dalek+ed25519+signature+curve25519-dalek+sha2+zeroize; argon2+blake2+password-hash+rand_core. Targets: Linux glibc x86_64/aarch64, macOS x86_64/arm64, Windows MSVC x86_64/arm64, WASI preview1. Only Linux x86_64 is currently built. Release is blocked until one minimal lock/SBOM per operation/target exists, full audit runs, clean process/build traces and symbol scans prove no C/assembly/unused direct crate, vectors pass, and all hashes enter the signed bundle.

Conditional getrandom exists only if D-CRYPTO-RNG1=B. Direct: getrandom 0.3.3, defaults off, no features. Lock SHA-256 0eebb0c965f07ee9930db104601ca0e2b6accda166b97f789a3830b9e6202046; metadata 5bcf1433a899596a2c547527e43ba7d4ebac75ee888ae0f61931a2932617554d; seven-package SBOM v2 da37628b1aafecb61e1b39e3513f2043adcd442566fef5bc4978ba05f54c236b with Cargo.lock-derived registry checksums. Superset: cfg-if 1.0.4, getrandom 0.3.3, libc 0.2.186, r-efi 5.3.0, wasi 0.14.7+wasi-0.2.4, wasip2 1.0.4+wasi-0.2.12, wit-bindgen 0.57.1. Active slices: Linux/macOS getrandom+cfg-if+libc; Windows/WASI-preview1 getrandom+cfg-if. wasm_js/js-sys/wasm-bindgen are absent. r-efi/wasip2/wit-bindgen must be absent from active slices. Removal requires direct-provider parity on all seven targets, failure/cancel/zeroization vectors, independent review, rollback, signed lock/SBOM deletion, and symbol absence.

Before #302/Epoch 3 closes, each direct/transitive security seam has a deletion gate: subtle constant-time implementation plus assembly review; sha2 vectors/differential; hkdf RFC5869 composition; x25519 RFC7748/all-zero/clamping/zeroization/independent review; argon2 RFC9106/PHC/DoS/memory clearing/differential/independent review; blake3 official tree/chunk/boundary vectors and portable review; chacha20poly1305 RFC8439/XChaCha vectors, nonce/AAD/tamper/zeroization and independent review; ed25519-dalek RFC8032 strict-invalid/canonical-key/signature/zeroization and independent review; rand_core removal with password-hash; conditional getrandom gate above. Every row requires all approved targets, differential tests, independent sign-off, rollback, generator/lock/SBOM/cache deletion, and symbol absence.

Beginner: no dependency ceremony. Expert: exact graph and evidence gaps visible. Hybrid: one operation selects one audited minimal closure.

decisions.title: Cryptographic entropy providers and failure contract
decisions.gist: Choose how cryptographic randomness reaches Jet on each platform and how entropy failure reaches the program.
decisions.explainer:
Ratified D-RANDSPLIT1 separates deterministic core.random from cryptographic core.crypto.random. D-CRYPTO-SUITE1=A requires misuse-resistant envelopes; D-PWHASH1=A requires generated password salts; D-DEP-CRYPTO1=A permits the existing RustCrypto AEAD/signature bridge but does not choose an entropy provider. I1 and I6 remain binding. This ballot owns only cryptographic entropy acquisition, its public failure shape, and migration of callers that internally need randomness. It does not choose Secret/Key types, envelope layout, password cost, or approve a new crate.

Current truth is unsafe. Native core.crypto.random.bytes calls /dev/urandom and falls back to wall-clock SplitMix. The crypto bridge uses /dev/urandom and falls back to a constant-state xorshift for envelope nonces, Ed25519 keygen, and Argon2 salts; Windows therefore takes the predictable fallback. The API is infallible and negative lengths become zero. Comptime contains a deterministic random implementation. All of those fallback paths retire under every option.

Common security law. A cryptographic request either returns exactly the requested number of fresh operating-system bytes or fails before exposing any output. Forbidden forever: core.random, timestamps, process/thread ids, counters, UUID state, hardware identifiers, fixed seeds, reused buffers, all-zero fill, partial success, best effort, user PATH tools, /dev/random, and automatic remote entropy. Provider output is not health-tested or modified by Jet; Jet trusts only the named tier-1 platform facility and reports its failure. No user/workspace/environment setting can replace, seed, downgrade, log, or intercept the provider. There is no deterministic crypto mode, test seed, retry flag, or expert bypass.

Exact public type for A/B is:
```jet
pub enum RandomError {
    NegativeLength
    TooLarge
    Unavailable
}
```
Exact signature is bytes(count: Int) -> [U8] ? RandomError. count < 0 returns NegativeLength without allocation/provider call. count > 1_048_576 returns TooLarge without allocation/provider call. Zero returns ok([]) without provider call. Each positive provider attempt owns exactly one private full-size allocation. That allocation is never shared with another request, never reused concurrently, and never returned until the attempt completes successfully. Linux short-fill/EINTR continuation stays within that attempt and its one allocation. On failure or post-call cancellation the entire allocation is cleared by the std-only non-elidable routine: write every byte with `std::ptr::write_volatile(ptr, 0)`, then execute `std::sync::atomic::compiler_fence(Ordering::SeqCst)` before drop. No ordinary fill/memset is accepted as proof. No partial list escapes. Debug/Display is respectively `cryptographic random length cannot be negative`, `one cryptographic random request is limited to 1048576 bytes`, or `the operating system could not provide cryptographic randomness`; no OS status, path, handle, buffer, or backend text appears. Larger protocols make explicit repeated calls and remain responsible for their own framing; the per-call cap is a compatibility promise.

Direct platform contract for A/C. Linux glibc x86_64/aarch64 calls getrandom(buf,len,0), never GRND_INSECURE or GRND_NONBLOCK. It blocks until the kernel pool is initialized, retries EINTR with the unfilled suffix, treats zero or every other errno as Unavailable, and loops over short positive fills. It never opens /dev/urandom. macOS x86_64/arm64 calls Security.framework SecRandomCopyBytes(kSecRandomDefault,...); errSecSuccess with a complete call succeeds and any other OSStatus is Unavailable, with no fallback or retry. Windows MSVC x86_64/arm64 calls BCryptGenRandom(NULL,buf,len,BCRYPT_USE_SYSTEM_PREFERRED_RNG); STATUS_SUCCESS succeeds and any other NTSTATUS is Unavailable, with no CryptoAPI fallback or retry. WASI preview 1 calls random_get over one private zero-initialized full-size buffer. Success returns only that complete buffer. ERRNO_INTR ends that provider attempt and makes its whole buffer tainted: Jet volatile-zeroizes and drops it completely before allocating a distinct fresh full-size buffer for the next attempt, then retries from byte zero, at most 16 consecutive times; at most one WASI attempt buffer exists at a time and no allocation or pointer is reused across retries; the seventeenth returns Unavailable. Every other errno returns Unavailable after the same full-buffer zeroization. No partial WASI buffer or suffix retry is permitted. wasm32-unknown-unknown/browser, Linux musl, iOS/Android, other Unix, and every target not named above are unsupported by this decision and return Unavailable without probing.

Freestanding has no ambient entropy provider. core.crypto.random.bytes and every safe operation needing fresh randomness return Unavailable before cryptographic work. No memory address, cycle counter, device id, unverified RDRAND, or board hook is guessed. This ballot adds no public provider-registration callback: a future hardware entropy API must separately decide device trust, startup/continuous tests, concurrency, failure, and audit. Experts may use deterministic bytes only as explicit inputs to already-ratified expert primitives inside their existing #Unsafe gate; they cannot make safe seal/keygen/password_hash pretend those bytes are fresh entropy.

Blocking, cancellation, and retry. Entropy acquisition is a synchronous native runtime operation and may block only where the named OS call blocks. Jet adds no timeout because abandoning a kernel CSPRNG request cannot make weaker bytes acceptable. Task cancellation is outside RandomError and remains the D-TASKRUNTIME1 control-plane outcome. If already requested before allocation/provider entry, the call performs no provider work and the enclosing task takes its ordinary cancelled outcome. If observed after any provider return, Jet volatile-zeroizes the whole buffer and propagates task cancellation; it returns neither ok(bytes) nor err(RandomError). Linux glibc retries EINTR against the still-unfilled suffix. WASI uses the fresh-full-buffer retry law above. macOS/Windows status failures are final. A retry by user code is a new full request and receives a new buffer. No provider call occurs while holding a Jet scheduler/global lock.

Migration and internal consumers. A/B change random.bytes from [U8] to [U8] ? RandomError, a breaking public signature that ships in a major release plus edition opt-in. Older editions retain the source-level [U8] signature but use the selected provider immediately: invalid length or entropy failure produces existing E3001 at the Jet call with message `core.crypto.random.bytes: <RandomError Display>` and exit 70; no insecure compatibility fallback survives. This is a narrow security correction to runtime behavior, not a claim of compatibility for programs that relied on predictable fallback. This ballot authorizes the provider and random.bytes only. It does not silently change any other public error or artifact contract. Safe seal/file_seal and signing-key generation remain disabled until proposed D-CRYPTO-API1 and D-CRYPTO-ENVELOPE2 ratify their exact signatures and RandomError-cause shape. password_hash remains disabled until proposed D-PWHASH-POLICY1 ratifies its exact entropy-failure shape. CLI/package key generation and any infallible tool consumer remain disabled until proposed D-CRYPTO-DIAG1 ratifies exact Jet diagnostic copy, exit, cleanup, and no-artifact behavior. UUID migration needs its own owning law and is not authorized here. Once each gate ratifies compatibly, that consumer must call this same provider and must never catch Unavailable to substitute bytes.

Comptime/dev/JIT. core.crypto.random is unavailable in comptime, pure evaluation, package/module-field evaluation, deterministic tests, and interpreter execution; reaching it produces the existing native-only/purity boundary and never evaluates a seeded model. Delete the current comptime deterministic crypto-random arm. A native JIT may call the same provider and failure path as AOT only when parity is real; otherwise it declines before execution. core.random remains the sole deterministic/test PRNG and W0410 continues rejecting it in cryptographic contexts. Expert primitives may consume explicit test vectors at comptime only when they are pure operations and their separate law permits it; they never call this provider.

Testing seam. Provider injection exists only behind cfg(test) inside the generated/bridge runtime, is unreachable from Jet source and release artifacts, and can script short fills, EINTR, zero, failure, cancellation, and canary writes. Tests prove exact fill, one active private allocation per attempt, distinct WASI allocations across retries with no overlap/reuse, suffix retry, zeroization on failure, no output on partial failure, cap/negative preflight, and no fallback symbol/string. Released-artifact scans reject SplitMix/xorshift/timestamp fallback and test-hook symbols. Native clean-host CI runs real-provider tests on Linux glibc x86_64/aarch64, macOS x86_64/arm64, Windows x86_64/arm64, and a real WASI preview-1 runtime. Unsupported and freestanding targets prove Unavailable. Statistical tests may catch gross wiring errors but never certify security or replace provider/failure tests.

Diagnostics and audit. RandomError is a runtime value for A/B, not a new E-code. Old-edition fail-fast uses existing E3001 exactly as above. CLI/key-generation operations that cannot return RandomError require D-CRYPTO-DIAG1 ratification before shipping; raw OS errors are never printed. Audit output may record provider identity, target, requested length, success/failure, and duration, but never bytes or a reusable provider handle.

Beginner pass: request bytes and handle one typed failure; nonce/salt generation stays internal. Expert pass: provider, target matrix, blocking, retry, cap, cancellation, migration, audit, freestanding behavior, and injection proof are exact. Hybrid pass: safe envelopes, expert primitives needing fresh randomness, CLI keygen, AOT, and native JIT consume one provider implementation; no second debug/test randomness path exists.
decisions.story: Rina deploys the same Jet service on Linux glibc x86_64/aarch64, macOS, and Windows, then builds a WASI worker. It creates session keys, encryption nonces, signing keys, and password salts. An unavailable entropy source must stop that operation clearly; it must never produce a predictable key, silently return fewer bytes, or work on Linux glibc x86_64/aarch64 while becoming deterministic on Windows.

options.name: Direct OS providers, typed failure
options.detail: Recommended. Use the exact Linux glibc getrandom, macOS SecRandomCopyBytes, Windows BCryptGenRandom, and WASI random_get contract above with no new crate. Expose fallible random.bytes and propagate the same failure through every cryptographic consumer. This makes failure recoverable, keeps I6 unchanged, and gives each supported host one auditable provider.

options.name: Audited getrandom bridge, typed failure
options.detail: Use the Rust getrandom crate behind the existing generated runtime bridge, with the same public type, cap, exact-fill, no-fallback, target matrix, migration, and tests. The crate owns platform syscall details; Jet still launders errors into RandomError. This option is conditional on a separate I6 ballot approving the exact crate version, features, transitive graph, audit record, and native-implementation obligation; without that ratification B cannot ship.

options.name: Direct OS providers, fail-fast API
options.detail: Use A's exact direct providers and no-fallback law but retain random.bytes(count) -> [U8]. Invalid length or provider failure always emits E3001 and exits 70 in every edition. This avoids a signature migration, but reusable libraries cannot recover or select a safe alternative, and an expected platform limitation becomes a process-wide panic.

comparisons.note: getrandom centralizes platform CSPRNG selection and returns an error rather than weak bytes. B adopts that backend; A adopts the same fail-closed contract directly to avoid a new dependency.
crypto/rand.Reader is the one security RNG and Read fills or errors. Jet likewise separates it from deterministic core.random and forbids fallback.
getRandomValues uses the host CSPRNG and caps a request. This ballot does not claim browser support until Jet has a separately proven browser runtime provider.

decisions.title: Argon2id password policy and rehash law
decisions.gist: Choose Jet's exact Argon2id writer defaults, hostile-PHC verification limits, and upgrade signal.
decisions.story: Imani launches a login service with no cryptography tuning. Five years later Jet raises its password cost, old accounts still log in, and successful logins upgrade hashes gradually. An attacker submits a PHC string claiming a terabyte of memory and a billion passes; Jet rejects it before allocation instead of exhausting the server.
decisions.detail:
Inherited law. D-PWHASH1=A ratifies one self-describing Argon2id PHC writer, verification from stored parameters, old-hash verification, and expert cost control. D-CRYPTO-SUITE1=A requires safe beginner APIs plus audited expert primitives. Proposed D-CRYPTO-API1 owns Secret and PasswordHash nominal types and final Result spelling; this ballot owns policy values and parser/resource behavior. Proposed D-CRYPTO-RNG1 must ratify a compatible fallible OS provider before password_hash ships. D-DEP-CRYPTO1=A does not by itself approve the final password suite. Proposed D-DEP-CRYPTO-SUITE2 must approve the exact Argon2 implementation version, features, transitive graph, audit record, and native-replacement obligation before any option ships; this ballot approves no crate. Option A exact writer. `password_hash` always writes Argon2id version 0x13 as canonical PHC `$argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=3,p=1$$`. Memory m is 65,536 KiB total, iterations t=3, lanes p=1, salt is exactly 16 fresh bytes from RNG1, output is exactly 32 bytes. PHC base64 is the PHC alphabet without padding; writer parameter order is exactly m,t,p and decimal integers have no sign/leading zero. Password bytes are used exactly as supplied: no Unicode normalization, trimming, case folding, NUL termination, or text encoding conversion after Secret construction. Empty password is valid; input cap is 1,048,576 bytes. Generated salt, intermediate blocks, derived output before PHC encoding, and password-owned scratch are non-elidably zeroized after last use. Accepted PHC grammar. Safe PasswordHash.parse accepts only `$argon2id$v=19$m=,t=,p=

$$` with exactly six `$` fields, exactly one each m/t/p in any order, ASCII decimal without sign/leading zero, no unknown/duplicate parameter, canonical unpadded PHC base64, and no whitespace/trailing byte. It rejects argon2d, argon2i, missing/other version, padded/noncanonical base64, or decoded mismatch before hashing. Text cap 4096 bytes is checked before scanning. Decoded salt is 8..64 bytes; output 16..64 bytes. m is 8,192..262,144 KiB, t 1..10, p 1..8, m >= 8*p, and checked m*t <= 1,048,576 KiB-rounds. Decimal overflow, product overflow, or any cap violation returns PasswordPolicy before large allocation. Parser stores validated numeric fields and decoded lengths in PasswordHash; verification never reparses unchecked text. Verification and oracle. `password_verify` uses the parsed record's algorithm/version/parameters, constant-time compares the complete derived output, and is operationally fallible: its API1-compatible shape is `Bool ? CryptoError`. Only a completed password mismatch returns `ok(false)`; success returns `ok(true)`. Unsupported resource/platform, admission/allocation failure, or backend failure returns its mapped error, never false. Malformed, unsupported, or over-cap input cannot inhabit PasswordHash. Cancellation is D-TASKRUNTIME1 control flow, not false or CryptoError. No error includes password, salt/hash bytes, PHC text, backend text, or which comparison byte failed. Applications should project unknown user, malformed stored record, mismatch, and operational failure through one externally chosen login response. This ballot does not create a public dummy-hash helper; any such helper and its exact signature belong to D-CRYPTO-API1 and cannot be assumed before that ballot ratifies it. Resource and cancellation law. Argon2 runs on the runtime's blocking CPU pool, never an async/event-loop worker and never while holding a Jet global/scheduler lock. Admission weight is conservative total resident memory, not Argon's block count alone. Before admission compute in checked integers and round up to 1,024 KiB: `m + ceil(m/8) + 2048 + ceil(password_bytes/1024) + 1` KiB. The terms are respectively Argon's exact block allocation, the bridge's maximum auxiliary scratch, fixed allocator/thread/backend overhead, the already-owned password storage charged again conservatively, and salt/output/PHC scratch. The audited bridge must own exactly one m-KiB block arena plus at most `ceil(m/8)+2048` KiB auxiliary memory; it may not hide another arena, spawn per-lane arenas outside m, or borrow caller buffers after return. The default process budget is 311,296 KiB (304 MiB): A at the maximum 1,048,576-byte password weighs 77,824 KiB, so exactly four fit; B weighs 299,008 KiB, so exactly one fits. A job reserves full weight before allocation and releases only after every secret/intermediate buffer is zeroized. FIFO waiters are cancellation-aware. Before admission, cancellation removes the waiter with no allocation. After admission, Jet checks cancellation at each implementation-proved Argon2 pass/slice boundary; if the audited backend cannot stop at such a boundary, it completes the derivation, constant-time discards the result, zeroizes all state, releases budget, then propagates the ordinary task-cancelled outcome. It never returns true, false, PHC, or CryptoError after observed cancellation. The 311,296 KiB budget is fixed in A/B/C; there is no environment, runtime mutation, or expert budget override. No public admission, dummy, budget, or policy helper is created by A/B. C's exact calibration/policy surface is the sole conditional helper set and remains wholly gated on API1. The budget never lowers m/t/p, rewrites a PHC, or turns failure into mismatch. A request whose weight exceeds configured budget returns ResourceUnavailable before allocation. OS allocation/backend resource failure returns ResourceUnavailable for both hash and verify. Unsupported 32-bit/freestanding/comptime/interpreter targets return ResourceUnavailable before secret work; native AOT/JIT share one implementation. Audit may record algorithm/version/m/t/p, conservative weight, wait/duration, success/mismatch/error/cancelled, never password/salt/hash/PHC. Rehash is option-scoped and pure. Under A, `needs_rehash()` is true when salt<16, output<32, m<65536, t<3, or p!=1. Under B it is true when salt<16, output<32, m<262144, t<2, or p!=1. A/B return false for records at or above both selected m/t baselines with salt/output at or above baseline and p=1; Jet never silently downgrades a stronger accepted record. Under C, calibration produces an immutable persisted `PasswordPolicy`; the only honest query is `needs_rehash(current: PasswordPolicy)`, and C cannot borrow A's thresholds or expose zero-argument needs_rehash. C is conditional on API1 ratifying exactly `PasswordPolicy.calibrate() -> PasswordPolicy ? CryptoError`, `PasswordPolicy.parse(text: String) -> PasswordPolicy ? CryptoError`, `.text() -> String`, and `password_hash_with_policy(password: &Secret, policy: PasswordPolicy) -> PasswordHash ? CryptoError`. Canonical policy text is `argon2id-policy/v1;m=;t=;p=1;salt=16;out=32`; applications persist this deployment identity beside configuration. `PasswordPolicy.parse` first rejects text longer than 128 UTF-8 bytes before scanning, then accepts only ASCII bytes in the exact field order and spelling `argon2id-policy/v1;m=;t=;p=1;salt=16;out=32`. There is no whitespace, sign, leading zero, duplicate, unknown, omitted, reordered, empty, or trailing field; m must be exactly 65536, 131072, or 262144 and t exactly decimal 3..10. Non-UTF-8/non-ASCII, malformed decimal, duplicate/reordered/unknown fields, leading zero, whitespace, and trailing bytes map InvalidEncoding; a syntactically exact `argon2id-policy/` prefix maps UnsupportedVersion; canonical syntax with m/t/p/salt/out outside the candidate set maps PasswordPolicy. Parsing never benchmarks, allocates Argon memory, accepts a forged host identity, or widens hard PHC caps. `.text()` emits only this canonical form. Calibration uses fixed public 32-byte password and 16-byte salt, p=1, candidates m in [65536,131072,262144] and t in 3..10. In an otherwise idle single blocking worker it runs two discarded warmups then seven measured hashes per candidate using monotonic time. Eligible median is <=750 ms; choose greatest m, then greatest t, then lower median. If none qualifies, select A's floor m=65536,t=3—never weaker. Missing monotonic clock, any sample failure, or `(max-min) > median/4` for the chosen candidate returns ResourceUnavailable and emits no policy. Calibration is explicit, never automatic at startup or login. Moving hosts keeps the persisted policy and rehash baseline; an operator explicitly recalibrates and atomically replaces deployment policy. needs_rehash compares against the supplied persisted policy; a newly calibrated weaker policy never marks a stronger stored m/t for downgrade. A future algorithm/version replacement must first ballot its acceptance window and ordering. Rehash happens only after `password_verify` returns ok(true), generates a fresh RNG1 salt, returns a new PHC, and never mutates stored data itself. Failure/cancellation leaves the old verified record intact; callers choose transactional persistence. There is no automatic background rewrite. Expert policy. `core.crypto.expert.argon2id` remains inside lexical #Unsafe and may choose m/t/p, 8..64-byte explicit salt, and 16..64-byte output only inside the same hard parser caps and admission budget. A/B expose no `expert.password_hash(policy)` helper. If C and API1 ratify the exact PasswordPolicy surface above, `password_hash_with_policy` generates a fresh salt and returns canonical PHC; deterministic explicit salts are for protocol/import/vector work, never a safe optional argument. #Unsafe does not bypass allocation checks, zeroization, cancellation, PHC canonicality, or the process budget. Safe writer exposes no knobs, environment override, host calibration, benchmark-derived downgrade, pepper, deterministic salt, or algorithm selector. Pepper/keyed hashing needs a separate secret-storage/API decision. Compatibility. Existing arbitrary String password inputs migrate to consumed Secret; `password_hash_with_salt` moves to expert #Unsafe. Existing Argon2id v19 PHCs inside accepted caps continue verifying. Current writer outputs outside the exact default remain readable and `needs_rehash` reports by the law above. Argon2i/d, bcrypt, scrypt, PBKDF2, and unknown PHC ids are not guessed or auto-migrated; applications import them only after a separate algorithm ballot. No alias survives the major-edition migration. Exact errors. Both password_hash and password_verify reject password Secret length above 1,048,576 bytes as PasswordPolicy before admission or backend entry. PasswordHash.parse maps PHC shape, whitespace, decimal syntax, base64 syntax/canonicality, and decoded-length failure to InvalidEncoding; argon2d/argon2i/unknown id to UnsupportedAlgorithm; missing or non-19 version to UnsupportedVersion; syntactically valid numeric values outside m/t/p/product/input/text policy to PasswordPolicy. password_hash maps RNG1 failure to EntropyUnavailable, admission impossibility/unsupported platform/allocation resource failure to ResourceUnavailable, and audited backend invariant failure to Internal. password_verify returns `Bool ? CryptoError`: completed mismatch is ok(false); admission/platform/allocation resource failure is ResourceUnavailable; backend invariant is Internal. Cancellation remains task control flow after finish-discard/checkpoint zeroization, never an error or false. D-CRYPTO-API1 must ratify these categories, fallible verify, PasswordHash/Secret types, and any public policy/calibration/dummy/admission helper before this policy ships. CLI import/rehash tooling additionally waits on D-CRYPTO-DIAG1 exact copy/exits/no-artifact law. Acceptance. Pin Argon2 RFC 9106 and PHC known-answer vectors for exact default and every accepted boundary; deterministic expert vectors prove salt/output. Hostile tests cover 4097-byte text, decimal/product overflow, duplicate/unknown/missing params, every algorithm/version, base64 padding/noncanonical bits, salt/output/m/t/p bounds, m<8p, huge claims before allocation, wrong password, empty/max password, rehash partial order, fresh salts, RNG failure, admission FIFO, cancellation before admission and at every pass/slice/finish-discard boundary, exact weight arithmetic/overflow, 77,824/299,008 KiB weights, four A jobs/one B job under 311,296 KiB, backend arena/scratch ownership ceiling, budget exhaustion, allocation/resource/backend error mapping, zeroization, no secret diagnostics/audit, AOT/JIT parity, and unsupported targets. Parser fuzzing has fixed byte/step/allocation budgets. PasswordPolicy fixtures cover exact 128/129-byte preflight, every field omission/duplication/reorder/unknown, leading zeros/signs/overflow, ASCII and UTF-8 whitespace, trailing bytes, version changes, every allowed m/t pair, forged m/t/p/salt/out values, canonical text round trip, and proof that parse performs no calibration or Argon allocation. Timing tests are regression signals, never constant-time proof. Beginner pass: hash, store one string, verify; no costs or salts. Expert pass: exact version, m/t/p, salt/output, caps, admission, audit, import, and rehash are explicit. Hybrid pass: safe and expert calls share one parser, Argon2 engine, limits, zeroization, scheduler, vectors, and PasswordHash value.

options.name: Balanced fixed default with bounded verification
options.detail: Recommended. Write m=65536 KiB, t=3, p=1, 16-byte salt, 32-byte output; accept only bounded Argon2id v19 PHCs and expose pure needs_rehash. This is predictable across supported hosts, memory-hard, server-safe under weighted admission, and upgradeable without beginner tuning.
options.code:
stored :: crypto.password_hash(&password)?
// $argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=3,p=1$...$...
parsed :: crypto.PasswordHash.parse(stored.text())?
assert(!parsed.needs_rehash())
assert(crypto.password_verify(&password, parsed)?)

options.name: Memory-first fixed default
options.detail: Write m=262144 KiB, t=2, p=1 with the same grammar, caps, errors, and expert controls. Fresh output establishes B's own rehash baseline: salt 16, output 32, m 262144, t 2, p 1; needs_rehash never borrows A's thresholds. At the maximum password its conservative 299008 KiB weight permits one active B job under the 311296 KiB (304 MiB) default budget.

options.name: Host-calibrated writer
options.detail: Explicitly calibrate the exact bounded candidate matrix and persist canonical PasswordPolicy identity; fresh output plus that policy establishes C's rehash baseline, and callers pass current policy to needs_rehash. Calibration and policy APIs are unavailable unless D-CRYPTO-API1 ratifies the exact signatures in this ballot. This adapts to a deployment but makes policy rollout an operator-controlled configuration migration rather than a Jet-release constant.
options.code:
policy :: crypto.PasswordPolicy.calibrate()?
config.write_atomic("password-policy", policy.text())?
stored :: crypto.password_hash_with_policy(&password, policy)?
// Host moves keep this policy until explicit recalibration.

comparisons.note: OWASP recommends Argon2id with a minimum memory/time tradeoff and periodic upgrades. A exceeds the common floor while pinning a stable fleet policy and explicit rehash signal.
PHP stores algorithm, cost, salt, and hash together and exposes password_needs_rehash. A keeps that upgrade loop but rejects hostile stored costs before allocation.
libsodium offers interactive/moderate/sensitive fixed profiles. A chooses one beginner profile and moves bounded deviations behind Jet's audited expert gate.

decisions.title: Exact safe and expert core.crypto API
decisions.gist: Choose the exact typed value API that makes common cryptography hard to misuse while preserving complete raw-algorithm control under #Unsafe.
decisions.explainer: Inherited law and batch status. D-CRYPTO-SUITE1=A, D-PWHASH1=A, D-RANDSPLIT1, and D-DEP-CRYPTO1=A are live ratified law. D-DEP-CRYPTO-SUITE2, D-CRYPTO-RNG1, D-PWHASH-POLICY1, D-CRYPTO-ENVELOPE2, D-CRYPTO-VAULT1, D-CRYPTO-KEYWRAP1, and D-CRYPTO-DIAG1 are companion decisions proposed in this batch; each grants nothing until independently ratified. This ballot owns in-memory value seal/open plus standalone wrapped-secret bytes. ENVELOPE2 is file-only: paths, streaming, atomic publication, file format, and v1 file migration. VAULT1 is the latest compatibility-required owner of persistent SigningKey/X25519SecretKey storage, including only internal store atomic backup/recovery, and VaultError; it never owns portable key backup. API1 cannot ship persistent key calls until its selected types/signatures are compatible. KEYWRAP1 is the sole owner of portable vault-key export/import. DIAG1 owns projections. This ballot adds no dependency, vault mutation API, file API, password cost, entropy provider, or diagnostic code.
decisions.story: Mina encrypts a tenant record for a recipient, verifies passwords, signs releases, and derives a session key. Today keys, signatures, envelopes, hashes, and passwords are interchangeable strings or byte lists. She needs purpose-bound values that cannot be printed or swapped, one recoverable error family, and explicit raw interoperability without this ballot inventing a storage vault or file-stream lifecycle.
decisions.inWild:
use core.crypto as crypto

recipient :: crypto.X25519SecretKey.generate()?
box :: crypto.seal([recipient.public_key()], record, aad: tenant.bytes())?
plain :: crypto.open(&recipient, box, aad: tenant.bytes())?

password :: crypto.Secret.from_text(take(input))
stored :: crypto.password_hash(&password)?
if crypto.password_verify(&password, stored)? { login() }

signing :: crypto.SigningKey.generate()?
sig :: crypto.sign(&signing, release_bytes)
print(crypto.verify(signing.public_key(), release_bytes, sig)?)
decisions.detail:
Option A exact law follows.

Home and types. Safe names live only in `core.crypto`; raw algorithms live only in `core.crypto.expert`; CSPRNG stays `core.crypto.random`. Public nominal types are `Secret`, `SigningKey`, `VerifyKey`, `X25519SecretKey`, `X25519PublicKey`, `SharedSecret`, `Signature`, `Sealed`, `WrappedKey`, `PasswordHash`, `Digest256`, and `Digest512`. Secret, SigningKey, X25519SecretKey, and SharedSecret are move-only; zeroize on drop; cannot clone, compare, hash, serialize, reflect fields, Debug, or Display; diagnostics show only `<secret Type>`. `Secret.from_text(take text)` and `Secret.from_bytes(take bytes)` consume the owned source and clear its storage. No safe raw-secret export exists. Public types clone and serialize only through named canonical methods. No implicit String/[U8] conversions exist.

API error scope. CryptoError is closed and used only by core.crypto value, key, digest, KDF, password, and expert functions in this ballot: InvalidLength {operation,parameter,expected,actual}, InvalidEncoding {operation,value_kind}, UnsupportedVersion {operation,version}, UnsupportedAlgorithm {operation,algorithm}, OpenFailed, NonContributoryKey, OutputLength {operation,minimum,maximum,actual}, PasswordPolicy {reason}, EntropyUnavailable, ResourceUnavailable {resource}, Internal {incident_id}. It contains no backend/OS/secret material. File APIs use companion FileCryptoError owned by ENVELOPE2; persistent vault APIs use VaultError owned by VAULT1. They may project through DIAG1 to common terminal categories but are not aliases/variants of CryptoError. Cancellation is task control flow. Only CryptoError appears in signatures below.

Locked implementation gate. No safe seal/open/wrap/unwrap or Ed25519 sign/verify ships until D-DEP-CRYPTO-SUITE2 ratifies its revised exact lock: chacha20poly1305 0.10.1 (defaults off; alloc) and ed25519-dalek 2.2.0 (defaults off; alloc,zeroize), their complete 55-package transitive graph, Cargo.lock checksums/licenses/features, fresh RustSec report, target slices, and Epoch-3 deletion rows, or native replacement proof. The prior 37-package draft is insufficient.

Exact value-envelope signatures and bytes. X25519SecretKey.generate() -> X25519SecretKey ? CryptoError; .public_key() -> X25519PublicKey. X25519PublicKey.from_bytes(exactly32) and .bytes(); public text encoding is lowercase Bech32m HRP jetx25519. seal(recipients:[X25519PublicKey],plaintext:[U8],aad:[U8]=[]) -> Sealed ? CryptoError; open(recipient:&X25519SecretKey,envelope:Sealed,aad:[U8]=[]) -> [U8] ? CryptoError. Limits: recipients 1..256 unique, plaintext <=16,777,216, AAD <=16,777,216. Safe callers never provide nonce/algorithm.

Sealed canonical JETV/v1 bytes are: magic JETV[4], version u8=1, suite u8=1, flags u16=0, recipient_count u16, ephemeral_public[32], salt[16], payload_nonce[24], then sorted recipient stanzas, payload_len u32, ciphertext[payload_len], tag[16]. Each stanza is recipient_public[32], wrapped_file_key[48]. Sort lexicographically by public bytes; duplicates reject. Writer draws independent ephemeral X25519 secret, salt, payload nonce, and 32-byte file key from RNG1. shared=X25519(ephemeral,recipient), all-zero rejected; KEK=HKDF-SHA256(shared,salt, ASCII JETV1 wrap || ephemeral_public || recipient_public), 32 bytes; wrap_nonce=first24(HKDF-SHA256(shared,salt, ASCII JETV1 nonce || ephemeral_public || recipient_public)); wrapped key is XChaCha20-Poly1305(file_key) with AAD ASCII JETV1 stanza || serialized fixed header || recipient_public. Payload is XChaCha20-Poly1305(plaintext) under file_key/payload_nonce with AAD ASCII JETV1 payload || complete header+stanzas || caller AAD. Header changes, recipient changes, wrong/missing AAD, wrong recipient, unwrap/tag/tamper all return OpenFailed. Recipient identities and exact lengths are visible; AAD is not stored. JETV numeric parser law: fixed header is exactly 82 bytes; each stanza exactly 80; recipient_count 1..256; payload_len 0..16777216; total bytes exactly 82 + 80*recipient_count + 4 + payload_len + 16 and at most 16797798. All additions/multiplications use checked unsigned arithmetic before allocation. Stanzas must be strictly increasing by public-key bytes, so duplicate or out-of-order input rejects. Sealed.from_bytes checks cap, magic/version/suite/flags/count, lengths, order, checked arithmetic, and exact consumption with no trailing byte; it returns public InvalidLength/InvalidEncoding/UnsupportedVersion/UnsupportedAlgorithm and does not authenticate. This public parse distinction is intentional and observable. Only after successful Sealed construction does open begin recipient/secret work; from that boundary every no-match, all-zero, unwrap, wrong AAD/key, or tag cause collapses to OpenFailed. .bytes returns canonical bytes. Secrets/intermediates zeroize; no partial plaintext escapes. ENVELOPE2 cannot redefine JETV.

WrappedKey is also owned here, not by file ENVELOPE2. wrap(secret:&Secret,recipient:X25519PublicKey) -> WrappedKey ? CryptoError; unwrap(recipient:&X25519SecretKey,wrapped:WrappedKey) -> Secret ? CryptoError. Secret length is 0..1,048,576. Canonical JETW/v1 bytes: magic JETW[4], version1, suite1, flags u16=0, recipient_public[32], ephemeral_public[32], salt[16], ciphertext_len u32, ciphertext, tag[16]. Fresh ephemeral secret and salt; KEK/24-byte nonce derive by HKDF-SHA256 with domains JETW1 key/JETW1 nonce and both public keys; XChaCha AAD is ASCII JETW1 wrap plus serialized header. Wrong recipient/all-zero/unwrap/tag/tamper collapses OpenFailed. JETW numeric parser law: fixed header through ciphertext_len is exactly 92 bytes; ciphertext_len 0..1048576; total bytes exactly 92 + ciphertext_len + 16 and at most 1048684. Checked unsigned arithmetic precedes allocation; flags/reserved must be zero; exact consumption forbids trailing bytes. WrappedKey.from_bytes exposes public InvalidLength/InvalidEncoding/UnsupportedVersion/UnsupportedAlgorithm only for this framing. After successful construction, unwrap collapses recipient mismatch, all-zero agreement, wrong key, or tag failure to OpenFailed. This is portable one-recipient process-memory Secret wrapping only. VAULT1 exclusively owns persistent SigningKey/X25519SecretKey storage, including only internal store atomic backup/recovery, and never portable key backup. KEYWRAP1 exclusively owns portable export/import of those vault key rows and must use its distinct WrappedVaultKey/JVKW format; neither VAULT1 nor KEYWRAP1 may reuse or reinterpret JETW.

`SigningKey.generate() -> SigningKey ? CryptoError`; `.public_key() -> VerifyKey`. `VerifyKey.from_bytes(bytes:[U8] exactly32) -> VerifyKey ? CryptoError`; `.bytes() -> [U8]`. `Signature.from_bytes(bytes:[U8] exactly64) -> Signature ? CryptoError`; `.bytes() -> [U8]`. `sign(key:&SigningKey,message:[U8] <=1073741824) -> Signature`; `verify(key:VerifyKey,message:[U8] <=1073741824,signature:Signature) -> Bool ? CryptoError`. Verify uses strict RFC 8032; canonical mismatch is ok(false), operational/internal failure is err.

`x25519(secret:&X25519SecretKey,public:X25519PublicKey) -> SharedSecret ? CryptoError`; it clamps per RFC 7748 and constant-time rejects an all-zero result as NonContributoryKey. `hkdf_sha256(ikm:&Secret,salt:[U8]=[],info:[U8]=[],length:Int) -> Secret ? CryptoError`, length exactly 0..8160 inclusive; no partial output. `sha256(data:[U8]) -> Digest256`, `blake3(data:[U8]) -> Digest256`, `sha512(data:[U8]) -> Digest512`; digest `.bytes()` and lowercase `.hex()`. `constant_time_equal(a:&Secret,b:&Secret) -> Bool` folds length difference without early length return.

`PasswordHash.parse(text:String) -> PasswordHash ? CryptoError`; `.text() -> String`. Under D-PWHASH-POLICY1=A or B, `PasswordHash.needs_rehash() -> Bool` uses that option's fixed total ordering. Under D-PWHASH-POLICY1=C, and only under C, API1 ratifies exactly: `PasswordPolicy.calibrate() -> PasswordPolicy ? CryptoError`; `PasswordPolicy.parse(text:String) -> PasswordPolicy ? CryptoError`; `PasswordPolicy.text() -> String`; `password_hash_with_policy(password:&Secret,policy:PasswordPolicy) -> PasswordHash ? CryptoError`; and `PasswordHash.needs_rehash(current:PasswordPolicy) -> Bool`. C has no zero-argument needs_rehash; A/B expose no PasswordPolicy, calibrate, or password_hash_with_policy. `password_hash(password:&Secret) -> PasswordHash ? CryptoError` exists under A/B only; `password_verify(password:&Secret,stored:PasswordHash) -> Bool ? CryptoError` exists under every option. Only completed constant-time mismatch is ok(false); ResourceUnavailable/Internal is err and cancellation is task control. Exact PHC grammar, m/t/p/salt/output values, accepted caps, admission, dummy-hash helper, and rehash ordering are wholly D-PWHASH-POLICY1 and not chosen here.

Persistence companion boundary. API1 defines only process-memory SigningKey and X25519SecretKey. D-CRYPTO-VAULT1 is the latest compatibility-required companion decision and sole owner of persistent typed-key storage, Secret effect, KeyRef<T>, authority, rotation/revocation, atomicity, internal store atomic backup/recovery and VaultError; it never owns portable key backup; it supports SigningKey and X25519SecretKey and no SealKey exists. API1 invents no vault path or method. Until VAULT1 ratifies compatibly, private keys are process-memory only. JETW wraps Secret values only and does not imply safe SigningKey/X25519SecretKey import/export. D-CRYPTO-KEYWRAP1 is the sole companion decision owner of portable vault-key export/import; it must remain type- and byte-distinct from JETW.

Exact expert surface. Every call requires lexical `#Unsafe("reason")`: `xchacha20poly1305_seal(key:[U8] exactly32,nonce:[U8] exactly24,plaintext:[U8] <=1073741824,aad:[U8] <=16777216) -> [U8] ? CryptoError`; matching open takes ciphertext 16..1073741840 and returns `[U8] ? CryptoError`. `aes256gcm_seal/open` are identical except nonce exactly12. `ed25519_sign(seed:[U8] exactly32,message:[U8] <=1073741824) -> Signature ? CryptoError`; `ed25519_verify_strict(public:[U8] exactly32,message:[U8] <=1073741824,signature:[U8] exactly64) -> Bool ? CryptoError`. `x25519(secret:[U8] exactly32,public:[U8] exactly32,reject_all_zero:Bool=true) -> Secret ? CryptoError`. `hkdf_sha256(ikm:[U8],salt:[U8],info:[U8],length:Int 0..8160) -> Secret ? CryptoError`. `argon2id(password:&Secret,salt:[U8] 8..64,memory_kib:Int,iterations:Int,lanes:Int,output_length:Int 16..64) -> Secret ? CryptoError`, additionally blocked on D-PWHASH-POLICY1's numeric caps. Four separately named functions—`secret_bytes(secret:&Secret) -> [U8]`, `signing_key_bytes(key:&SigningKey) -> [U8]`, `x25519_secret_bytes(key:&X25519SecretKey) -> [U8]`, and `shared_secret_bytes(secret:&SharedSecret) -> [U8]`—are the sole raw secret exposures; each returns a caller-owned audited copy. Every expert result uses the same CryptoError; #Unsafe never bypasses allocation bounds, canonical Ed25519, memory safety, or cleanup.

Testing and compatibility. Release safe APIs have no seed, nonce, salt, provider callback, environment override, or deterministic mode. Provider injection exists only under cfg(test), is unreachable from Jet source, and is absent from release artifacts. Fixed vectors use expert raw inputs inside named #Unsafe test regions. Current byte/String APIs and `? String` errors migrate only in a major-version/edition change with targeted diagnostics and no permanent aliases. Old editions retain no predictable RNG fallback. File and v1 source migration is not claimed here and follows ENVELOPE2 only. Acceptance rejects secret Display/Debug/clone/serialize/reflection, wrong nominal roles, raw safe nonces, expert calls outside #Unsafe, wrong lengths/bounds, nonfallible password verification, and release deterministic seams; proves RFC vectors, strict Ed25519 invalids, X25519 all-zero, HKDF boundaries, password mismatch versus operational failure, zeroization, error consistency, and AOT/JIT parity. Beginner pass: generate recipient/signing keys and call seal/open/sign/verify/password APIs without algorithm or nonce knowledge. Expert pass: exact algorithms, raw encodings, AAD, nonces, KDF/cost bounds, exposure, audit, and companion gates are explicit. Hybrid pass: safe and expert entrypoints share checked primitives, CryptoError, vectors, and audit; no second hidden crypto system.

options.name: Purpose-bound nominal types plus gated raw primitives
options.detail: Recommended. Use exactly the nominal types, free functions, CryptoError, JETV/JETW byte laws, expert functions, and companion gates above. Wrong-role keys are compile-time errors; safe entropy/nonces are internal. Persistent key storage stays blocked on VAULT1; file/v1 behavior stays with file-only ENVELOPE2; API1 itself owns value wrapping bytes.
options.code:
recipient :: crypto.X25519SecretKey.generate()?
box :: crypto.seal([recipient.public_key()], data, aad: tenant.bytes())?
plain :: crypto.open(&recipient, box, aad: tenant.bytes())?
password :: crypto.Secret.from_text(take(input))
stored :: crypto.password_hash(&password)?
valid :: crypto.password_verify(&password, stored)?

options.name: Compiler-sealed tagged key family
options.detail: Complete alternative. Replace SigningKey/VerifyKey/X25519SecretKey/X25519PublicKey with compiler-sealed `Key<Ed25519Sign>`, `Key<Ed25519Verify>`, `Key<X25519Secret>`, and `Key<X25519Public>`. Secret, SharedSecret, Signature, Sealed, WrappedKey, PasswordHash, Digest256/512, CryptoError, JETV/JETW, all bounds, free/expert functions, file boundary, compatibility and acceptance are exactly A. Exact mapping: generate/public_key/from_bytes/bytes/text are methods on matching Key<Tag>; seal/open/sign/verify/x25519 substitute those tags. VAULT1 currently admits only concrete SigningKey/X25519SecretKey, so B blocks persistence until VAULT1 is amended to map Ed25519Sign->SigningKey storage record and X25519Secret->X25519SecretKey record without serializing/retagging tags; no other tag is storable. Wrong tags remain compile-time mismatches.
options.code:
recipient :: crypto.Key<crypto.X25519Secret>.generate()?
public :: crypto.Key<crypto.X25519Public> :: recipient.public_key()
box :: crypto.seal([public], data, aad: aad)?
plain :: crypto.open(&recipient, box, aad: aad)?
signing :: crypto.Key<crypto.Ed25519Sign>.generate()?
sig :: crypto.sign(&signing, data)
valid :: crypto.verify(signing.public_key(), data, sig)?

options.name: Free canonical functions plus non-owning bound views
options.detail: Complete alternative. Keep all Option A types, canonical free functions, CryptoError, JETV/JETW, bounds, gates, expert surface and acceptance. Add compiler-known closure-scoped views only: `with_recipient(key:&X25519SecretKey, body:fn(&RecipientView)->R)->R` and `with_signer(key:&SigningKey, body:fn(&SignerView)->R)->R`. Views borrow for the callback invocation, cannot be returned, stored, captured by an escaping closure, serialized, cloned, or constructed directly; existing v1 no-stored/no-returned-reference law enforces escape rejection with no lifetime syntax. Sealed traits are `RecipientOps` and `SignerOps`; only the matching view implements one. RecipientView exposes exactly `public_key() -> X25519PublicKey` and `open(envelope:Sealed,aad:[U8]=[]) -> [U8] ? CryptoError`, with open using its borrowed secret key. It has no seal method: canonical free `seal(recipients:[X25519PublicKey],plaintext:[U8],aad:[U8]=[]) -> Sealed ? CryptoError` needs no secret binding and remains the only seal surface. SignerView exposes exactly `public_key() -> VerifyKey` and `sign(message:[U8]) -> Signature`. Views add grouping and repeated-use ergonomics but no state, nonce counter, format, backend, or alternative semantics; canonical free calls remain available.

comparisons.note: Sodium informs the high-level operations and collapsed open failure; Jet adds purpose-bound types and lexical expert gating.
Age informs recipient-oriented envelopes, but ENVELOPE2—not this API ballot—owns the serialized file format, streaming, publication, and file migration law.
RustCrypto supplies primitive-shaped expert interoperability; Jet safe calls own composition and typed errors.

decisions.title: Recipient and streaming file envelope
decisions.gist: Choose the authenticated recipient format Jet writes for large files, including its version, algorithms, limits, and migration law.
decisions.explainer: Scope and inherited law. D-CRYPTO-SUITE1=A requires misuse-resistant seal/open, file envelopes, algorithm agility, and expert primitives. D-RANDSPLIT1 keeps deterministic randomness outside crypto. Proposed D-CRYPTO-RNG1 owns fresh OS entropy and RandomError; this envelope cannot write until RNG1 ratifies a compatible fallible provider. D-DEP-CRYPTO1=A already approves the RustCrypto `chacha20poly1305` family used here, including XChaCha in principle; it does not pin the final exact version/features or separately approve HKDF-SHA256 and X25519 additions. Proposed D-DEP-CRYPTO-SUITE2 is a compatibility/exact-graph gate only: it records precise versions, features, transitive graph, audit, and native-replacement obligation without reopening the approved chacha20poly1305 family. This ballot owns the serialized envelope, recipient wrapping, streaming and migration behavior. Current D-CRYPTO-API1 cleanly owns value-only JETV/JETW and general Secret/key/CryptoError types; it already defers every file path, streaming, JETC, and v1 behavior to this ballot. ENVELOPE2 adds only the X25519PublicKey path API and FileCryptoError below, with no Recipient/FileSealed type. A's exact path API is `file_seal(recipients: [X25519PublicKey], source: Path, destination: Path) -> () ? FileCryptoError` and `file_open(identity: &X25519SecretKey, source: Path, destination: Path) -> () ? FileCryptoError`; `FileCryptoError` is exactly `OpenFailed`, `SealFailed(CryptoError)`, `SourceIo`, `DestinationExists`, or `DestinationIo`, with operation and redacted path but no OS/backend text. Safe calls accept no raw key, nonce, algorithm, metadata, stream, or overwrite flag; an existing destination is DestinationExists and is never overwritten. `core.crypto.expert.open_v1(key: [U8], envelope: [U8]) -> [U8] ? OpenFailed` and `core.crypto.expert.migrate_v1(key: [U8], source: Path, recipients: [X25519PublicKey], destination: Path) -> () ? FileCryptoError` remain lexical #Unsafe. OpenFailed has no public payload. Proposed D-CRYPTO-DIAG1 must ratify CLI copy, exits, cleanup, and audit projection before any infallible tool command ships. No option here approves a crate.
decisions.story: Mara encrypts a 40 GiB database backup for two teammates and an offline recovery key. She writes one complete envelope atomically to a local backup path, uploads only that completed file, and opens it on another supported host. A changed byte, removed final chunk, wrong recipient, old-format downgrade, or failed entropy call must produce no plaintext artifact and no clue about which secret was almost right.
decisions.detail:
Option A exact law follows.

Format identity and integers. The only writer magic is ASCII `JETC`; version is byte 0x02. Every multibyte integer is unsigned little-endian. The fixed prefix is: magic[4], version u8, kind u8 (1=file only), suite u8 (1 only), flags u8 (0 only), header_len u32, and body_len u64. Unknown version, kind, suite, flags, reserved value, noncanonical order, or trailing byte is rejected; writers never emit an unknown field. `header_len` counts the complete variable header. `body_len` is ciphertext-body bytes, not plaintext bytes. `file_seal` v2 accepts only a no-follow-opened regular file. Before generating any envelope secret or header, Jet creates a private staged snapshot: POSIX uses a mode-0600 create-new file in the destination filesystem, keeps its exclusive descriptor, and unlinks its name immediately; Windows uses a same-volume create-new temporary with owner-only DACL, no sharing, and delete-on-close. Jet copies the source through the held source handle into that stage while computing SHA-256 and byte length, fsyncs/FlushFileBuffers the stage, rewinds and hashes every staged byte again, then reopens the no-follow source and requires identical device/inode-or-file-id, length, modification identity, EOF, and full SHA-256 on a second complete read. Any mismatch, source read error, cancellation, or stage hash mismatch returns SourceIo, zeroizes buffers, and destroys the owned stage before RNG1 or output creation. Seal then reads only the immutable held staged handle, computes exact body_len with checked arithmetic from its verified length, rechecks staged identity/hash/EOF before FINAL, and destroys the stage after completion. Later source mutation cannot change emitted plaintext. Pipes, sockets, devices, and unknown-length readers are unsupported by v2 rather than backpatched or buffered; a future unknown-length stream requires a separately versioned authenticated-length or trailer law. Header plus body must consume the staged snapshot exactly. No native struct layout, varint, JSON, CBOR, text normalization, or platform endian enters the wire format.

Suite 1. Recipient key agreement is X25519. KDF is HKDF-SHA256. Recipient-key wrapping and payload encryption are XChaCha20-Poly1305 with 16-byte tags. SHA-256 is used only for commits/identifiers, never as encryption. Safe writers have no algorithm parameter and always emit suite 1. AES-256-GCM is read-only legacy-v1 migration under the existing `core.crypto.expert` plus `#Unsafe` gate; it is never a v2 suite, automatic fallback, platform optimization, or FIPS claim. Adding, replacing, or preferring a suite requires a new version/suite ballot and known-answer/interoperability vectors before a writer changes.

Variable header, exact order. Header bytes are: file_id[16], ephemeral_x25519_public[32], payload_nonce_prefix[16], chunk_size u32, recipient_count u16, metadata_len u32, then exactly recipient_count stanzas, then metadata bytes, then header_tag[16]. `file_id`, a 32-byte file_key, the ephemeral X25519 secret, and the 16-byte payload nonce prefix are four independent fresh D-CRYPTO-RNG1 requests; none is derived from another. Any request failure returns SealFailed(EntropyUnavailable), non-elidably zeroizes every value already obtained plus all partial header/body buffers, removes only the owned temporary file, and publishes nothing. `chunk_size` is exactly 1,048,576. `recipient_count` is 1..256. The writer rejects duplicate public keys and sorts stanzas lexicographically by the 16-byte recipient id, then full public key, so one logical recipient set has one encoding. The ephemeral secret, shared secrets, KEKs, and file key are non-elidably zeroized after their last use and never serialized. All-zero X25519 input/shared output is rejected.

Recipient stanza. Each stanza is exactly recipient_id[16], recipient_public[32], wrapped_key[48]. recipient_id is the first 16 bytes of SHA-256 over ASCII `JETC2 recipient id` followed by the raw 32-byte X25519 public key. Including the full public key makes collisions unambiguous and recipient identity intentionally visible; this version does not promise anonymous recipients. Sender computes shared=X25519(ephemeral_secret, recipient_public), then KEK=HKDF-SHA256(shared, salt=file_id, info=ASCII `JETC2 wrap key` || ephemeral_public || recipient_public), 32 bytes. Wrap nonce is HKDF-SHA256(shared, salt=file_id, info=ASCII `JETC2 wrap nonce` || ephemeral_public || recipient_public), first 24 bytes. wrapped_key is XChaCha20-Poly1305(file_key[32]) with AAD `JETC2 wrap aad` || fixed_prefix || file_id || ephemeral_public || payload_nonce_prefix || chunk_size || recipient_count || metadata_len || recipient_id || recipient_public. Each derived KEK/nonce is unique to the fresh ephemeral secret, file_id, and distinct recipient; a writer never reuses them. Open computes only stanzas whose full public key matches the key's derived public key, performs constant-time tag verification, and still reports the collapsed failure below.

Metadata. V2 initially requires metadata_len=0 for both writers and readers. Any nonzero metadata_len returns OpenFailed before body allocation. No filename, path, owner, permissions, timestamps, host, user, MIME, comments, or source length is inferred or stored. A future metadata surface requires a separate owner ballot pinning its exact #Unsafe construction API, canonical bytes, visibility, caps, parser, diagnostics, and compatibility law before this reserved field may become nonzero; this ballot approves no expert metadata path.

Header authentication. `header_tag` authenticates the entire fixed prefix and variable header before header_tag under the 32-byte file key using XChaCha20-Poly1305 over empty plaintext. Its nonce is payload_nonce_prefix || little-endian u64 0. Its AAD is ASCII `JETC2 header` followed by those exact serialized bytes. A recipient unwraps a candidate file key, verifies header_tag before allocating body output, and discards/zeroizes it on failure. This binds every recipient, order, public metadata, length, kind, suite, and flag. Removing/adding/reordering a stanza therefore invalidates the envelope; v2 does not support recipient-only rewrap. Adding a recipient requires authenticated open plus a new complete seal with a fresh file key, ephemeral key, file_id, nonce prefix, and chunks.

Streaming body. Body is a sequence of records: plaintext_len u32, record_flags u8, ciphertext[plaintext_len], tag[16]. Reserved flag bits reject; bit 0 FINAL is the only flag. Non-final plaintext_len must be exactly chunk_size. Final plaintext_len is 0..chunk_size and exactly one FINAL record is required, including an empty FINAL record when plaintext length is an exact multiple or zero. No record may follow FINAL. Record index begins at 1 and may not exceed 1,048,577: a maximum 1 TiB file uses 1,048,576 full 1 MiB records plus the mandatory empty FINAL record at index 1,048,577. Record nonce is payload_nonce_prefix || little-endian u64 index. Record AAD is ASCII `JETC2 chunk` || SHA-256(complete fixed prefix and variable header including header_tag) || index u64 || plaintext_len u32 || record_flags u8. This authenticates order, boundaries, finality, header, and declared total body length. Writers reject file plaintext above 1 TiB; body_len overflow or mismatch rejects before publication. Readers cap header_len at 32 MiB, body_len at 1 TiB plus exact record/tag overhead, recipients at 256, metadata at 16 KiB, records at 1,048,577, and never allocate from an unchecked field. File APIs hold at most one plaintext chunk plus bounded header state.

Publication and cancellation. Both operations no-follow-open the destination parent and snapshot its POSIX dev+ino or Windows volume-serial+FILE_ID_128 before creating a random 0600 same-directory temporary. Immediately before install they reopen the caller's parent path without following symlinks/reparse points and require the same identity; drift fails DestinationIo. They fsync/FlushFileBuffers the completed temp before install. POSIX install uses `linkat(parent_fd,temp,parent_fd,destination,0)` so an existing name atomically fails EEXIST -> DestinationExists, then `unlinkat` removes the temp name and `fsync(parent_fd)` durably records both directory changes; any link/unlink/directory-fsync failure is DestinationIo and success is not reported without the directory fsync. Windows 10+ uses `SetFileInformationByHandle(FileRenameInfoEx)` relative to the held parent with `FILE_RENAME_FLAG_FAIL_IF_EXISTS | FILE_RENAME_FLAG_POSIX_SEMANTICS`, never ReplaceIfExists/MoveFileEx replacement, then `FlushFileBuffers` on the held directory; name collision is DestinationExists, unsupported flag/filesystem or flush failure is DestinationIo. The held parent identity and same-volume temp make path replacement/cross-volume races fail rather than redirect or overwrite. If install linked the destination but later temp-unlink/directory-flush fails, return DestinationIo, report the destination may contain a complete authenticated file, and never claim rollback; cleanup removes only a still-owned temp name and never the destination. Any earlier entropy/read/write/authentication/cancellation/fsync/close/install failure non-elidably zeroizes secrets and buffered plaintext, closes handles, removes only the owned temp, and leaves any prior destination unchanged. file_open does not install plaintext until header and every record including FINAL verify. Task cancellation is the D-TASKRUNTIME1 control-plane outcome, checked between records and before publish; it is not an authentication result. No provider call or filesystem I/O occurs while holding a Jet scheduler/global lock.

Tamper and oracle law. Every file_open failure caused by envelope bytes or identity—bad magic/kind/flags/reserved/order/length/trailing/canonical encoding, unsupported version/suite, policy cap, no matching recipient, X25519 rejection, unwrap failure, header/chunk tag failure, reordering, duplication, truncation, appended bytes, wrong key, or metadata failure—returns the same payload-free FileCryptoError.OpenFailed and identical beginner copy/timing class; no recipient index, matching id, parser offset, algorithm backend, tag, OS error, or partial plaintext is exposed. Implementations perform bounded dummy unwrap/tag work when zero recipient matches so observable work does not directly reveal key membership; tests compare operation counts, not wall-clock equality claims. Raw forensic reason/offset is available only in redacted audit after authentication or under the existing expert #Unsafe inspection gate, never from safe open. D-CRYPTO-DIAG1 owns exact terminal copy and exit before CLI ships.

Encoding and keys. The human public-recipient encoding is lowercase Bech32m with HRP `jetx25519`, payload exactly the raw 32-byte public key, canonical checksum, no mixed case, whitespace, aliases, or optional padding. Display may show that public encoding. Secret/private keys never implement Display/Debug/serialization through this ballot; their storage/import/export belongs to D-CRYPTO-API1 and Secret/Key law. Expert raw public bytes map to the identical Recipient value after length/all-zero/canonical checks. Envelope bytes are binary; transport uses existing canonical `core.encoding.base64` only when the caller explicitly asks, with no `JETC:` text wrapper.

Downgrade, migration, and compatibility. The v2 safe writer never emits v1, AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305-with-12-byte-nonce, password-derived keys, or unauthenticated data. Safe file_open accepts only v2 and maps every v1 byte to OpenFailed. Historical v1 grammar is exactly `magic[4]=JETC || version u8=1 || algorithm u8 || nonce[12] || ciphertext[plaintext_len] || tag[16]`, with no flags, length, AAD, metadata, recipient, padding, or trailing field; ciphertext and tag consume the entire remainder. Total length is 34..1,073,741,858 bytes, plaintext cap 1,073,741,824, key exactly 32 bytes, nonce exactly the serialized 12 bytes. Algorithm 1 is IETF ChaCha20-Poly1305; 2 is AES-256-GCM; both use empty AAD and their final 16 bytes are the AEAD tag. `core.crypto.expert.open_v1` inside `#Unsafe("migrate JETC v1")` accepts only this canonical grammar; bad key length, cap/length/magic/version/id, tag failure, mutation, truncation, or appended byte all return the same payload-free OpenFailed and no plaintext. No retry, alternate parser, or algorithm guess exists. `migrate_v1` opens then reseals as v2 recipients into a new destination; it never edits in place, deletes the source, or reports success before v2 reopen verification. V1 writers retire. A major-release/edition note names the removal; fixtures pin every historical accepted byte. Magic/version mutation never falls back to v1. Unknown future v2 suite never falls back to suite 1.

Testing and gates. Acceptance includes byte-for-byte golden vectors for header, each stanza, empty/exact/partial final records, 1 MiB boundaries, multi-recipient order, zero reserved metadata field, file kind, X25519 RFC 7748, HKDF RFC 5869, XChaCha vectors, and historical v1 ids. Differential round trips cover Linux glibc x86_64/aarch64, macOS x86_64/arm64, Windows MSVC x86_64/arm64, and WASI preview 1 only where RNG1/provider and filesystem laws support them. Hostile fixtures cover every length/count/overflow/canonicalization cap, duplicate recipient, low-order/all-zero X25519, wrong key, every single-bit mutation, stanza removal/reorder, chunk reorder/duplicate/truncate/append, missing/multiple FINAL, nonce/index exhaustion, temp collision, short I/O, ENOSPC, cancellation at each boundary, fsync/rename failure, symlink swap, zeroization, and released-artifact scans for legacy writers/fallback/test hooks. Tests prove no output artifact/partial bytes and FileCryptoError.OpenFailed for every open-side format/identity failure. V1 goldens pin both algorithm ids, empty/maximum payloads, exact nonce/tag bytes, 33/34/max/max+1 lengths, every prefix byte, unknown id, wrong key, mutation/truncation/append, and zero trailing tolerance. Publication tests race parent replacement and destination creation at every boundary, verify POSIX linkat no-replace plus post-link directory fsync, Windows FileRenameInfoEx fail-if-exists plus directory flush, destination-may-exist reporting after post-install durability failure, and never overwrite/remove a preexisting destination. Fuzzers use a fixed parser budget and never allocate from untrusted lengths. the compatible exact-graph D-DEP-CRYPTO-SUITE2 gate, D-CRYPTO-RNG1, revised D-CRYPTO-API1 deferral, and D-CRYPTO-DIAG1 criteria remain blocked until their live ballots ratify compatibly; Option B additionally requires an age-format/I6 ballot.

Beginner pass: pass recipients and paths; Jet chooses fresh secrets, chunks safely, authenticates everything, and publishes atomically. Expert pass: exact suite, bytes, caps, enforced metadata absence, recipient identity leakage, audit, streaming state, legacy migration, and raw public-key conversion are inspectable and controlled. Hybrid pass: file seal/open, expert inspection, and migration share one parser, key schedule, authenticated grammar, and failure law; value seal/open remains API1-owned and is not this file format; convenience never creates a second default format.

options.name: JETC v2 recipient envelope
options.detail: Recommended. Write one versioned Jet file format: X25519 recipient wrapping, HKDF-SHA256, XChaCha20-Poly1305 payload chunks, no implicit metadata, bounded parsing, atomic output, and explicit expert-only v1 migration. Record lengths reveal exact plaintext length; v2 provides content confidentiality, not padding or size hiding. Beginner path calls and expert inspection/migration share the same authenticated byte grammar.
options.code:
recipients :: [alice.public_key(), recovery.public_key()]
crypto.file_seal(recipients, path("backup.db"), path("backup.db.jetc"))?
crypto.file_open(&alice, path("backup.db.jetc"), path("restored.db"))?

$ jet crypto inspect backup.db.jetc
format: JETC v2
suite: X25519 + HKDF-SHA256 + XChaCha20-Poly1305
recipients: 2
chunk size: 1048576
plaintext size: 42949672960 (visible)
metadata: none

options.name: age v1 interoperability
options.detail: Choose published age v1 interoperability and explicitly decline the JETC v2 byte grammar in this ballot. No file API ships from B alone: a follow-up age-conformance ballot must pin the complete age header/stanza/payload grammar, limits, recipient/error/migration law and exact I6 graph first. Until it ratifies, file_seal/file_open remain unavailable rather than approximating age or borrowing A fields. Value seal/open remains API1-owned JETC.

options.name: Decline file envelopes
options.detail: Explicitly decline file encryption and defer any file format to a future ballot. C adds no file grammar, writer, reader, compatibility promise, or API; file_seal/file_open remain unavailable. D-CRYPTO-SUITE1's general file-envelope goal stays open on card #302 until a future ballot ratifies, while API1 recipient-based value JETV remains available independently.

comparisons.note: age uses recipient stanzas and a streaming authenticated payload with a small misuse-resistant command surface. A adopts recipient wrapping and streaming while keeping a byte-pinned Jet format; B chooses direct interoperability.
comparisons.code:
age -r age1... -o backup.age backup.db
age -d -i key.txt -o restored.db backup.age

comparisons.note: secretstream authenticates ordered chunks and an explicit final tag so truncation and reordering fail. A pins equivalent ordered-final semantics instead of exposing nonce/chunk bookkeeping to users.
Tink binds ciphertext to a key and associated data through safe templates rather than raw nonce APIs. A similarly fixes the safe suite and authenticates the complete header and chunk position.

decisions.title: Persistent cryptographic key lifecycle in core.vault
decisions.gist: Choose how typed cryptographic keys persist, rotate, revoke, and move between hosts without adding raw safe export or breaking the existing Secret-gated repo vault.
decisions.explainer:
Batch status: compatibility-required with D-CRYPTO-API1 and D-CRYPTO-KEYWRAP1; these companion decisions are proposed in this batch and each grants nothing until independently ratified. Inherited truth. D-JPK-SECRETCRYPTO1=A owns core.vault's age-encrypted repository store, local X25519 identity, and temporary FFI bridge. Live core.vault exposes only get(name: String) -> String?; every reachable call requires the existing Secret effect (E1264), and comptime/build use is E1265 with no #Impure escape. This ballot extends that module without renaming get, changing its Option behavior, adding an effect, or treating Secret as ordinary Fs. All new core.vault calls require #(Secret); signatures use ordinary Jet T ? E syntax. D-CRYPTO-API1 must ratify SigningKey and X25519SecretKey; this ballot persists exactly those two secret-key roles. D-CRYPTO-RNG1 gates generation. D-DEP-CRYPTO-SUITE2 must ratify its revised exact ed25519-dalek 2.2.0 (alloc,zeroize), X25519, and zeroize slices or their native replacements before typed-key calls ship. D-CRYPTO-DIAG1 gates CLI copy/exits. No safe portable wrapping ships until a separate D-CRYPTO-KEYWRAP1 ratifies a standalone key-backup format, recipient/privacy law, dependencies, and diagnostics; file-only D-CRYPTO-ENVELOPE2 does not own key wrapping.

Types and binding. VaultKey is sealed and compiler-known, implemented only by SigningKey and X25519SecretKey. KeyRef<T> is an immutable public-metadata value containing provider=.Repo, repository_uuid[16], NFC name, generation u64, opaque_id[16], and record_hash[32]. It is created only from authenticated vault/v2 bytes, cannot be forged from String, retagged, or reflected into fields, and a load matches every field plus T before decrypting key bytes. Clone/hash/compare are allowed. Display is repo:<name>@v<generation>; Debug adds only opaque_id's first eight hex characters. Name is NFC UTF-8 1..128 bytes, excludes slash, backslash, NUL/control, dot components, and leading/trailing whitespace. String-secret and typed-key namespaces are disjoint.

Exact read API, all #(Secret): current<T: VaultKey>(name: String) -> KeyRef<T>? ? VaultError; versions<T: VaultKey>(name: String) -> [KeyRef<T>] ? VaultError newest first; load<T: VaultKey>(reference: &KeyRef<T>) -> T ? VaultError; status<T: VaultKey>(reference: &KeyRef<T>) -> KeyStatus ? VaultError. KeyStatus is Active, Retired, or Revoked. load accepts Active and Retired. Revoked returns Revoked before copying key material. current returns none only when no typed logical name exists; wrong T is WrongType. get remains exactly String? and never reads typed entries.

Old-record and rotation law. Applications persist the exact KeyRef<X25519SecretKey> with their own record index when creating recipient-encrypted data; the encrypted envelope also carries the corresponding public recipient identity under its owning format. Opening an old record loads that stored KeyRef, never current(name). New writes resolve current once and persist that exact ref. Signing verification uses the persisted VerifyKey; a SigningKey reference is needed only to create new signatures. rotate creates generation n+1, marks it current, retires prior current, and never rewrites a KeyRef or old record. record_hash binds only immutable type/name/generation/id/provenance/created time/public-key digest/key-byte digest; load recomputes that immutable hash. Mutable status/time/reason remain authenticated by payload_hash but are excluded from KeyRef identity, so rotation or revocation cannot invalidate or retarget the reference.

Option A mutation authority. Runtime mutation uses only the prepared-plan, exact-preview, typed one-use authorization, and concrete commit functions in the final closure below. Possessing #(Secret) alone never writes. Interactive approval uses the native preview; headless mutation needs exact jet trust grant vault.write:<repository_uuid>. Workspace/source/environment/DAP/stdin cannot approve. No unrevoke, generation reuse, in-place mutation, destructive purge, or implicit rotation exists.

Revocation is logical, not erasure. A revoked row retains encrypted key bytes so repository history and backups remain structurally readable, but safe load refuses it. Existing plaintext/ciphertext/signatures are not recalled or deleted. Raw expert export performed before revocation cannot be clawed back. Reimporting identical raw bytes after revocation creates a new opaque id and next generation, remains audit-visible as reimported, and never reactivates or aliases the revoked KeyRef. A safe backup/import API remains absent until D-CRYPTO-KEYWRAP1.

Raw import/export. No safe byte/text import/export exists. Exact prepared #Unsafe import and API1 raw-export function names are pinned in the final closure below; vault adds no second exporter. Public VerifyKey/X25519PublicKey keep API1 canonical encoding.
