Canonical vault/v2 plaintext grammar. Integers are unsigned little-endian; text is canonical NFC UTF-8. Bytes are exactly: magic "JVLT"[4], version u8=2, flags u8=0, reserved u16=0, repository_uuid[16], revision u64>=1, string_count u32, key_name_count u32, key_version_count u32; then String rows, KeyName rows, KeyVersion rows, and payload_hash[32]=SHA-256 of every preceding byte. Total plaintext cap is 16,777,216 bytes and exact consumption is required.
String row: name_len u16, name bytes, value_len u32, value UTF-8 bytes. Caps: 4,096 rows, name 1..128, value 0..1,048,576. Rows sort by normalized name bytes and duplicate/colliding names reject.
KeyName row: type u8 (1=Ed25519 signing, 2=X25519 secret), name_len u16, name, current_generation u64 (0 exactly when no version is Active), latest_generation u64. Caps: 1,024 names. Rows sort (type,name); duplicates reject.
KeyVersion row: type u8, status u8 (1=Active,2=Retired,3=Revoked), provenance u8 (1=Generated,2=Imported), reserved u8=0, name_len u16, name, generation u64>=1, opaque_id[16], created_unix_ms u64, status_unix_ms u64, reason_hash[32], public_key_hash[32], key_len u16=32, key_bytes[32]. Caps: 8,192 versions. Rows sort (type,name,generation); generation is contiguous from 1 through latest, opaque ids unique, exactly one Active equals nonzero current, retired/revoked are never current, and every row has one KeyName. Unknown value, nonzero reserved/flag, non-NFC, noncanonical ordering, overflow, trailing byte, bad count/relation/hash, or duplicate rejects before key release. Historical unversioned String pairs are a distinct v1 input, never guessed from JVLT bytes.

Outer protection and migration. The canonical plaintext, including raw secret-key rows, exists only in zeroized memory and is encrypted as one age payload to the existing repository recipient set under D-JPK-SECRETCRYPTO1; no nested home-grown encryption. Readers accept historical pair stream and authenticated v2. get preserves historical behavior. First authorized mutation decodes all historical pairs, creates a random repository_uuid, writes revision 1 v2, decrypt-verifies exact bytes, and preserves every String entry. It never infers a key from a String, name, ~/.jet signing file, or length. Typed import is explicit #Unsafe only.

Atomic writer and recovery. All supported platforms require a local filesystem with atomic same-directory replacement; otherwise UnsupportedProvider. Common flow: no-follow open owner-controlled .jet, acquire one exclusive create-new .jet/secrets.age.lock containing repository_uuid/revision/pid/process-start/nonce, re-read store identity+hash, write random create-new private temp, fsync/FlushFileBuffers, decrypt-verify, install, sync directory/volume where supported, then remove only owned temp/lock. An existing lock is stale only after ten minutes, same owner, process identity proved dead, nonce well-formed, and store revision/hash still equals the lock; recovery is audited and uses create-new quarantine rename, never blind delete.
Linux glibc uses openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, O_NOFOLLOW/O_CLOEXEC, mode 0600, pidfd for stale-owner proof, renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE) for replacement, fsync store and directory; lack of these primitives returns UnsupportedProvider. macOS uses openat/O_NOFOLLOW, fcntl exclusive lock plus pid start identity, mode 0600, renamex_np(RENAME_SWAP), fsync file and directory. Windows uses CreateFileW with reparse rejection and owner-only DACL, exclusive non-share lock handle, process creation-time proof, FlushFileBuffers, and ReplaceFileW with write-through on the same volume. After exchange/swap, the old file occupies Jet's temp name and is removed only after directory/volume sync. Pre-install conflict returns Conflict with old store intact. Failure after install but before durable sync returns DurabilityUnknown and states the new revision may be visible; callers inspect revision before retry. Cancellation before install cleans up; after install Jet finishes durability/readback and returns the committed result, avoiding duplicate mutation.

Errors and suppression. VaultError is closed: InvalidName, NotFound, WrongType, Revoked, Locked, AuthorityDenied, Conflict, UnsupportedProvider, InvalidEncoding, DurabilityUnknown, Crypto(CryptoError), Io {operation,redacted_path}, Internal {incident_id}. Missing/wrong identity and age-open failure collapse to Locked. No value contains key/store bytes, identity/recipient, raw OS/backend/dependency prose, or foreign path. Secret/key/buffer data are non-elidably zeroized after last use. Handled errors are program data; unhandled uses E3001/exit70. E1264/E1265 remain the only effect diagnostics; wrong T is normal type error and expert outside #Unsafe is E0510. CLI commands remain blocked until D-CRYPTO-DIAG1 pins copy/JSON/exits/no-artifact/audit.

Platforms and acceptance. A supports Linux glibc x86_64/aarch64, macOS x86_64/arm64, and Windows MSVC x86_64/arm64 after real primitive tests. WASI, browser, mobile, musl, freestanding, comptime, pure, and interpreter return UnsupportedProvider before key work. Tests pin every v2 byte/cap/relation, v1 migration, exact KeyRef old-record workflow, restart/load, rotation, revoke/reimport truth, concurrent conflict, stale-lock proof, each OS install/durability boundary, cancellation, zeroization, redaction, dependency gates, and released-artifact absence of test/raw safe export. Beginner pass: generate once, persist the returned typed reference, load after restart. Expert pass: exact bytes, authority, versions, imports, conflicts, durability, provider and audit are inspectable. Hybrid pass: Strings and typed keys share one Secret gate, recipient authority, atomic writer and audit path; raw control remains #Unsafe.

Closure amendment; controls any earlier shorthand. Exact mutation binding. MutationPlan<T:VaultKey> is move-only, nonserializable, five-minute-lived, and bound to canonical repository identity plus starting revision. prepare_generate<T>(name:String) -> MutationPlan<T> ? VaultError; prepare_store<T>(name:String,key:take T) -> MutationPlan<T> ? VaultError; prepare_rotate<T>(name:String) -> MutationPlan<T> ? VaultError; prepare_retire<T>(reference:&KeyRef<T>,reason:String) -> MutationPlan<T> ? VaultError; prepare_revoke<T>(reference:&KeyRef<T>,reason:String) -> MutationPlan<T> ? VaultError. Preparation validates name/reference/current state and snapshots action, type, name, exact reference fields, normalized reason hash, starting store hash/revision, and for store the public/key digests while retaining the moved key in zeroized private storage. It generates no new key and mutates nothing. operation_hash=SHA-256(ASCII "JVLT2 operation" || canonical repository_uuid || starting_revision || starting_store_hash || action u8 || type u8 || name_len/name || reference-or-zero fields || reason_hash || store public/key digests-or-zero). authorize_write(operation:&MutationPlan<T>,reason:String) -> VaultWrite<T> ? VaultError shows action/type/name/generation transition/repository/reason, binds exact operation_hash+preview hash+user/session, and returns a one-use capability that cannot authorize another plan. commit_generate<T:VaultKey>(write:take VaultWrite<T>,plan:take MutationPlan<T>) -> KeyRef<T> ? VaultError; commit_store<T:VaultKey>(write:take VaultWrite<T>,plan:take MutationPlan<T>) -> KeyRef<T> ? VaultError; commit_rotate<T:VaultKey>(write:take VaultWrite<T>,plan:take MutationPlan<T>) -> Rotation<T> ? VaultError; commit_retire<T:VaultKey>(write:take VaultWrite<T>,plan:take MutationPlan<T>) -> () ? VaultError; commit_revoke<T:VaultKey>(write:take VaultWrite<T>,plan:take MutationPlan<T>) -> () ? VaultError. Commit rejects any hash/revision/expiry mismatch before effect. Generated key material is drawn only after authorization through RNG1. retire/revoke signatures are therefore concrete, generic-bounded, and fallible.

Read outcome correction. current<T>(name) returns ok(None) when that typed name is absent or has no Active generation; it never returns a revoked/retired fallback. If the same normalized name exists under the other key type, it returns WrongType. versions remains newest-first and includes all statuses.

Exact digest domains. public_key_hash=SHA-256(ASCII "JVLT2 public key" || type u8 || canonical public_key[32]). key_digest=SHA-256(ASCII "JVLT2 key bytes" || type u8 || secret key_bytes[32]); it never renders or leaves the encrypted/zeroized store pipeline. record_hash=SHA-256(ASCII "JVLT2 immutable record" || type u8 || provenance u8 || name_len u16/name || generation u64 || opaque_id[16] || created_unix_ms u64 || public_key_hash[32] || key_digest[32]). Active reason_hash is 32 zero bytes. Retired/revoked reason is NFC UTF-8 1..256 bytes; reason_hash=SHA-256(ASCII "JVLT2 status reason" || status u8 || reason_len u16 || reason bytes). Rotation uses exact reason "rotated". payload_hash=SHA-256(ASCII "JVLT2 payload" || every canonical vault/v2 byte before payload_hash). record_hash excludes mutable status/status time/reason. All preimages use the little-endian encodings and canonical text already pinned; no ambiguous concatenation exists.

Dependency correction. D-JPK-SECRETCRYPTO1=A continues to authorize the existing age outer-store bridge only. Live D-DEP-CRYPTO1=A authorizes the existing Ed25519 backend family, but typed SigningKey generation/import/load ships only after its exact version/features/transitives/checksums/license/advisory lock is owner-approved by a compatible dependency artifact or native replacement proof. X25519SecretKey typed operations additionally remain blocked on D-DEP-CRYPTO-SUITE2's exact X25519/zeroize slice. VAULT1 approves no crate by implication.

Portable backup API names. Only after D-CRYPTO-KEYWRAP1 ratifies compatibly, core.vault adds export_to_recipients<T:VaultKey>(reference:&KeyRef<T>,recipients:[X25519PublicKey]) -> WrappedVaultKey ? KeyWrapError; export_to_passphrase<T:VaultKey>(reference:&KeyRef<T>,passphrase:&Secret) -> WrappedVaultKey ? KeyWrapError; import_wrapped<T:VaultKey>(write:take VaultWrite<T>,plan:take WrappedImportPlan<T>) -> KeyRef<T> ? KeyWrapError. prepare_import_wrapped<T>(name:String,wrapped:WrappedVaultKey,unlock:KeyUnlock) -> WrappedImportPlan<T> ? KeyWrapError fully authenticates and retains zeroized key material. authorize_wrapped_import<T>(plan:&WrappedImportPlan<T>,reason:String) -> VaultWrite<T> ? KeyWrapError shows destination/type/origin and binds the exact operation hash, repository revision, user/session, and expiry. commit cannot substitute bytes/unlock/name. No earlier generic export_wrapped/import_wrapped spelling ships.

Platform install correction. Linux/macOS exchange/swap leaves the prior store at the prepared backup name; it is removed only after new-file readback and directory fsync. Windows does not claim exchange or universal directory fsync: create private same-volume temp and unique .jet/secrets.age.prev.<nonce>; FlushFileBuffers(temp), call ReplaceFileW(store,temp,backup,0) after exclusive-handle/revision recheck, reopen+decrypt-verify+FlushFileBuffers(new store), then attempt volume metadata flush with an owner-authorized volume handle. If ReplaceFileW fails, prior store remains and temp/empty backup cleanup is owned. If replacement succeeds but readback/file/volume durability cannot be proved, return DurabilityUnknown, retain the backup and journal paths, and state new revision may be visible; recovery compares authenticated revisions and either completes new revision or restores backup atomically. Only after proof may Jet remove backup. Windows never describes the old file as occupying the temp name.

Option B authenticated journal. Its two-store journal is exactly .jet/vault.txn.age, an age-encrypted payload to the same existing repository recipients, mode 0600/current-user DACL, with canonical plaintext: magic "JVTX"[4], version u8=1, state u8 (1=Prepared,2=StringsInstalled,3=KeysInstalled), reserved u16=0, txid[16], repository_uuid[16], starting_strings_hash[32], new_strings_hash[32], starting_keys_hash[32], new_keys_hash[32], strings_temp_name_len u16/name, keys_temp_name_len u16/name, created_unix_ms u64, payload_hash[32]=SHA-256(ASCII "JVTX1 payload" || all preceding bytes). Names are exact basenames .secrets.<txid>.tmp and .crypto-keys.<txid>.tmp; no separators; total plaintext <=1024 and exact consumption. Journal and both staged files decrypt-verify before first install. Each state transition rewrites/fsyncs/replaces the journal under the same OS law. Readers seeing a journal take the exclusive transaction lock, verify starting/current/new hashes, finish the missing install(s) forward, verify both recipient revisions, mark KeysInstalled, sync, then remove journal/backups; any impossible hash/state returns DurabilityUnknown and serves neither mixed store. No blind rollback or unauthenticated recovery occurs.

Final API/authorization closure; controls conflicting shorthand. Exact mutation functions are:
prepare_generate<T:VaultKey>(name:String) -> MutationPlan<T> ? VaultError;
prepare_store<T:VaultKey>(name:String,key:take T) -> MutationPlan<T> ? VaultError;
prepare_rotate<T:VaultKey>(name:String) -> MutationPlan<T> ? VaultError;
prepare_retire<T:VaultKey>(reference:&KeyRef<T>,reason:String) -> MutationPlan<T> ? VaultError;
prepare_revoke<T:VaultKey>(reference:&KeyRef<T>,reason:String) -> MutationPlan<T> ? VaultError.
authorize_write<T:VaultKey>(plan:&MutationPlan<T>,reason:String) -> VaultWrite<T> ? VaultError.
commit_generate<T:VaultKey>(write:take VaultWrite<T>,plan:take MutationPlan<T>) -> KeyRef<T> ? VaultError;
commit_store<T:VaultKey>(write:take VaultWrite<T>,plan:take MutationPlan<T>) -> KeyRef<T> ? VaultError;
commit_rotate<T:VaultKey>(write:take VaultWrite<T>,plan:take MutationPlan<T>) -> Rotation<T> ? VaultError;
commit_retire<T:VaultKey>(write:take VaultWrite<T>,plan:take MutationPlan<T>) -> () ? VaultError;
commit_revoke<T:VaultKey>(write:take VaultWrite<T>,plan:take MutationPlan<T>) -> () ? VaultError.
reason for manual retire/revoke is NFC UTF-8 1..256 bytes with no control/NUL/leading/trailing whitespace. rotate alone uses canonical reason "rotated"; no caller reason exists. All commits verify action/type/operation_hash/preview_hash/repository/start revision/expiry and consume both values.

Raw expert import has no unbound one-step form. core.vault.expert.prepare_import_signing(name:String,bytes:take [U8]) -> MutationPlan<SigningKey> ? VaultError and prepare_import_x25519(name:String,bytes:take [U8]) -> MutationPlan<X25519SecretKey> ? VaultError require lexical #Unsafe, exact 32-byte canonical validation, moved-buffer zeroization, and Imported provenance. The ordinary authorize_write binds that plan. core.vault.expert.commit_import_signing(write:take VaultWrite<SigningKey>,plan:take MutationPlan<SigningKey>) -> KeyRef<SigningKey> ? VaultError and commit_import_x25519(write:take VaultWrite<X25519SecretKey>,plan:take MutationPlan<X25519SecretKey>) -> KeyRef<X25519SecretKey> ? VaultError commit it. Raw export names are exactly API1's core.crypto.expert.signing_key_bytes and x25519_secret_bytes; VAULT adds none.

Wrapped import names are exactly KEYWRAP1: prepare_import_wrapped<T:VaultKey>(name:String,wrapped:WrappedVaultKey,unlock:KeyUnlock) -> WrappedImportPlan<T> ? KeyWrapError; authorize_wrapped_import<T:VaultKey>(plan:&WrappedImportPlan<T>,reason:String) -> VaultWrite<T> ? KeyWrapError; commit_import_wrapped<T:VaultKey>(write:take VaultWrite<T>,plan:take WrappedImportPlan<T>) -> KeyRef<T> ? KeyWrapError. Export names are exactly export_to_recipients<T:VaultKey>(reference:&KeyRef<T>,recipients:[X25519PublicKey]) -> WrappedVaultKey ? KeyWrapError and export_to_passphrase<T:VaultKey>(reference:&KeyRef<T>,passphrase:&Secret) -> WrappedVaultKey ? KeyWrapError. No alias survives.

Exact operation bytes. action is u8: 1 Generate, 2 Store, 3 Rotate, 4 Retire, 5 Revoke, 6 RawImport, 7 WrappedImport. type is u8: 1 SigningKey, 2 X25519SecretKey. Canonical operation preimage order is ASCII "JVLT2 operation" || repository_uuid[16] || starting_revision u64 || starting_store_hash[32] || provider_binding_hash[32] || action u8 || type u8 || name_len u16 || name || reference_present u8 || reference_repository_uuid[16] || reference_generation u64 || reference_opaque_id[16] || reference_record_hash[32] || reason_len u16 || reason || public_key_hash[32] || key_digest[32] || wrapped_hash[32]. When reference_present=0, all four reference payload fields are zero; absent reason has reason_len=0 and no bytes; unavailable public/key/wrapped facts are 32 zero bytes. All integers little-endian, text canonical as above, exact fields only. operation_hash=SHA-256(preimage). WrappedImport uses wrapped_hash=SHA-256(ASCII "JVKW1 wrapped bytes" || exact canonical WrappedVaultKey bytes); RawImport/Store bind public/key digests; Generate/Rotate bind neither because key generation occurs after approval.

Exact preview bytes are ASCII "JVLT2 authority preview" || operation_hash[32] || action u8 || type u8 || repository_uuid[16] || starting_revision u64 || name_len u16 || name || transition_from_generation u64 || transition_to_generation u64 || reason_len u16 || reason || authority_reason_len u16 || authority_reason || expires_unix_ms u64. transition value is zero when absent; Generate/Store/RawImport/WrappedImport target next generation, Rotate carries current and next, Retire/Revoke carry referenced generation as from and zero as to. preview_hash=SHA-256(these bytes). The native preview renders these same public facts. The issued VaultWrite additionally binds preview_hash, authenticated user/session identity and expiry in its unforgeable private state; user/session bytes are not silently inserted into preview_hash.

Starting-store and authority-reason closure. starting_store_hash never hashes randomized age ciphertext, filesystem metadata, path, mtime, or recipient wrapping. After authenticated age open, a vault/v2 store uses starting_store_hash=SHA-256(ASCII "JVLT2 starting store" || canonical vault/v2 plaintext including its verified payload_hash[32]). A historical pair store is decoded, canonicalized as count u32 followed by name_len u16/name/value_len u32/value rows sorted by NFC name bytes with the historical caps, then uses SHA-256(ASCII "JVLT1 starting store" || those canonical bytes). Missing store uses SHA-256(ASCII "JVLT0 absent store") only for a create operation after no-follow absence proof. Invalid/noncanonical/unopenable input yields Locked/InvalidEncoding and no plan. operation_hash, conflict checks, locks and recovery compare this plaintext-derived hash plus revision/repository_uuid; provider_binding_hash=SHA-256(ASCII "JVLT2 provider recipients" || recipient_count u16 || sorted canonical recipient encodings with u16 lengths) is independently included in operation_hash; recipient additions/removals therefore invalidate a plan. Re-encryption to the same canonical contents and identical recipient set does not invalidate a plan, while any semantic content/status/key/provider-recipient change does.

authorize_write and authorize_wrapped_import authority_reason is NFC UTF-8 1..256 bytes, no NUL/control, leading/trailing whitespace, invalid UTF-8, non-NFC, or embedded line separator; invalid input returns InvalidName before preview/token issuance. authority_reason_len is u16 little-endian and safe because of the 256-byte cap. The exact normalized bytes enter preview_hash once; UI/audit render the same bytes and never substitute/truncate them.

Expiry enforcement uses monotonic time. Preview displays expires_unix_ms=wall-clock issue time plus 300,000 ms and binds that u64 in preview_hash for human/audit correlation. The private plan and VaultWrite also store monotonic_issue and monotonic_deadline=issue+300 seconds from the same runtime clock. Every authorize/commit compares monotonic now to deadline; wall-clock rollback/forward cannot extend or prematurely expire authority. Missing/failed monotonic clock returns UnsupportedProvider before preview. Suspension counts as elapsed when the platform monotonic clock counts it; expiry is final and requires a newly prepared plan/preview.

Imported-origin grammar closure. Every KeyVersion row inserts these fields after public_key_hash[32] and before key_len: origin_present u8; origin_repository_uuid[16]; origin_name_len u16; origin_name bytes; origin_generation u64; origin_opaque_id[16]; origin_record_hash[32]. If origin_present=0, UUID/generation/id/hash are all zero, origin_name_len=0, and no name bytes follow. Generated and raw #Unsafe imported rows use 0. If origin_present=1, origin_name follows the same NFC 1..128-byte vault-name law, generation>=1, UUID/id/hash are nonzero, and the row must have Imported provenance; only authenticated KEYWRAP import may create it. Cross-repository or different-name JVKW import copies the exact authenticated origin fields. Same-repository idempotent import creates no row. Unknown/invalid combination is InvalidEncoding before key release.

The immutable record hash preimage is amended to ASCII "JVLT2 immutable record" || type u8 || provenance u8 || name_len u16/name || generation u64 || opaque_id[16] || created_unix_ms u64 || public_key_hash[32] || key_digest[32] || origin_present u8 || origin_repository_uuid[16] || origin_name_len u16/origin_name || origin_generation u64 || origin_opaque_id[16] || origin_record_hash[32], using the same zero/omission rule. payload_hash authenticates these serialized fields again. KeyRef<T> still binds the destination repository/name/generation/id plus this destination record_hash; origin metadata is inspectable audit provenance, never a second load target or alias.

Migration. Historical unversioned String pairs migrate with no KeyVersion rows, so no origin fields exist. This decision has not shipped a vault/v2 writer; earlier unpublished draft layouts are not accepted as wire formats or guessed. The first ratified v2 reader/writer requires the origin fields above from day one. Future removal/change requires a version ballot and byte fixtures.

Ed25519 dependency gate. D-DEP-CRYPTO1=A is only family-level authority for ed25519-dalek. Companion D-DEP-CRYPTO-SUITE2 proposes ed25519-dalek 2.2.0 with defaults off and features [alloc,zeroize] inside exact 55-package Cargo.lock SHA-256 42e2879fae279e42e1a99422e94d7a96bc8965a07a4ec7b1f47bbe922c214a2d and SBOM-v2 SHA-256 dbe299850bf88167eea701a76e6e6f66af493f792c7d48a31ad794f27df8e6fc. SigningKey generate/store/load/raw import, public-key recomputation, KEYWRAP signing-key validation, and any vault/v2 Signing row remain blocked until that exact slice ratifies and a fresh full RustSec report, signed evidence bundle, per-operation/target minimal locks, vectors, symbol/process proof and Epoch-3 removal row pass—or a first-party Ed25519 replacement passes RFC 8032 strict vectors, differential, side-channel/assembly, zeroization, target-parity, independent-review and artifact-absence proof. VAULT1 alone approves none of that.

First-write repository identity closure. Preparing any mutation against a proved-absent store or authenticated historical pair store sets starting_revision=0 and has no pre-existing repository_uuid. The prepare call draws provisional_repository_uuid[16] exactly once from D-CRYPTO-RNG1, rejects all-zero, stores it inside the move-only MutationPlan, and uses that same value as repository_uuid in operation_hash and preview_hash. The native preview and audit display its lowercase hex UUID together with "create vault/v2 revision 1". RNG failure returns EntropyUnavailable before preview; retrying preparation creates a different plan/UUID and requires new authority.

authorize_write binds the provisional UUID, starting_revision=0, exact JVLT0-absent or JVLT1-canonical starting_store_hash, provider_binding_hash, operation fields and expiry. commit re-proves absence or reopens/authenticates the historical store, recomputes the same starting hash and provider binding, and rejects any appearance/change/recipient change as Conflict before writing. It must serialize that exact provisional UUID into vault/v2 repository_uuid and revision=1; generating, substituting, normalizing, or adopting another UUID at commit is Internal before publication. Readback verifies UUID/revision/operation result before durability success.

Existing vault/v2 preparation never draws a UUID: it copies authenticated repository_uuid and revision>=1 into the plan, and commit writes the same UUID with revision+1 using checked arithmetic. A historical pair store that disappears, becomes v2, or changes any canonical pair/provider recipient after preparation is a conflict, not a fresh first write. A missing store that appears is likewise a conflict. Thus absence/historical identity, recipient authority, provisional UUID and first revision are one previewed compare-and-swap fact with no substitution window.
decisions.story: Mina generates one X25519 identity for tenant backups and one Ed25519 release-signing key, restarts the service, rotates the backup identity without losing old records, revokes a compromised version, and restores an authorized host. Today core.vault reads String secrets from one age-encrypted repository store but cannot preserve nominal key roles or immutable versions. She needs exact typed references, atomic mutation, explicit write authority, and honest backup/revocation semantics without raw safe export.

options.name: One versioned repository vault
options.detail: Recommended. Migrate the existing age-encrypted store to canonical vault/v2 containing disjoint String and typed Signing/X25519 rows. One-shot VaultWrite permits runtime/operator workflows; immutable KeyRef versions make old-record access, rotation and revocation exact. This preserves one Secret gate, one recipient set and one atomic store.
options.code:
op :: vault.prepare_rotate<crypto.X25519SecretKey>("backup")?
write :: vault.authorize_write(&op, reason: "scheduled backup-key rotation")?
rotation :: vault.Rotation<crypto.X25519SecretKey> =
    vault.commit_rotate(take(write), take(op))?
// New records persist rotation.current; old records keep rotation.previous.

options.name: Separate typed repository key store
options.detail: Keep .jet/secrets.age and get(String) byte-for-byte unchanged. Put the same canonical key-name/key-version grammar, repository_uuid, authority, KeyRef binding, lifecycle, errors and atomic platform law in .jet/crypto-keys.age; omit String rows and set string_count=0. Both files use the existing age recipient set and #(Secret), but updates cannot rewrite ordinary secrets. Cross-file recipient rotation stages and decrypt-verifies both, then records a fsynced transaction journal with both starting/new hashes before either swap. A crash may leave one swap installed; every reader that sees the journal completes the second swap or returns DurabilityUnknown, and never serves mixed recipient revisions. More isolation, but two encrypted artifacts and two-file crash recovery violate the one-store simplicity of A.
options.code:
op :: vault.prepare_generate<crypto.SigningKey>("release")?
write :: vault.authorize_write(&op, reason: "create signer")?
ref :: vault.commit_generate(take(write), take(op))?
// writes .jet/crypto-keys.age; .jet/secrets.age unchanged

options.name: CLI-managed typed repository vault
options.detail: Use A's exact vault/v2 bytes, KeyRef reads, old-record workflow, lifecycle, migration, platform atomicity, errors and gates, but expose no runtime authorize_write/generate/store/rotate/retire/revoke/import calls. Only D-CRYPTO-DIAG1-ratified jet vault key commands mutate after native preview or exact CI grant. Applications with #(Secret) load versions but cannot change the store. Smallest runtime authority; cannot provision transactionally inside a service workflow.
options.code:
$ jet vault key rotate backup --type x25519
Preview: create backup@v3; retire backup@v2; preserve v1/v2
[Rotate] [Cancel]
created repo:backup@v3

fn open_old(ref: vault.KeyRef<crypto.X25519SecretKey>) -> crypto.X25519SecretKey ? vault.VaultError #(Secret) {
    return vault.load(&ref)?
}

comparisons.note: Vault uses versioned logical key names, explicit policy, rotation, and revocation without returning raw key material. A adopts typed versions and explicit mutation authority inside Jet's existing local encrypted store, not a network service.
comparisons.code:
vault write transit/keys/payments/rotate
vault write transit/keys/payments/config min_decryption_version=2

comparisons.note: KMS references durable key identities and separates use from administration. A keeps that separation with Secret-gated load plus one-shot VaultWrite, while remaining offline and repository-scoped.

SOPS and age commit recipient-encrypted ciphertext so authorized machines can decrypt offline. A preserves Jet's ratified age store and adds typed key/version records rather than inventing a second vault.
comparisons.code:
sops --encrypt secrets.yaml > secrets.enc.yaml
age -R recipients.txt -o secrets.age plaintext

decisions.title: Portable wrapped vault-key backup
decisions.gist: Choose the exact portable authenticated format for backing up typed SigningKey and X25519SecretKey versions to recipients or a passphrase.
decisions.explainer:
Scope and gates. D-CRYPTO-VAULT1 owns persistent SigningKey/X25519SecretKey rows, KeyRef<T>, Secret effect, VaultWrite, rotation/revocation, and atomic store mutation. D-CRYPTO-API1 owns those key types and public keys. This ballot owns only portable wrapped-key bytes and export/import semantics. It does not reuse API1's JETW generic-Secret format or file-only ENVELOPE2. D-CRYPTO-RNG1 must ratify compatible entropy. D-DEP-CRYPTO1=A approves algorithm families only. Companion D-DEP-CRYPTO-SUITE2 now locks chacha20poly1305 0.10.1 (defaults off; alloc) and ed25519-dalek 2.2.0 (defaults off; alloc,zeroize) inside its exact 55-package Cargo.lock SHA-256 42e2879fae279e42e1a99422e94d7a96bc8965a07a4ec7b1f47bbe922c214a2d and SBOM-v2 SHA-256 dbe299850bf88167eea701a76e6e6f66af493f792c7d48a31ad794f27df8e6fc. These exact slices cover JVKW XChaCha payload/stanza AEAD and strict Ed25519 public-key derivation/validation. They grant nothing while unratified, and no KEYWRAP mode ships until SUITE2 ratifies plus a fresh full RustSec report, signed evidence bundle, per-operation/target minimal locks, vectors, symbol/process proof, and Epoch-3 removal rows pass—or native replacement proof passes. Passphrase mode also waits on D-PWHASH-POLICY1's admission/cancellation/resource substrate. D-CRYPTO-DIAG1 gates CLI copy/exits. These companion decisions are proposed in this batch; each grants nothing until independently ratified.

Surface and roles. WrappedVaultKey is public authenticated ciphertext: clone, compare, .bytes(), and from_bytes are allowed; Display is WrappedVaultKey(mode:<recipient|passphrase>,type:<signing|x25519>,origin:<name>@v<generation>) and never shows recipient, salt, ciphertext, hashes, or key bytes. Origin repository/name/generation, mode/type, recipient public keys, and exact lengths are visible in bytes; JVKW promises neither origin nor recipient anonymity. It is not KeyRef<T> and cannot load directly. Exactly SigningKey and X25519SecretKey are supported; no role retagging. All export/import calls require #(Secret). export_to_recipients<T: VaultKey>(reference:&KeyRef<T>,recipients:[X25519PublicKey]) -> WrappedVaultKey ? KeyWrapError. export_to_passphrase<T>(reference:&KeyRef<T>,passphrase:&Secret) -> WrappedVaultKey ? KeyWrapError. prepare_import_wrapped<T:VaultKey>(name:String,wrapped:WrappedVaultKey,unlock:KeyUnlock) -> WrappedImportPlan<T> ? KeyWrapError fully authenticates/type-checks and retains zeroized key material while snapshotting the destination revision; KeyUnlock is Recipient(&X25519SecretKey) or Passphrase(&Secret). authorize_wrapped_import<T>(plan:&WrappedImportPlan<T>,reason:String) -> VaultWrite<T> ? KeyWrapError previews destination/type/origin and binds the plan operation hash. commit_import_wrapped<T>(write:take VaultWrite<T>,plan:take WrappedImportPlan<T>) -> KeyRef<T> ? KeyWrapError rejects substitution/revision/expiry mismatch. External-format migration uses VAULT1's exact core.vault.expert.import_signing/import_x25519 calls under lexical #Unsafe; this ballot adds no raw JVKW decrypt or second vault importer.

Canonical JVKW/v1. Integers are unsigned little-endian; text is NFC UTF-8. Common fixed prefix: magic "JVKW"[4], version u8=1, mode u8 (1=Recipient,2=Passphrase), key_type u8 (1=Ed25519 signing,2=X25519 secret), flags u8=0, header_len u32, ciphertext_len u32. Variable common header: origin_repository_uuid[16], origin_name_len u16, origin_name bytes 1..128 under VAULT1 name law, origin_generation u64>=1, origin_opaque_id[16], origin_record_hash[32], created_unix_ms u64, export_id[16], payload_nonce[24]. header_len counts every variable-header byte after the fixed prefix and before ciphertext. ciphertext_len is exactly 64; ciphertext is encrypted payload[64], followed by tag[16]. Total canonical size is fixed prefix 16 + header_len + 80 and capped at 8,192 bytes. Exact consumption required; unknown version/mode/type/flag, non-NFC/name violation, overflow, wrong count/length/order, reserved byte, or trailing byte rejects before secret work.

Payload is key_bytes[32] || public_key[32]. For SigningKey, public_key is strict canonical Ed25519 VerifyKey; for X25519SecretKey it is the exact derived X25519 public key. Import recomputes and constant-time compares the public key and validates the key type before vault mutation. Payload AEAD is XChaCha20-Poly1305 under backup_key[32] and payload_nonce, with AAD ASCII "JVKW1 payload" || the complete fixed and variable header. The tag is separate from ciphertext_len. Header, origin binding, mode parameters, recipients, and type are therefore authenticated.

Recipient mode header suffix. recipient_count u16 1..16, ephemeral_public[32], hkdf_salt[16], then recipient_count stanzas sorted lexicographically by recipient_public and unique. Stanza is recipient_public[32] || wrapped_backup_key[48]. Writer draws independent ephemeral X25519 secret, hkdf_salt, payload_nonce, backup_key, export_id from RNG1. For each recipient: shared=X25519(ephemeral_secret,recipient_public), reject all-zero; KEK=HKDF-SHA256(shared,salt, ASCII "JVKW1 recipient key" || export_id || ephemeral_public || recipient_public), 32 bytes; nonce=first24(HKDF-SHA256(shared,salt, ASCII "JVKW1 recipient nonce" || export_id || ephemeral_public || recipient_public)); wrapped_backup_key=XChaCha20-Poly1305(backup_key) with AAD ASCII "JVKW1 recipient aad" || common header through payload_nonce || recipient_count || ephemeral_public || salt || recipient_public. No recipient match performs one bounded dummy X25519/HKDF/AEAD path and returns OpenFailed.

Passphrase mode header suffix. argon_salt[16], memory_kib u32=65536, iterations u32=3, lanes u8=1, reserved[3]=0. Passphrase is exact Secret bytes, 16..1,048,576 bytes; no normalization, trimming, encoding conversion, environment input, default, hint, or stored verifier. backup_key=Argon2id v19(passphrase,argon_salt,m=65536,t=3,p=1,out=32) through PWHASH1's blocking-pool admission, cancellation, memory cap, and zeroization law. Writer draws independent salt, payload_nonce, export_id. Wrong passphrase and tamper both return OpenFailed. Passphrase length outside bounds is WeakPassphrase before KDF; Jet cannot measure entropy and never claims the length proves strength.

Parser/auth boundary. WrappedVaultKey.from_bytes performs only capped canonical framing and returns InvalidEncoding, UnsupportedVersion, UnsupportedMode, InvalidLength, or UnsupportedKeyType. It never authenticates. Once import begins secret work, wrong recipient/passphrase, all-zero peer, unwrap failure, payload/tag/header mutation that remains canonically framed, type/public mismatch, or key corruption collapse to one OpenFailed Display/JSON/audit category. No recipient index, match, Argon detail, parser offset after secret work, tag, salt, origin id, backend/OS/dependency prose, or partial key escapes. Operation-count tests cover no-match and wrong-passphrase classes; wall-clock equality is not claimed.

Export, import, and revocation truth. Export accepts Active or Retired references; a Revoked source returns Vault(Revoked). It loads the exact immutable KeyRef, never current(name), and binds every origin field. Export does not rotate, retire, or change current. The wrapped bytes are an independent bearer backup: later source retirement/revocation/deletion cannot recall or invalidate copies. Audit states this before export. Import requires a fresh one-use VaultWrite and never writes before full authentication/type/public validation. A destination repository cannot learn a later revocation made only in the source repository; bearer-copy audit states this. Cross-repository or different-name import creates the destination name's next generation with new opaque id and Imported provenance while preserving immutable origin metadata. It never recreates the origin KeyRef. In the same repository, if the exact origin reference still exists Active/Retired and key/public hashes match, import returns ok(existing_reference), records an idempotent AlreadyPresent audit outcome, and performs no mutation; if it is Revoked, import returns Vault(Revoked) and does not reactivate it. An operator wanting the same bytes after revocation must use explicit #Unsafe raw import to a different name; it creates a new id/generation and audit records reintroduction. No safe import downgrades current or overwrites a generation.

Errors and cancellation. The final KeyWrapError/VaultError closure below is exhaustive and controls earlier shorthand. Cancellation remains task control: export returns no bytes; prepared import before commit zeroizes retained material and mutates nothing; after vault install it follows VAULT1's committed-result/durability law. No error has automatic retry or raw backend text.

Zeroization and platform. Raw key, backup key, passphrase-derived key, ephemeral secret, shared secrets, KEKs, nonces, payload plaintext, caller-owned imported buffers, and bridge scratch are non-elidably zeroized after last use; WrappedVaultKey ciphertext and public header are not secret types. Recipient-only parse/crypto can run on any target supported by compatible API/RNG/dependency law, but vault export/import additionally follows VAULT1: Linux glibc x86_64/aarch64, macOS x86_64/arm64, Windows MSVC x86_64/arm64. WASI/browser/mobile/musl/freestanding/comptime/pure/interpreter return UnsupportedProvider through VaultError before key work. AOT/native JIT share one implementation.

Migration and acceptance. No byte sequence from JETW, JETV, JETC, age, PEM, raw 32-byte keys, or historical vault strings is guessed as JVKW. from_bytes requires magic/version. Expert migration explicitly parses the source format under #Unsafe, then exports a fresh JVKW. V1 writer/read fixtures are permanent until a future ballot defines a new version and migration window. Golden vectors pin every byte for both modes, both key types, 1/16 recipients, exact caps and empty/hostile fields. Tests cover KDF/AEAD/HKDF/X25519/Ed25519 vectors, origin/type/generation mutation, wrong unlock, no-match dummy work, source revoke after export, same-repo idempotent-success/Revoked, cross-repo new identity, raw reimport truth, RNG/resource/cancellation, zeroization, backend suppression, AOT/JIT, supported clean hosts, and release artifact scans.

Beginner pass: choose recovery recipients, export one opaque value, import with the matching identity. Expert pass: exact bytes, KDF costs, recipient visibility, origin binding, revocation limits, admission, audit and migration are explicit. Hybrid pass: recipient and passphrase modes share one grammar, payload, AEAD, error collapse, vault mutation and audit path; neither creates a second key type or raw safe escape.

Prepared import integration closure. The only import flow is prepare_import_wrapped<T:VaultKey>(name:String,wrapped:WrappedVaultKey,unlock:KeyUnlock) -> WrappedImportPlan<T> ? KeyWrapError; authorize_wrapped_import<T:VaultKey>(plan:&WrappedImportPlan<T>,reason:String) -> VaultWrite<T> ? KeyWrapError; commit_import_wrapped<T:VaultKey>(write:take VaultWrite<T>,plan:take WrappedImportPlan<T>) -> KeyRef<T> ? KeyWrapError. Preparation authenticates JVKW, recomputes type/public key, retains zeroized key bytes, copies origin fields into the destination plan, and snapshots destination plaintext hash/revision/provider binding. Authorization binds that exact plan hash; commit cannot substitute unlock, wrapped bytes, name, type, origin, or destination. No one-step import_wrapped alias exists.

KeyWrapError and VaultError boundary. KeyWrapError is exactly InvalidEncoding, UnsupportedVersion, UnsupportedMode, UnsupportedKeyType, InvalidLength, WeakPassphrase, OpenFailed, EntropyUnavailable, ResourceUnavailable, Vault(VaultError), and Internal {incident_id}. Direct Revoked, AlreadyPresent, AuthorityDenied, and Conflict variants do not exist. Every VaultError is nested one-for-one without text loss or flattening: InvalidName, NotFound, WrongType, Revoked, Locked, AuthorityDenied, Conflict, UnsupportedProvider, InvalidEncoding, DurabilityUnknown, Crypto(CryptoError), Io {operation,redacted_path}, and Internal {incident_id}. Source revoked and same-repository revoked-origin import therefore return Vault(Revoked); idempotent same-origin import returns ok(existing KeyRef). Destination authority/revision/durability/I/O failures remain their Vault(...) value.

Wrapped-byte/authentication failures never become Vault errors. Passing .Passphrase to mode Recipient or .Recipient to mode Passphrase, wrong recipient identity/passphrase, no stanza match, all-zero peer, unwrap/tag failure, authenticated origin/type/public mismatch, or framed tamper returns the identical direct OpenFailed before any vault plan/mutation. Unknown numeric mode in bytes remains parser-level UnsupportedMode. RNG/KDF failures before vault work are direct EntropyUnavailable/ResourceUnavailable; impossible wrapper invariant is direct Internal. If vault mutation begins only after successful authentication, its later errors use Vault(...). This ordering prevents wrong-unlock oracles while preserving actionable destination lifecycle errors.
decisions.story: Mina keeps release-signing and backup-decryption keys in the repository vault. She must place an offline recovery copy in a second location, restore it on a fresh authorized host, and prove which original key version it came from. A compromised source key is later revoked; the old backup cannot be magically recalled, and importing it must never silently revive the revoked reference.

options.name: Recipient and passphrase recovery
options.detail: Recommended. Ship both exact JVKW/v1 modes above. Recipient mode gives unattended/team recovery without a memorized secret; passphrase mode gives an offline human fallback with fixed Argon2id cost. Both use one payload, origin binding, parser, AEAD, errors and import path.
options.code:
wrapped :: vault.export_to_recipients(&release_ref, [offline.public_key()])?
paper :: vault.export_to_passphrase(&release_ref, &recovery_phrase)?

plan :: vault.prepare_import_wrapped<crypto.SigningKey>(
    "release-restored", wrapped, .Recipient(&offline)
)?
write :: vault.authorize_wrapped_import(&plan, reason: "disaster recovery")?
restored :: vault.commit_import_wrapped(take(write), take(plan))?

options.name: Recipient recovery only
options.detail: Use the exact recipient-mode JVKW/v1 grammar, origin binding, lifecycle, errors, zeroization and import law above; mode 2 is unsupported and no Argon2/passphrase dependency enters this decision. Recovery requires at least one X25519 identity, but automation and team/offline copies avoid password-guessing risk.
options.code:
wrapped :: vault.export_to_recipients(&backup_ref, [ops.public_key(), offline.public_key()])?
// Passphrase request:
Error: this wrapped-key mode is not supported
Fix: choose one or more X25519 recovery recipients

options.name: Passphrase recovery only
options.detail: Use the exact passphrase-mode JVKW/v1 grammar, origin binding, lifecycle, errors, zeroization and import law above; mode 1 is unsupported and no recipient stanza is emitted. One human-held Secret is enough to recover anywhere VAULT1 runs, but every copied blob becomes an offline guessing target and unattended rotation needs an external secret source.
options.code:
wrapped :: vault.export_to_passphrase(&release_ref, &recovery_phrase)?
plan :: vault.prepare_import_wrapped<crypto.SigningKey>(
    "release-restored", wrapped, .Passphrase(&recovery_phrase)
)?
write :: vault.authorize_wrapped_import(&plan, reason: "offline recovery")?
restored :: vault.commit_import_wrapped(take(write), take(plan))?

comparisons.note: age uses X25519 recipient stanzas and a random file key. JVKW recipient mode adopts that recovery shape but pins Jet key type, origin version, caps and vault import semantics.

Encrypted PKCS #8 wraps private-key bytes under password-based encryption but does not know Jet vault generations or revocation. JVKW passphrase mode adds exact origin/type binding and one fixed safe profile.
KMS imported key material keeps external origin and cannot make prior copies disappear after disable/delete. JVKW records the same honest bearer-copy and reimport boundary locally.

decisions.title: Typed crypto errors and misuse diagnostics
decisions.gist: Choose how recoverable cryptographic failures remain typed values and when compile-known misuse becomes E2702 without creating authentication or backend oracles.
decisions.story: Mina opens an encrypted tenant record. A wrong key must look exactly like changed AAD or a corrupt tag, while an unavailable entropy provider and a saturated password-hash worker pool need distinct recovery. During review, her teammate also writes a literal 12-byte nonce for XChaCha in an expert interop call; the compiler can name that mistake before it runs without pretending it can diagnose attacker-controlled ciphertext statically.
decisions.detail:
Inherited gates and current draft status. D-CRYPTO-SUITE1=A and D-PWHASH1=A are live ratified law. D-CRYPTO-API1, D-CRYPTO-ENVELOPE2, D-PWHASH-POLICY1, D-CRYPTO-VAULT1, D-CRYPTO-KEYWRAP1, D-CRYPTO-RNG1, and D-DEP-CRYPTO-SUITE2 are compatibility-required companion decisions proposed in this batch; each grants nothing until independently ratified. API1 owns CryptoError and value JETV/JETW parse/auth boundaries. ENVELOPE2 owns FileCryptoError and file-only JETC behavior. VAULT1 owns VaultError and persistent storage, including internal store atomic backup/recovery only. KEYWRAP1 owns KeyWrapError and portable vault-key export/import. This ballot only selects diagnostic projection; it adds no dependency, algorithm, syntax, envelope field, password cost, runtime JSON schema, or command surface.

Option A closed CryptoError. `CryptoError` is a public closed runtime enum with exactly: `InvalidLength { operation, parameter, expected, actual }`; `InvalidEncoding { operation, value_kind }`; `UnsupportedVersion { operation, version }`; `UnsupportedAlgorithm { operation, algorithm }`; `OpenFailed`; `NonContributoryKey`; `OutputLength { operation, minimum, maximum, actual }`; `PasswordPolicy { reason }`; `EntropyUnavailable`; `ResourceUnavailable { resource }`; and `Internal { incident_id }`. Fields contain only public operation/bounds/version/policy identifiers. No variant contains secret/key/password/plaintext/ciphertext/tag/salt/hash/PHC bytes, parser offset, recipient index/id, OS status/path/handle, dependency type/error, generated-Rust text, or backend prose. Cancellation remains D-TASKRUNTIME1 control flow and is not CryptoError; task cancellation unwinds after zeroization/owned cleanup. Allocation failure before a recoverable reservation is ResourceUnavailable; memory-safety invariant failure is Internal.

Error assignment. Constructor/import length mismatch -> InvalidLength. Canonical public-key/signature/value-envelope framing and PasswordHash PHC shape, whitespace, decimal syntax, base64 syntax/canonicality, or decoded-length failure -> InvalidEncoding. Unknown public value-envelope or PHC version -> UnsupportedVersion; unknown algorithm/PHC id, including argon2d/argon2i -> UnsupportedAlgorithm. HKDF or expert output outside exact bounds -> OutputLength. Direct X25519 agreement that completes with an all-zero result -> NonContributoryKey. Entropy provider unavailable -> EntropyUnavailable, laundering every RandomError.Unavailable; negative/too-large direct random.bytes remains RNG1-owned RandomError. Password Secret above 1,048,576 bytes, or syntactically canonical PHC numeric m/t/p/product/input/text values outside PWHASH hard policy -> PasswordPolicy before admission. Argon2 admission, unsupported platform, or allocation resource failure -> ResourceUnavailable. Audited backend invariant failure -> Internal with a fresh non-secret incident id. password_verify completed mismatch is ok(false); resource/backend/cancellation never becomes false. No backend string is interpolated.

Companion and authentication projection. API1 `Sealed.from_bytes` and `WrappedKey.from_bytes` expose their public framing InvalidLength/InvalidEncoding/UnsupportedVersion/UnsupportedAlgorithm before secret work; after successful construction, value `open`/`unwrap` collapses wrong key/recipient/AAD, all-zero agreement, unwrap, tag, or authenticated tamper to CryptoError.OpenFailed. ENVELOPE2 `file_open` uses FileCryptoError exactly: OpenFailed, SealFailed(CryptoError), SourceIo, DestinationExists, DestinationIo; structurally framed or authenticated file-open failure after source I/O begins collapses to FileCryptoError.OpenFailed. VAULT1 VaultError stays exactly InvalidName, NotFound, WrongType, Revoked, Locked, AuthorityDenied, Conflict, UnsupportedProvider, InvalidEncoding, DurabilityUnknown, Crypto(CryptoError), Io {operation,redacted_path}, Internal {incident_id}. KEYWRAP1 KeyWrapError stays exactly InvalidEncoding, UnsupportedVersion, UnsupportedMode, UnsupportedKeyType, InvalidLength, WeakPassphrase, OpenFailed, EntropyUnavailable, ResourceUnavailable, Vault(VaultError), Internal {incident_id}; wrapped authentication failures are direct OpenFailed and vault failures remain nested. These enums are companion values, never aliases or flattened CryptoError variants. Every projection preserves the owning draft's oracle collapse and redaction.

Stable Display/recovery. InvalidLength: `<operation>: <parameter> must be <expected>; got <actual>` / fix the public input length. InvalidEncoding: `<operation>: <value_kind> is not canonical` / parse or import the documented canonical form. UnsupportedVersion/Algorithm: `<operation>: version/algorithm <n> is not supported` / migrate with the named expert tool or supported writer. OpenFailed: `encrypted data could not be opened` / check the key and expected context, then obtain an intact supported envelope; never say which failed. NonContributoryKey: `X25519 peer key does not contribute to a shared secret` / reject the peer key and obtain a new authenticated public key. OutputLength: `<operation>: output length must be <min>..<max>; got <actual>` / choose a bound value. PasswordPolicy: `password hash is outside Jet's accepted policy` / migrate or regenerate after successful verification. EntropyUnavailable: `the operating system could not provide cryptographic randomness` / retry as a new deliberate operation or use a supported host; never substitute bytes. ResourceUnavailable: `<resource> is unavailable for this cryptographic operation` / retry later or adjust the separately ratified process-start budget. Internal: `Jet could not preserve a cryptographic invariant; incident <id>` / stop using the result, restart, and report the id with redacted audit. Secret-bearing values have no Display/Debug, so formatting an error cannot transitively reveal them.

E2702 reachability and precedence. First resolve syntax/effects/types. Expert call outside lexical #Unsafe emits E0510 only. Ordinary nominal-role or generic-bound incompatibility emits the ordinary type diagnostic only. E2702 is considered only after those checks pass, sema resolves a compiler-known `core.crypto`/`core.crypto.expert` callee, and a type or compile-time literal proves crypto misuse at the offending argument/call. Covered facts are only: literal/fixed key/public/signature/nonce length contradicts the selected expert algorithm; literal HKDF output outside 0..8160; literal Argon2 m/t/p/salt/output outside PWHASH hard caps; raw nonce/algorithm argument offered to a safe envelope call; or deterministic/test entropy seam reachable from a release build. `reject_all_zero:false` is not an E2702 case: inside valid #Unsafe it is an allowed expert choice, outside it E0510 wins. Dynamic bytes, attacker input, authentication mismatch, resource/backend/entropy failure, unsupported envelope bytes, password mismatch, and generic key-role mismatch never produce E2702. Dead code remains checked; generics diagnose at definition only when constraints prove a covered fact, otherwise at specialized call site with both spans.

E2702 exact diagnostic. Terminal UTF-8/NO_COLOR frame is `Error [E2702]: crypto API misuse
 --> <file>:<line>:<column>
 ...source span...
 Why: <operation> would use <public fact>, which violates <named requirement>
 Fix: <one exact safe replacement or required bound>
`; no algorithm/backend text beyond the public selected operation. Example Why `XChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce has 12 bytes; this operation requires exactly 24`; Fix `pass a 24-byte nonce, or use core.crypto.seal so Jet generates it`. Literal key length Fix names exact length; safe raw-nonce Fix removes the argument; deterministic seam Fix uses core.random only for non-crypto tests or expert fixed-vector input under #Unsafe. Each reason is a closed enum in compiler data, not formatted free text.

Machine/tool boundary. Compiler-owned E2702 JSON is exactly one `jet.diagnostic/v1` object: `{code:"E2702",class:"user",severity:"error",phase:"sema",what:"crypto API misuse",why,fix,reason,operation,expected?,actual?,primarySpan,relatedSpans:[]}`; field order/schema, workspace-relative paths, spans and redaction are pinned. LSP projects the same compiler diagnostic. DAP has no crypto ErrorResponse mapping. Runtime CryptoError/FileCryptoError/VaultError/KeyWrapError JSON rows are explicitly blocked until a general runtime-diagnostic owner ratifies their schema. First-party `jet crypto`, file, vault, key-wrap, import, rehash, and audit commands are explicitly blocked until their owning ballots plus DIAG1 ratify exact terminal/JSON rows, exits, cleanup and no-artifact law. No draft may claim JSON single-object behavior or CLI availability early.

Handled, unhandled, first-party, and compiler exits. Any handled CryptoError, including Internal, is ordinary program data: no diagnostic and no forced exit. Under A/C, an unhandled non-Internal CryptoError at `fn run` uses existing E3001 class user/tool as owned by runtime and exits 70 after cleanup; unhandled CryptoError.Internal uses E3001 class internal and exits 101 after fail-closed cleanup. A first-party command remains unavailable until it owns a row; once owned, it catches the typed value, emits that command's exact four-line frame, exits 1 for non-Internal operation failure and 101 for Internal, and publishes no artifact on failure. Compiler E2702 is class user, exits 1, and emits no program/artifact. A compiler/rustc/generated-code invariant failure is not CryptoError.Internal: existing compiler-internal ownership emits its compiler diagnostic and exits 101. Cancellation remains task control and follows only the owning runtime/command lifecycle.

Audit/backend suppression. Redacted audit may record operation, public algorithm/version, public sizes/bounds, target/provider identity, wait/duration, result category, cleanup/publication outcome, and incident id. It never records secrets, keys, nonce values, password/PHC/salt/hash, plaintext/ciphertext/tag, recipient identity for failed open, raw OS code, dependency error, parser offset after secret work, or generated source. Backend/dependency errors map through a closed internal table to EntropyUnavailable, ResourceUnavailable, OpenFailed, InvalidEncoding, or Internal; unknown backend errors become Internal. rustc/dependency prose is never shown.

Recovery and cleanup. Invalid input errors have no effect and caller may correct then issue a new operation. OpenFailed returns no partial plaintext and owned temps are removed. EntropyUnavailable exposes no key/nonce/salt/envelope and retry is a new operation. ResourceUnavailable reserves nothing or releases/zeroizes its reservation before return. Internal publishes nothing, performs fail-closed owned cleanup, and forbids reusing ambiguous crypto state. No CryptoError has `retryable`; recovery text distinguishes a new deliberate request from automatic replay.

I4 acceptance. diagnostics.md replaces E2702's reserved text with every covered reason/Why/Fix; `jet explain E2702` matches. UI snapshots cover every E2702 reason in TTY/plain/NO_COLOR/FORCE_COLOR plus Unicode/path spans, generics, dead code, and precedence proving E0510/type diagnostics suppress duplicate E2702. Compiler JSON schema/goldens, LSP severity/code/actions, exit 1/no artifact, and secret-redaction fixtures are pinned. Runtime value tests cover every CryptoError and companion projection, public framing versus authentication collapse, exact PWHASH parse/policy mapping, password mismatch versus operational failure, cleanup and backend suppression. A/C test E3001 exit70 for unhandled non-Internal and exit101 for unhandled Internal. B snapshots all eleven E2720..E2730 mappings, exact four-line frames/classes, fn-run exits 70/101, and future command exits 1/101, but cannot mark runtime JSON or command rows complete before their owners ratify. Tests assert all affected commands remain blocked and emit no ad-hoc Display/JSON. AOT/JIT parity and bounded operation-class tests apply; timing never claims wall-clock equality proves constant time. Beginner pass: one useful message and safe next action; wrong-key/tamper remains indistinguishable. Expert pass: typed category, public bounds, operation, audit, spans, target/provider, cleanup and incident id remain inspectable at ratified boundaries. Hybrid pass: libraries handle owning enums directly; projections never create a parallel exception taxonomy.

options.name: Typed runtime values plus focused E2702
options.detail: Recommended. Use current API1 CryptoError plus companion FileCryptoError/VaultError/KeyWrapError projections and focused E2702 with explicit precedence. Handled values remain program data; unhandled runtime and future first-party/compiler exits follow the exact boundary law above. Runtime JSON and command rows remain blocked until owned.

options.name: Typed values plus one E-code per runtime category
options.detail: Keep A's typed values and E2702, but allocate exactly eleven runtime projection codes: E2720 InvalidLength, E2721 InvalidEncoding, E2722 UnsupportedVersion, E2723 UnsupportedAlgorithm, E2724 OpenFailed, E2725 NonContributoryKey, E2726 OutputLength, E2727 PasswordPolicy, E2728 EntropyUnavailable, E2729 ResourceUnavailable, E2730 Internal. Terminal frames are exactly `Error [code] [class]`, then one-space-prefixed What/Why/Fix lines from A's pinned Display/recovery text. E2720..27 are class user; E2728..29 class tool; E2730 class internal. Handled values emit nothing. At fn run E2720..29 exit 70 and E2730 exits 101; in an independently ratified first-party command E2720..29 exit 1 and E2730 exits 101. Compiler E2702 remains exit 1. Runtime JSON/CLI emission remains blocked until its owner ratifies exact rows.
options.code:
E2720 InvalidLength       [user]
E2721 InvalidEncoding     [user]
E2722 UnsupportedVersion  [user]
E2723 UnsupportedAlgorithm [user]
E2724 OpenFailed          [user]
E2725 NonContributoryKey  [user]
E2726 OutputLength        [user]
E2727 PasswordPolicy      [user]
E2728 EntropyUnavailable  [tool]
E2729 ResourceUnavailable [tool]
E2730 Internal            [internal]
# fn run: 70 except Internal=101; owned command: 1 except Internal=101

options.name: Typed values with no crypto-specific sema diagnostic
options.detail: Keep A's exact CryptoError/runtime behavior but retire E2702. Literal wrong lengths and raw safe-API arguments receive ordinary type/argument diagnostics or runtime CryptoError; E0510 still gates expert calls. This minimizes diagnostic vocabulary, but a compile-known 12-byte XChaCha nonce gets a generic mismatch instead of the security-specific Why/Fix already reserved for core.crypto.

comparisons.note: Rust libraries return typed errors, while compiler type errors catch role mismatches. Jet adds a narrow security-specific sema diagnostic only where the compiler knows the cryptographic requirement.
Sodium deliberately collapses authentication failure. Jet preserves that collapse in typed values, CLI output, JSON, audit, and debugger projection rather than leaking backend causes.
Tink's safe templates prevent many misuses before execution. Jet makes the remaining compile-known boundary mistakes source-spanned E2702 diagnostics.

decisions.title: Exact shared core.http values, bodies, and errors
decisions.gist: Choose the one typed HTTP model shared by clients, servers, routers, and middleware.
decisions.explainer: Recommendation A gives beginners named text/json helpers while experts retain one byte-stream, ordered-header, typed-error model. It replaces current client/server wrapper duplication; it does not alter D-HTTPDEPTH1=A or D-WS1=B.
decisions.story: Mara writes an auth middleware once, tests it without a socket, then uses it around both an outbound API client and an inbound service. Today Jet has separate string-backed client/server values, eager text bodies, lossy header maps, and String errors, so streaming, repeated headers, binary data, cancellation, and safe limits cannot compose.
decisions.detail:
Option A exact law. `core.http` owns nominal `Method`, `Status`, `Version`, `HeaderName`, `HeaderValue`, `Headers`, `Request`, `Response`, `Body`, `Handler`, and closed `HttpError`. Client and server submodules re-export these exact values; no parallel HttpClientReq/HttpSrvReq model remains. Method accepts registered tokens plus `Method.custom(token)?`; Status validates 100..599. Headers preserve insertion order and repeated fields, compare names ASCII-case-insensitively, reject control/whitespace-invalid names and CR/LF/NUL values, and expose first/all/append/set/remove. Request contains method, typed Url, version, headers, Body, peer/local metadata and route params when present. Response contains status, version, headers, Body and trailers. `Handler.handle(take Request) -> Response ? HttpError` is the sole composition unit for client transport, router, middleware, and test doubles.

Body is move-only and byte-native. Constructors: empty(), bytes(take [U8]), text(take String, content_type: Mime = text/plain; charset=utf-8), json<T: Encode>(take T), form(...), multipart(...), reader(take Reader, length: Int?=none). Readers: bytes(limit: Int), text(limit: Int), json<T: Decode>(limit: Int), chunks(max_chunk: Int=65536), copy_to(&Writer, limit:Int). A body may be consumed once; second consumption is BodyConsumed. Unknown-length bodies stream with HTTP framing and never buffer implicitly. Default convenience decode limit is 8 MiB client and 1 MiB server; explicit limits are 0..1 GiB. Dropping/cancelling closes source and returns pooled connections only when framing was fully drained. Secret-bearing Authorization/Cookie/Set-Cookie values redact in Debug, diagnostics, audit, and logs.

HttpError is exactly InvalidMethod, InvalidUrl, InvalidHeader, InvalidStatus, BodyConsumed, BodyTooLarge{limit}, InvalidFraming, UnsupportedEncoding, Resolve{host}, Connect{address}, Tls{stage}, Timeout{phase}, Proxy{stage}, Redirect{reason}, Protocol{version}, Io{operation}, Cancelled, ResourceUnavailable{resource}, and Internal{incident_id}. No OS/backend prose, body bytes, credentials, cookies, URL userinfo/query, certificate private material, or generated Rust appears. HTTP non-2xx is a successful Response, never HttpError. Cancellation is task control where available and projects to Cancelled only at an API boundary that returns HttpError. Public parse failures can identify malformed public fields; authentication/TLS internals remain collapsed. Every variant has stable Display, recovery, diagnostic projection, and tests. Binary bodies never pass through UTF-8 lossiness.

Compatibility: current string helpers become source-migration diagnostics at the next allowed core API break, not permanent aliases. Existing `Client.get/post`, `Server.response/sse/static_file`, and request accessors lower to these same values where signatures remain compatible. Beginner pass: `.text()`, `.json()`, and ordinary handlers need no stream knowledge. Expert pass: repeated headers, trailers, exact limits, readers/writers, cancellation, audit, and connection reuse are explicit. Hybrid pass: helpers construct/consume the same Body and Handler; no framework-only second model.

options.name: Unified typed messages, streaming Body, and Handler
options.detail: One byte-native Request/Response/Body/Handler model serves every HTTP role; ergonomic codecs are checked helpers over it.

options.name: Separate ergonomic client and server values
options.detail: Keep distinct client/server request and response types, adding conversion calls at middleware and test boundaries. Role discovery is explicit, but shared policy can drift and conversion can buffer bodies.
options.code:
srv_req :: http.server.Request
common :: http.Message.from_server(take(srv_req))?
client_req :: common.into_client()?

options.name: Buffered text-first compatibility model
options.detail: Retain current String bodies/maps and add optional stream helpers beside them. Simple calls stay familiar, but binary payloads, repeated headers, bounded memory, pooling, and cancellation have two competing paths.
options.code:
resp.body()       // String
resp.body_stream() // separate semantics

comparisons.note: Request, Response, Header, Body, Handler compose across client/server; Body is streaming and must be closed.
Shared typed parts and handler pipelines preserve streaming/backpressure across roles.

decisions.title: Exact core.http client transport policy
decisions.gist: Choose client pooling, redirects, cookies, proxies, compression, timeouts, and protocol behavior.
decisions.explainer: Recommendation A keeps `http.get` ceremony-free but makes one immutable Client policy object the explicit expert path. Defaults are safe, bounded, HTTPS-first, environment-aware, and observable.
decisions.story: Inez calls hundreds of tenant APIs through corporate proxies. She needs safe HTTPS defaults, pooled connections, bounded streaming downloads, controlled redirects, cookies, gzip, per-phase deadlines, HTTP/2, and an audit trail without retrying unsafe writes or leaking credentials across origins.
decisions.inWild:
client :: http.Client.new()
  .timeout(total: 30s, connect: 5s, read_idle: 10s)
  .redirects(.Follow(max: 5, same_origin_credentials: false))
res :: client.send(http.Request.get(url).header("accept", "application/json"))?
decisions.detail:
Requires D-HTTP-CORE2=A. Option A exact law. `Client.new()` owns a Send+Sync pool keyed by scheme, host, port, proxy, TLS identity/policy and protocol; default per-origin idle=8, global idle=64, idle timeout=90s, max concurrent per origin=64, DNS cache positive=60s/negative=5s. `http.get/post` use one process-default Client with identical policy. Keep-alive is default; unread bodies make that connection non-reusable unless explicitly drained within limit. HTTP/2 negotiates ALPN for HTTPS and reuses multiplexed sessions; HTTP/1.1 remains supported; cleartext h2c requires explicit expert policy. No HTTP/3.

Redirect default Follow(max:10): only 301/302/303 rewrite POST to GET; 307/308 preserve method/body only when replayable; cycles and max return Redirect. Cross-origin redirects strip Authorization, Proxy-Authorization and Cookie; downgrade HTTPS->HTTP is denied unless explicit policy. CookieJar is opt-in on custom Client, RFC6265bis domain/path/secure/samesite/expiry bounded to 4096 cookies and 180/domain; shortcut helpers are stateless. Redirect history is inspectable. Automatic retries default only for stale pooled connection before request bytes and idempotent methods with replayable bodies, max one; no status retry.

Timeout has dns, connect, tls, write_idle, first_byte, read_idle, and total phases; defaults total=30s, connect/tls=10s, idle=30s. Zero means immediate, none disables only when explicitly supplied. Task deadline is the upper bound. Proxy policy defaults `FromEnvironment`: HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY/ALL_PROXY and NO_PROXY parsed once per request with lowercase precedence rules documented; credentials redact. Explicit None disables env. CONNECT tunnels HTTPS. SOCKS requires separately ratified support and is absent.

Request bodies support bytes/text/json/form plus streaming reader and multipart parts with known/unknown length. Response decompression advertises gzip and transparently decodes gzip by default, removes Content-Encoding/Length from decoded view while raw metadata remains inspectable; unsupported encoding errors, no silent bytes. `.raw_encoding()` opts out. Upload/download backpressure uses 64KiB chunks and configured caps. TLS inherits D-TLS1 system roots/SNI/hostname validation; custom roots, client identity, pins, minimum TLS and danger overrides use `core.tls` typed policy, never booleans; danger requires #Unsafe. Each response exposes protocol, remote address, redirect history, timings, reused_connection.

No ambient cache. Client clones share pool/jar; policy builders return a new client namespace. Beginner pass: `http.get(url)?.text()` works safely. Expert pass: every pool/proxy/TLS/deadline/redirect/compression/replay/audit fact is controllable. Hybrid: shortcuts send through the same Client implementation.

options.name: Safe pooled Client with explicit policy builders
options.detail: Requests-style shortcuts and one reusable policy-rich Client share transport semantics.
options.code:
res :: http.get(url)?
api :: http.Client.new().proxy(.None).cookies(.Memory).protocols([.Http2,.Http11])
res2 :: api.send(take(req))?

options.name: Global transport policy
options.detail: Pooling and environment policy live in process-global setters. Short calls are compact, but tests/tenants can interfere and authority is hidden.
options.code:
http.configure(proxy: env, redirects: 5)
http.get(url)?

options.name: One connection per request
options.detail: Every request dials independently; streaming exists but pooling, cookie state, multiplexing and shared policy are caller-owned.
options.code:
req :: http.Request.get(url)
http.send_once(take(req))?

comparisons.note: Client scopes pooling, cookies, redirects, proxies and timeouts while top-level helpers stay simple.
Client wraps a reusable Transport with redirect policy and streaming response bodies.

decisions.title: Exact core.http server, router, middleware, and lifecycle
decisions.gist: Choose safe server defaults, route law, middleware composition, streaming, shutdown, files, and logging.
decisions.explainer: Recommendation A makes the safe production path the default while retaining exact expert policy on one Server/Router/Handler mechanism. It replaces the current unbounded read-to-String and thread-per-connection behavior.
decisions.story: Omar runs a public REST and SSE service. A slow client must not exhaust memory or threads; route conflicts must fail before listening; middleware must preserve typed errors; shutdown must drain healthy work, cancel stragglers, and publish no partial response; files need traversal-safe ranges and logs must redact secrets.
decisions.inWild:
router :: http.Router.new()
router.get("/users/{id}", show_user)
router.get("/assets/{*path}", http.static_files(root))
app :: http.middleware.recover(http.middleware.access_log(router))
server :: http.Server.bind("127.0.0.1:8080", app)?
server.serve(shutdown: ctx)?
decisions.detail:
Requires D-HTTP-CORE2=A. Option A exact law. Router patterns use literal segments, `{name}` one-segment params, and final `{*name}` catch-all only; percent-decode each segment once after splitting, reject invalid UTF-8/encoded slash ambiguity, dot traversal and duplicate names. Static beats param beats wildcard; then registration order. Duplicate method+equivalent pattern and ambiguous equal-specificity overlap fail at registration with RouteConflict. HEAD falls back to GET without body; OPTIONS auto-lists methods; 405 carries Allow; unknown is 404. Methods get/post/put/patch/delete/head/options plus on(Method,...). Params are immutable typed map. No regex route language.

Router implements Handler. `middleware(fn(next:Handler)->Handler)` wraps handlers; order is declaration order, outermost first request/last response. Built-ins: request_id, recover, timeout, body_limit, cors(explicit policy), compression, access_log(core.log), and static_files. Panic/internal failure closes/publishes nothing if headers unsent and maps to redacted 500+incident; after streaming begins it aborts connection. Middleware cannot read a body twice; buffering requires explicit bounded bytes(limit).

Server.bind(SocketAddr|String, Handler, options=Safe) -> Server ? HttpError; `.local_addr()`, `.serve(shutdown: Context=never)`, `.shutdown(grace:Duration=30s)`, `.serve_listener(take TcpListener,...)`. Defaults: header bytes 32KiB, header count 100, request-line 8KiB, body 1MiB unless route raises it, read-header 5s, read-idle 30s, write-idle 30s, keepalive idle 60s, max requests/connection 1000, global connections 10k with per-IP 256, handler concurrency bounded by task scheduler. Over-limit returns 400/408/413/431/503 as appropriate then closes when framing is unsafe. Parse incrementally; reject request smuggling: conflicting Content-Length, invalid/multiple transfer framing, obs-fold, whitespace-before-colon, CL+TE, invalid chunks. HTTP/1.1 keepalive/pipelining preserves response order; HTTP/2 streams share Handler with per-stream/connection flow control.

Response Body streams bytes/chunks/SSE with backpressure. SSE sets text/event-stream, no buffering, heartbeat optional, cancellation closes generator. Trailers require declaration before headers. Graceful shutdown stops accepts/GOAWAY, lets active requests finish until grace, cancels rest, drains no new keepalive work, returns report counts. TLS uses D-TLSSERVE1 typed material and core.tls policy; cert reload is atomic typed callback, old connections keep old config.

`static_files(root: Path, index=["index.html"], symlinks:.Deny)` canonicalizes beneath root, denies traversal/special files, infers core.mime, supports GET/HEAD, single byte range 206/416, If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since, ETag, zero-copy where safe; directory listing off. Access log is a core.log typed event containing request id, method, redacted path (query omitted by default), route template, status, bytes, duration, peer/protocol/TLS; never Authorization/Cookie/body. Beginner pass: bind router and serve. Expert pass: every parser/limit/scheduler/TLS/shutdown/file/log fact is typed and auditable. Hybrid: built-ins are ordinary Handler wrappers.

options.name: Bounded Handler server with deterministic Router
options.detail: Safe production limits, typed lifecycle, streaming/backpressure and middleware are default parts of one server model.
options.code:
router.get("/users/{id}", show)
server :: http.Server.bind("0.0.0.0:8080", http.middleware.access_log(router))?
server.serve(shutdown: app_context)?

options.name: Minimal listener plus optional framework layer
options.detail: Core serves handlers with basic parsing; routing, middleware, files, limits and shutdown policy live in another package. This splits D-HTTPDEPTH1's batteries-included path.
options.code: http.listen(addr, (conn) => framework.serve(conn, app))?

options.name: Callback server with global defaults
options.detail: Keep `serve(addr,mux)` and configure limits/logging/shutdown globally. Compact, but authority, tests and multiple-server policy become ambient.
options.code:
http.server_limits(body: 1*MiB)
Server.serve(addr, mux)?

comparisons.note: Handler/ServeMux, streaming bodies, Server timeouts and Shutdown form one production server substrate.
Router and middleware lower to one service abstraction with body backpressure.

decisions.title: Temporary production HTTP and compression dependency closure
decisions.gist: Whether generated Jet programs may use a locked audited Rust HTTP stack until native replacement closes in Epoch 3.
decisions.explainer: Recommendation B follows I6's Epoch-3 end state: build the production protocol stack natively now, retaining only already-ratified TLS bridges until their inherited deletion gates close. Option A is ballot-complete as a bridge policy, but grants no package because no exact graph is attached.
decisions.story: Priya ships the same Jet service on Linux, macOS, Windows and WASI. The compiler currently emits a hidden ureq/rustls bridge while the server is an unsafe-in-practice handwritten parser. She needs HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, TLS, pooling, gzip and multipart to use one reviewed dependency closure whose exact packages, features, licenses, advisories, targets and deletion gates are owner-approved before any network fetch.
decisions.inWild:
$ jet audit dependencies --package service
core.http bridge: D-DEP-HTTP2
operation slice: client-http2-gzip
lock/sbom/rustsec/targets: signed, exact match
network: unopened before verification
decisions.detail:
Companion to D-HTTP-CORE2/CLIENT2/SERVER2; each grants nothing until independently ratified. Current truth: client bridge names ureq and TLS bridges name rustls/system roots; server HTTP/1.1 is handwritten std-only, reads unbounded bytes into lossy String, uses thread-per-connection, and does not supply production HTTP/2/compression/parsing. Option A authorizes a generated-program-only bridge, never compiler/seam Cargo.toml deps (I6), containing a minimal maintained pure-Rust HTTP/1.1 parser/codec, HTTP/2 framing/HPACK, async-or-readiness transport compatible with core.tasks/core.net, gzip codec, MIME multipart support, rustls and platform roots. No OpenSSL/C, native assembly, Tokio-only parallel runtime, ambient DNS/RNG, or default features are implicitly approved.

This draft deliberately does not pretend an exact graph exists. Before queue-ready implementation authority, attach: exact direct crate names/versions/default-features/features; complete per-target Cargo.lock checksums; SPDX/license-file hashes; cargo-deny policy; fresh RustSec DB revision and zero-unapproved report; minimal operation slices (client h1, client h2, server h1, server h2, gzip, multipart, TLS client/server); build/process/symbol traces on Linux x86_64/aarch64, macOS x86_64/arm64, Windows MSVC x86_64/arm64, WASI where supported; MSRV/tool hashes; deterministic generator hash; signed DSSE bundle and offline verify-before-fetch. WASI unsupported server/listener operations must return typed UnsupportedTarget, not silently omit behavior. Any advisory/yank/license/feature/graph change requires owner amendment.

Release rejects unsigned, expired, rollback, mixed-lock, extra-feature, unused-direct-crate or network-before-proof state. Generated manifests select only the operation-minimal slice.
